A delivered peer item starts with its stable message id and sender name. A successful send is already durable even when its result says queued; do not resend it. Shared-task workflow is list, get, claim with the current revision, perform the work, then complete. Task readiness never starts an owner. Before wait_agent, use list_agents and make sure another required member is running or provisioning; use send_message first when the required member is inactive. wait_agent observes only changes after that call starts, never wakes a member, and returns noProgress immediately when no other member can produce a change. tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

<path>C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-our-free-model\index.js</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: /**
2:  * Our Free Model — plugin entry (Host half).
3:  *
4:  * Wiring: one adapter instance, two provider routes (usable now / region-limited
5:  * on this egress), a live-catalog + availability-probe loop behind them, the
6:  * browser-facing JSON API the settings page reads, and the OpenAI-compatible
7:  * forward listener.
8:  *
9:  * On top of the model lane the plugin owns a small distribution channel of its
10:  * own: a remote announcement feed the repository owner publishes by pushing a
11:  * JSON document, an in-app self-updater that verifies and installs new releases
12:  * from the same repository, and a self hot-reload that swaps the running plugin
13:  * for the code now on disk. All three report to the browser over one
14:  * Server-Sent-Events route, because the kernel has no notification service and
15:  * the settings page should not have to poll.
16:  *
17:  * Every harness facility is reached through `ctx`, and only the one the plugin
18:  * cannot exist without is declared in `inject`, so a composition that omits the
19:  * rest degrades a feature rather than failing the plugin: no web server means no
20:  * in-app dashboard, no attachments means image blocks fall back to the text
21:  * projection the runtime already performs. See `inject` below.
22:  *
23:  * @module index.js
24:  */
25: 
26: import path from 'node:path'
27: import fs from 'node:fs'
28: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
29: import { FreeModelAdapter, ROUTE_LABELS, ROUTE_MAIN, ROUTE_REGION } from './src/adapter.js'
30: import { JsonStore, SETTINGS_INITIAL, STATS_INITIAL, STATS_VERSION, DATA_DIR_NAME, MIN_DECODE_MS, decodeWindow, migrateStats, pruneDays, recordTurn, recordUsage, resolveDshHome } from './src/store.js'
31: import { buildCatalog, parseListing } from './src/catalog.js'
32: import { STATE, detectEgress, probeCatalog } from './src/probe.js'
33: import { generateKey, startForwardServer, toOpenAiUsage } from './src/forward.js'
34: import { CODE, UpstreamError, getJson } from './src/http.js'
35: import { mintRequestId, sessionForConversation } from './src/upstream.js'
36: import { DEFAULT_LEVEL, budgetLadder } from './src/effort.js'
37: import { windowTokens } from './src/stream.js'
38: import { AnnouncementFeed } from './src/feed.js'
39: import { PluginUpdater, restoreBackup } from './src/updater.js'
40: import { selfReload, watchPackage, isReloading } from './src/reload.js'
41: import { createPushHub } from './src/push.js'
42: import { rejectionFor, isLoopbackHost } from './src/trust.js'
43: import { resolveAttributionUserAgent } from './adapter/kernel.js'
44: 
45: export const name = 'our-free-model'
46: 
47: /** The installed package directory — the self-updater and hot reload operate here. */
48: const PKG_URL = new URL('./', import.meta.url)
49: const PKG_DIR = fileURLToPath(PKG_URL)
50: const ENTRY_URL = new URL('index.js', import.meta.url).href
51: 
52: /** Published version of the installed package, read once at load. */
53: function readPackageVersion() {
54:   try {
55:     return String(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(PKG_DIR, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).version ?? '')
56:   } catch {
57:     return ''
58:   }
59: }
60: 
61: /**
62:  * `llm` is what the plugin exists for, so it is the only hard requirement of the
63:  * plugin itself.
64:  *
65:  * Cordis withholds from a context any service its fiber does not name in
66:  * `inject`, and keeps that fiber PENDING while a named one is absent — which is
67:  * how v1.2.1 stayed permanently inactive on a composition with no HTTP server,
68:  * the surface issue #4 reported. So nothing else may be named here: a headless
69:  * composition would rather serve models without a settings page than serve
70:  * nothing.
71:  *
72:  * What that costs and what still works:
73:  * - `webServer` — the in-app dashboard and the SSE push channel. Reached through
74:  *   a nested `ctx.inject` fiber (see the browser-facing API section), which pends
75:  *   on its own and never blocks the lane above.
76:  * - `timer` (`ctx.interval`) — nothing. The background loops are plain unref'd
77:  *   timers (see `every`), because reading a mixin off an undeclared service
78:  *   throws rather than answering `undefined`.
79:  * - `connection`, `attachments` — one feature each: the fence falls back to its
80:  *   structural replica, image blocks to the text projection. Both are read with
81:  *   `ctx.get()`, which is the opportunistic lookup that answers `undefined`.
82:  */
83: export const inject = ['llm']
84: 
85: /** Static fallback catalog, so a cold start with no network still lists models. */
86: const FALLBACK_CATALOG = buildCatalog([
87:   'mimo-v2.6-flash-free', 'mimo-v2.5-free', 'ling-3.0-flash-fin-free',
88:   'nemotron-3-ultra-free', 'nemotron-3.5-lightning-free', 'space-bunny-free',
89:   'muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free', 'muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free',
90: ])
91: 
92: /** Where the plugin's own announcement copy lives; bump it to re-announce. */
93: export const ANNOUNCEMENT_VERSION = '2026-09-25.1'
94: 
95: /**
96:  * Who owns the plugin's bytes — the distribution mode:
97:  *
98:  * - `self` (default): the plugin updates itself from its repository, publishes
99:  *   its announcement feed, and hot-reloads, exactly as before.
100:  * - `managed`: the plugin arrived through a distribution pack (an EAC
101:  *   integration pack, a Mojobox install). The pack manager owns the bytes now,
102:  *   so the in-app updater, the announcement channel and the hot reload stand
103:  *   down — two writers to one installed directory is a corrupted install. The
104:  *   model lane is untouched; this is about who ships the code, not what it does.
105:  *
106:  * `config.distribution` (what a pack's bundle patch passes) outranks the
107:  * settings file, and the settings API never accepts the field back, so an
108:  * install that shipped managed stays managed.
109:  */
110: const MANAGED_MESSAGE = 'this installation is managed; updates are handled by the pack that installed it'
111: 
112: /** Effective distribution mode: config override first, then the settings file. */
113: function distributionOf(config, settings) {
114:   if (config?.distribution === 'managed' || settings.get().distribution === 'managed') return 'managed'
115:   return 'self'
116: }
117: 
118: export function apply(ctx, config) {
119:   const logger = ctx.logger ?? console
120:   const home = resolveDshHome()
121:   const dataDir = path.join(home, DATA_DIR_NAME)
122:   fs.mkdirSync(dataDir, { recursive: true })
123:   const packageVersion = readPackageVersion()
124: 
125:   // A hot reload re-enters apply with fresh stores; the generation counter lives
126:   // on globalThis so the new instance knows it replaced a predecessor, and does
127:   // the post-swap bookkeeping itself (the old closure must not touch stores
128:   // after its own dispose — that would race the new instance's writes).
129:   const generation = (globalThis[Symbol.for('our-free-model.generation')] ?? 0) + 1
130:   globalThis[Symbol.for('our-free-model.generation')] = generation

* on this egress), a live-catalog + availability-probe loop behind them, the
* browser-facing JSON API the settings page reads, and the OpenAI-compatible
* On top of the model lane the plugin owns a small distribution channel of its
* own: a remote announcement feed the repository owner publishes by pushing a
* JSON document, an in-app self-updater that verifies and installs new releases
* from the same repository, and a self hot-reload that swaps the running plugin

* the settings page should not have to poll.

* rest degrades a feature rather than failing the plugin: no web server means no
* in-app dashboard, no attachments means image blocks fall back to the text
* projection the runtime already performs. See `inject` below.

lines.text: * Contributes three things to the web shell:
*   1. a settings section (`settings.section` id `our-free-model`) holding the
*      model roster with live availability, the usage dashboard, the OpenAI
*      forward listener and the plugin's own switches;
*   2. a first-run announcement (`settings.onboarding`) that is versioned, so
*      bumping the copy re-announces once and never nags again;
*   3. nothing else — no shadowing of the stock model picker, whose grouping by
*      provider route is exactly the mechanism this plugin uses for its tag.
* Data is read over the plugin's own same-origin `/api/our-free-model/*` routes
* rather than a typed Remote binding, because those routes are served by the same
* host process on every kernel line this plugin targets.
* Hand-written ModuleLoader bundle: no build step, no dependency beyond the
* `react` the shell already provides. All colour comes from theme variables so
* the page survives a scheme switch.

if (result.state === 'ready') {

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

Wait — `subprocess.spawnTerminal` is the underlying primitive. And the **bash terminal backend** (`dsh-terminal-bash`) registers with `ctx.terminals` using `shellPath`/`shellArgs` **config**. That's the `terminal_open` tool path (used by the agent's `terminal_open` tool). The `terminals` service spawn request is `{type, name?, cwd?}` — the backend owns argv from its config.

content.text:
Now I have the complete picture of the client side. Critical discoveries:

1. The sidebar terminal plugin uses client services: `sidebarRight`, `sidebarRightTabs`, `webTerminals`, `theme`, `shortcuts`, `slots`, `locale`.
2. To open a terminal tab: `tab.actions.openTab("terminal", { params: { shellPath } })` — or `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabFromTarget("terminal", target)`.
3. `ctx.webTerminals` is the client service that owns terminal views: `ctx.webTerminals.view(sessionId, key, contentId, terminalId?, shellPath?)`, `ctx.webTerminals.launchShells(sessionId, signal)`, `ctx.webTerminals.selectShell(path)`, `ctx.webTerminals.retainTabs(...)`, `ctx.webTerminals.close(...)`.

So the cleanest path for my plugin:
- Register a **slot** in the sidebar (e.g. `sidebar.panellist` — "Global panel icons") or `sidebar.footer.action`.
- On click: open a terminal tab via `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabFromTarget("terminal", target)` with params `{ shellPath }`.

But `shellPath` must be a **discovered shell** (from `shellCandidates`: zsh, bash, fish, pwsh, powershell, cmd) resolved via `subprocess.resolveExecutable`. On Windows, `cmd` and `powershell`/`pwsh` are available. My SSH command is not a shell.

Hmm. So how do I get `ssh` into the terminal?

Wait — key insight. Let me re-read `TerminalController.spawn`:

```js
const shell = request.shellPath === void 0
  ? await resolveShell(subprocess, this.config.shell, signal)
  : (await this.shells(agent, signal)).find((candidate) => candidate.path === request.shellPath)
if (shell === void 0) throw new Error("Selected shell is not available in this execution environment")
const handle = await subprocess.spawnTerminal({
  argv: [shell.path, ...shell.args], ...
})
```

So `shellPath` is restricted to discovered shells. But `shellCandidates` is plugin **config** on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-terminal-controller`. I can patch that config via cordis.patch.yml to add a candidate — e.g. a wrapper executable that I install on PATH which execs ssh. `profile(candidate)` → args `["-i"]` for non-cmd shells. My wrapper ignores extra args.

Wait, but `discoverShells` calls `resolveShell(subprocess, profile(candidate), signal)`, and `resolveShell` calls `subprocess.resolveExecutable(shell.path)`. `subprocess` here is the Host's subprocess service (local Windows). If I put `dzrobot-ssh.cmd` or `dzrobot-ssh.exe` on PATH, `resolveExecutable('dzrobot-ssh')` would find it. On Windows, `.cmd` resolution — `resolveExecutable` probably uses `where`-like resolution and may or may not handle `.cmd`. There's a risk.

Hmm, but hold on. Is there a simpler, more robust route? Let me think about what `ssh` needs:
- A PTY for interactive password/keys — but we already have **key-based passwordless** login working (`BatchMode=yes` succeeded!). So `ssh -tt duzhong@duzhong.local` needs no interactive input.
- The terminal controller spawns `[shell.path, ...shell.args]` with cwd = session workspace.

**Alternative approach that avoids all this**: Don't use the DSH terminal at all for the SSH session. Instead, my plugin's sidebar button opens a **rightbar tab of my own kind** (I can register a tab kind via `sidebarRightTabs.register`) whose body is my own React component rendering an `<iframe>`? No.

Better: my plugin can render a terminal into its own tab using **the xterm bundle that ships in the terminal package**? Not accessible from my package (it's `require.async('./client.terminal.js')` relative to that package). Client plugins load via ModuleLoader with `require` for shared modules; xterm may be exposed. Let me check `client.terminal.js` header to see what it imports — if it does `require('@xterm/xterm')` then ModuleLoader might expose xterm to my package too. Let me check.

Actually, let me step back and consider the **most robust approach given constraints**:

**Approach A (shim shell)**: Patch `api-terminal-controller` config `shellCandidates` to include a shim executable name, install a shim script (e.g. `dzrobot-ssh.cmd` / `.exe`) on PATH that execs `ssh -tt duzhong@duzhong.local "$@"`-ish. Then my sidebar button opens a terminal tab with `params: { shellPath: <resolved shim path> }`. The DSH terminal machinery gives a real interactive terminal, resize, scrollback, everything. The shim appears in the terminal's shell picker (bonus).

Risk: `resolveExecutable` on Windows + `.cmd`; PATH mutation; the shim's argv `['-i']`.

Hmm, actually wait. Do I even need a shim? What if I use `cmd` or `pwsh` as the shell... no, argv is fixed at spawn.

Let me check whether `subprocess.spawnTerminal` is reachable from my plugin directly: my Host half could call `ctx.subprocess.spawnTerminal({argv: ['ssh', ...], ...})` — but then I'd have to implement the whole BrowserTerminal + Remote stream plumbing to show it in the browser. That's exactly what `terminalController` does. Not feasible without reimplementing 1000 lines.

**Approach B (two-click, no shim)**: sidebar button opens the terminal tab (default shell), and *types* the ssh command into it via the terminal write API. The client service `ctx.webTerminals.view(...)` returns a TerminalView with `.write(data)`. So: open terminal tab → get view → `view.write('ssh duzhong@duzhong.local\r')`. That's a "click in the sidebar → an SSH session starts" experience with zero shims/config patching, using only public client services!

That's elegant. The terminal opens and the ssh command runs automatically. The view's `write` requires `writable` state (attached + running + controller). Timing: need to wait for phase === 'connected' before writing. The view is observable (`view.state.subscribe`).

But there's a subtlety: `ctx.webTerminals.view(sessionId, key, contentId, terminalId?, shellPath?)` — the args come from tab params. To open a tab and get a view, I need the tab key and contentId. Alternatively `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabFromTarget("terminal", target)` opens a tab; then I need its key to compose the view.

Hmm, this is getting deep into undocumented client services (`webTerminals`, `sidebarRight`). They're real services in the live slot tree (I saw `sidebar.right.pane.tab` occupancy), and `cordis_inspect_query` on client Service listed only: layout, locale, sessions, slots, theme, timer, uiWorkspace, workspaces. **`webTerminals` and `sidebarRight` are NOT in the inspectable client Service catalog!** That means they exist but aren't part of the public/documented service surface I can rely on... Actually the inspect catalog listed only 8 services; the sidebar-terminal plugin's `inject` names `sidebarRight`, `sidebarRightTabs`, `webTerminals` — those are real client services but maybe registered as non-Service or in a scope the inspector doesn't show. The inspector might show only root-scope Services. Hmm, they might be client-only services not exposed via the Service inspect provider (which may only list ones registered with certain metadata).

Given the risk, let me verify empirically what's available to a client plugin. But I can't easily introspect the client at runtime without writing a plugin and loading it...

**Approach C (safest, fully self-contained)**: My plugin's sidebar button opens a **settings/rightbar panel of my own** that offers "打开 SSH 终端" and does the connection through my own Host API — and for the interactive session, uses the documented, inspectable **terminalController Remote API** (`ctx.remote.terminal.create/follow/write/resize`) with the **`shellPath` restriction**... which blocks ssh.

OK so the shellPath restriction is the crux. Let me actually test what `shells()` returns and whether a shim works. Empirical testing beats speculation.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider. There's a **much better idea**. What is `shellCandidates`? It's config: `["zsh","bash","fish","pwsh","powershell","cmd"]`. `resolveShell(subprocess, configured, signal)` — `configured` is `this.config.shell` = `{path, name, args}`. The **configured shell** is used as the *preferred* shell and is NOT restricted to candidates! Look:

```js
async function discoverShells(subprocess, configured, candidates, signal) {
  const preferred = await resolveShell(subprocess, configured, signal);
  ...
  for (const shell of [preferred, ...found]) { ... }
```

```js
tab.actions.openTab("terminal", { replaceTab: true, params: { shellPath: path } })
```

`params: { shellPath }` — the tab params carry `shellPath`, and the terminal body creates the terminal with that shellPath. And `spawn()` resolves shellPath against `discoverShells(...)`. So ANY registered shell candidate works.

Now: **`shellCandidates` is config** of api-terminal-controller. If I add a candidate that is an actual shell-like executable I control, I can pass its path. The cleanest, least intrusive candidate: a real executable already on PATH that can run ssh? No.

BUT — what about `cmd`? `profile('cmd')` → kind 'cmd' → args `[]`. `resolveShell(subprocess, profile('cmd'))` → resolves `cmd` → `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe` with args `[]`. So creating a terminal with `shellPath = 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\cmd.exe'` spawns `cmd.exe` with no args, cwd = workspace, interactive. Then I can write `ssh duzhong@duzhong.local\r` into it! **cmd.exe is already a candidate** (`shellCandidates` default includes `"cmd"`). And on Windows, `discoverShells` also tries `pwsh`, `powershell`, `zsh`, `bash`, `fish` — those that exist get included. So `powershell` and `cmd` will definitely be found on Windows.

I'll capture the return value of openTabFromTarget in the diag too.

(b) **Dynamic Client half** (cordis_define-style): the Client Builtins list (`ctx`, `React`, `host`, `styles`, `console`) applies to *dynamic* client halves created by the Cordis tools.

I'll go with (a) — proven by two shipped plugins.

Now I have everything needed for the client side:

- `ctx.sidebarRight.commandTarget(element)` → `{sessionId, paneId, host, tabId, occurrence, navigationRevision}` or `undefined` if no session is on-screen.
- `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabFromTarget('terminal', target)` → opens a terminal tab using the guide's placement rules. **Returns undefined** (void). So I need to find the tab afterwards.
- `ctx.sidebarRight.tabDomain.occurrence(sessionId, {id: key})` → held occurrence with `.navigation` snapshot (`{params, address, revision}`).
- `ctx.webTerminals.view(sessionId, key, contentId, terminalId, shellPath)` → TerminalView.

Getting the key of the newly opened tab: `openTabFromTarget` doesn't return it. But `tabDomain` can list occurrences? `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabs` is a snapshot store of tabs; the sidebar-terminal plugin uses `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabs.getSnapshot().filter(tab => tab.kind === 'terminal')` where each tab has `.sessionId`, `.contentId`, `.tabId`, `.kind`. 

So after `openTabFromTarget('terminal', target)`, I can poll `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabs.getSnapshot()` for a terminal tab in that session that is new. Then `view = ctx.webTerminals.view(sessionId, tab.tabId, tab.contentId, undefined, undefined)`.

Hmm wait — but by opening the tab, the terminal body component mounts and itself calls `ctx.webTerminals.view(sessionId, key, contentId, terminalId, shellPath)` (from the sidebar-terminal's `view()` helper with the same key/contentId). Since `view()` caches by `(sessionId, key)`, calling it from my plugin with the same tabId returns the SAME TerminalView instance. 

Then I wait for `view.state` snapshot phase === 'connected' && writable, then `view.write('ssh ...\r')`.

Note: `TerminalView.refresh()` is called on `view()` creation; `mount()` triggers connect. The body's mount happens when the tab renders. My call to `view()` might happen before the body mounts — but `view()` returns the cached instance and `mount()` is called by the body. If my plugin calls `view()` first, it creates the view and calls `refresh()` (which creates the terminal). Then the body's `view()` returns the same instance and calls `mount()`. Fine.

Risk: if the body's `view()` is called with a different `shellPath`... it uses tab params. Both undefined → default shell.

So the flow works. The write must wait for `writable === true` (phase 'connected' and `controllerId === attachmentId`). Good.

Now, **is `sidebarRight` reachable?** It's a client service; the terminal plugin injects it. I'll use `ctx.get('sidebarRight')` defensively and report to diag.

I'll pass my button's element via ref. `commandTarget(element)`: `focusedTarget(element)` uses `sidebarTargetFromElement(element, ...)` → if my element is not inside a sidebar-right pane, it returns undefined; then `if (focused !== undefined || element?.closest("[data-sidebar-right-session]"))` — my footer button isn't inside that; then falls back to `screen()` — the on-screen session's active dock pane. That's what I want ("open from outside"). 

So passing my element works: it falls back to the on-screen session's active pane.

{"content": "# dsh-dzrobot-ssh

在 DeepSeek Harness 的**侧边栏一键 SSH 连上小车**（RK3588 / `duzhong.local`）。

然后把 `ssh` 命令**输入到 DSH 自带的终端里**——所以你得到的是真正的交互式终端：回显、
Tab 补全、Ctrl-C、窗口缩放、回滚缓冲全都是应用自带的那一套，不是另做一份仿制品。

## 为什么这样做

DSH 的终端服务在 Host 侧只允许用**已发现的 shell** 启动进程（`shellPath` 必须是
`subprocess.resolveExecutable` 能解析出来的候选 shell），所以插件不能直接把
`ssh` 当成一个 shell 塞进去。于是分成两半：

| 半身 | 负责 |
| --- | --- |
| Host (`index.js`) | 配置、探测（`ssh -o BatchMode=yes`）、小车信息、本地 JSON API |
| Client (`client.js`) | 侧栏按钮、设置页；打开终端标签页并把命令行写进去 |

交互式终端由 DSH 终端服务承载，插件只负责"打开 + 输入命令"，因此不重复实现终端。

关键取舍：探测路径一律带 `BatchMode=yes`。它关掉所有交互式提问，所以需要密码的小车会
**明确报"需要密码"**，而不是卡在一个看不见的提示符上。真正打开的交互式终端不带这个限制，
所以需要密码的小车照样能用——在终端里手输一次密码即可。

## 安装

已经在 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop` 里注册好了：

- `node_modules/dsh-dzrobot-ssh` → 指向本目录的 **junction**（改这里的代码立刻生效）
- `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里加了 `dsh-dzrobot-ssh`
- 这个包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 负责挂载 Host 半身；浏览器半身由 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client` 声明

Host 半身是热加载的（改完立刻生效）。**浏览器半身需要刷新页面**——页面的启动清单是在
加载时注入的，新插件不会自己出现在已经打开的页面上。

## 配置

默认值来自这台机器上已有的 `~/.ssh/config`：主机 `duzhong.local`、用户 `duzhong`、
端口 22、走 `~/.ssh/id_rsa` 免密。

设置页（Settings → 小车 SSH）可以改：主机/IP、用户名、端口、`ssh` 别名（填了优先用别名）、
附带的 `ssh` 参数。配置存在 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/settings.json`。

## HTTP API

前缀 `/api/dzrobot-ssh`（仅本机回环可访问；有 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断）。

| 方法 | 路径 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/status` | 配置、上次探测结果、小车信息、等价命令行 |
| POST | `/probe[?car=0]` | 探测可达性与免密登录；`car=0` 跳过信息采集 |
| POST | `/describe` | 只采集小车信息（用户/主机名/内核/运行时长） |
| GET/POST | `/config` | 读取 / 保存配置（空主机名会被拒） |
| GET/POST | `/diag` | 诊断日志（浏览器半身上报，落 `diag.jsonl`） |
| GET/POST | `/selftest` | 一次性自检开关 |

```bash
node scripts/check-ssh.mjs            # 直接测 SSH 层（含真实登录）
node scripts/test-host.mjs            # Host 半身：路由 + 真实探测 + 配置校验
node scripts/test-client.mjs          # Client 半身：完整连接流程（打桩侧栏/终端服务）
```

`test-client.mjs` 会打桩 `sidebarRight` / `webTerminals`，验证"打开终端 → 等可写 →
写入 ssh 命令"的完整链路，所以对这两个服务的行为假设一旦错了，会在脚本里失败，
而不是变成界面上一次没反应的点击。

## 排错

- **图标是红点**：小车不可达。检查它是否已上电、是否连上同一 WiFi（本机与它同在
  `192.168.43.x`），以及 `ping duzhong.local`。
- **黄点 / "需要密码"**：能连上但免密不成立。把本机公钥装到小车：
  `ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub duzhong@duzhong.local`（或手动追加到
  `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`）。
- **点一下没反应**：看 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/diag.jsonl`，每一步都有记录；
  也可以在设置页复制等价命令，直接在终端里粘贴运行。

## 先回答你那个问题

**不能。** 另一个 DSH 对话窗口是独立的会话，我派生的 teammate 共享的是**我**这个会话的工作目录，跟那边不互通。所以我没有"等武将连上"——我自己探测了一下，发现小车**已经连上了**，就直接开工了：

- `duzhong.local` → `192.168.43.17`（和你本机 `192.168.43.18` 同网段），22 端口通
- RK3588 aarch64，内核 `6.1.43-rockchip-rk3588`，用户 `duzhong`
- 你 `~/.ssh/config` 里本来就有 `dzrobot` 条目，`id_rsa` 免密**直接可用**（比我原本打算做的密码登录更省事，所以按免密实现，密码登录也照常能用）

## 交付物

[README.md](dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh/README.md) · 代码在 [dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh](dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh)

已注册进 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`（junction 指向工作区，Host 半身 `fiberPhase: active`，改代码立刻生效）。

**关键设计**：DSH 的终端服务只允许用"已发现的 shell"启动进程（`shellPath` 必须能解析），所以不能把 `ssh` 当 shell 塞进去。于是拆成两半——Host 负责探测和拼命令，Client 负责**打开 DSH 自带终端标签页并把命令写进去**。你得到的是真正的交互式终端：回显、Tab 补全、Ctrl-C、缩放、回滚全是应用自带那套。

## 已验证的证据

三套测试全过（`check-ssh` / `test-host` / `test-client`，含真实 SSH），另外在**真实浏览器里**跑通了一次完整链路：

```
connect.probe   → state:"ready", 661ms        ← 真实探测小车
connect.tab     → tab2 终端标签页打开
connect.writable→ phase:"connected" cmd.exe running   ← 终端真的起来了
connect.wrote   → ssh ... duzhong@duzhong.local       ← 命令已写入并回车
```

**小车侧的铁证**：当时车上有活着的 `sshd: duzhong@pts/1` 登录会话，`who` 里能看到 pts/1 从你本机 IPv6 地址登入。（我自己的诊断命令都是 `@notty`，所以 pts/1 只可能来自那个终端。）

顺带修了一个坑：测试脚本原先会和线上共用 `settings.json`，跑测试可能改掉你的小车地址——现在测试走临时 `DSH_HOME`，实测前后线上配置字节一致。

## 还差你一下

侧栏图标已注册、两个组件都能正常渲染（`render(sidebar.footer.action) -> element`），但**你自己那一次点击**我没法代替。你刷新页面后：

- 看 **Settings 旁边**有没有小车图标（左上角有状态点：绿=可免密登录，红=不可达，黄=需要密码）
- 点一下 → 右侧应弹出终端并自动 ssh 登入
- 想排查就翻 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/diag.jsonl`，每一步都有记录（我已经清空，等你这一下）

没刷新的话现在看不到图标——浏览器半身要刷新才加载，这一步我替不了你。

content.text: 接下来我们再对插件进行更新，更新VNC链接，进入该插件后，可以根据需要自由选择vnc界面窗口或是终端窗口，还有文件目录窗口，文件目录下可访问小车的文件目录

The user wants to extend the plugin:
1. Add VNC connection
2. After entering the plugin, freely choose between: VNC window / terminal window / file directory window
3. File directory window: browse the car's file directories (SFTP-ish)

So this is a bigger feature: a full "car" panel with three tabs/views:
- VNC (remote desktop to the car)
- Terminal (SSH terminal — already works)
- Files (browse car's filesystem)

{"content": "#!/bin/bash
# Probe the car for remote-desktop and file-access facilities.
# Run with: Get-Content probe-vnc.sh -Raw | ssh duzhong@duzhong.local "bash -s"

echo "=== session / display ==="
echo "XDG_SESSION_TYPE=${XDG_SESSION_TYPE:-?} DISPLAY=${DISPLAY:-?(unset)}"
loginctl list-sessions --no-legend 2>/dev/null | head -10

echo
echo "=== VNC-ish processes ==="
ps -eo pid,etime,cmd 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei 'vnc|xrdp|websockify|novnc' | grep -v grep
echo "(end of process list)"

echo
echo "=== listening TCP ports ==="
ss -lntp 2>/dev/null | head -40

echo
echo "=== VNC binaries ==="
for b in x11vnc wayvnc tigervncserver vncserver Xvnc x0vncserver websockify novnc_proxy vncpasswd; do
  p=$(command -v "$b" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$p" ]; then echo "FOUND $b -> $p"; else echo "no    $b"; fi

Excellent, very informative:

**VNC on the car:**
- `Xtigervnc :1` listening on **0.0.0.0:5901** (and IPv6), `-SecurityTypes VncAuth,TLSVnc`, password file `/home/duzhong/.vnc/passwd`, geometry 1280x800x24.
- systemd unit `vncserver@:1.service` active/running.
- No websockify/noVNC on the car.
- **xrdp is installed** (0.9.17) — RDP, port 3389, but not listening (no xrdp process).
- VNC port 5901 is reachable from the network (0.0.0.0 bind).

**SFTP**: `/usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server` exists → SFTP works over SSH.

So for VNC in the browser I need:
1. A WebSocket↔TCP bridge on the Host (DSH side) to reach 5901 (ideally through an SSH tunnel so we don't depend on the VNC port being exposed, and to avoid the VNC password prompt... but VncAuth still requires the VNC password; the tunnel doesn't remove that).
2. A noVNC client in the browser.

Options for the bridge:
- DSH's `webServer.registerUpgrade(route)` — **there's a websocket upgrade registration!** I saw `registerUpgrade(route: WebUpgradeRoute)` in the webServer service. That's exactly what I need: my Host half can register a WS upgrade route at `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` and pipe frames to a TCP socket connected to the car's 5901. 

For noVNC: I need the client JS. Options:
(a) Download noVNC from npm/GitHub and vendor it into my plugin (served as a client asset). noVNC's modern package (`@novnc/novnc`) is an ES module ~ several hundred KB. I'd need to serve it from my plugin and load it in the browser.
(b) Write a **minimal RFB client myself** in the client half. RFB protocol with VncAuth (DES challenge-response) + raw/hextile encoding... Writing a VNC client from scratch is substantial (DES for VncAuth is the annoying part; but if I use **TLSVnc or None**... no, VncAuth needs DES). Actually implementing DES in JS is ~150 lines (or use WebCrypto? WebCrypto has no DES). doable but risky, plus framebuffer decoding, pointer/keyboard events, and those images can be big. Too much.
(c) Since noVNC is available on npm, I could `pnpm add @novnc/novnc` into the profile and load it... but client plugin assets are loaded via ModuleLoader — `require('@novnc/novnc')` would only work if it's in the client module graph, which is for `dsh.client` plugins, not arbitrary deps. Hand-written client.js can't import arbitrary npm packages.

Hmm, wait: how does the client module loader resolve `require('react')`? It's a shared module registry. Only shell-provided modules. So no noVNC.

(d) **Use the car's own xrdp + browser RDP?** No browser RDP client either.

(e) **Check the 8080 python3 process** — the docs said "网页 :8080（浏览器实时画面弹窗）". That's the project's own camera-viewer web page (`tools/cam_viewer.py` + `cam_viewer.html` in my workspace!). That's the vision window over HTTP — a live camera view. Not a full desktop.

So for a real VNC view inside DSH, I need noVNC vendored.

Let me check: can I download noVNC? I have `web_fetch` (returns text) and PowerShell with internet. The machine has internet (the car connects via the phone hotspot; the laptop downloaded things?). Let me test connectivity to npm registry / GitHub via PowerShell.

If I can download `@novnc/novnc` (the npm tarball or GitHub release), I can vendor `lib/` (or the built `novnc.esm.js`?) into my plugin as static assets, serve them via my own HTTP route (`/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/...`), and load the ES module in an iframe or via dynamic import in my client half.

That's the pragmatic route. noVNC npm package structure: `@novnc/novnc` ships `lib/` (ES modules: `core/rfb.js`, etc.) plus `lib/vendor/...`. There's also a bundled single-file build? The npm package has `lib/` ES modules and requires an import map or bundler. Hmm — loading ES modules from my plugin's static route works: `<script type="module">import RFB from '/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/core/rfb.js'</script>`, but rfb.js imports relative paths (`./util/...`, `../vendor/...`) — those resolve against the module URL, so if I serve the whole `lib/` tree at a stable path prefix, relative imports work natively in the browser! That's clean: serve the directory tree, and the browser resolves the module graph.

Alternatively serve noVNC's prebuilt `vnc.html`+`vnc_lite.html` app in an **iframe** — noVNC's release tarball includes `vnc.html`, `app/`, and `lib/` and works when served over HTTP. Then my panel just iframes `/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/vnc.html?autoconnect=1&host=...&port=...&password=...`. Using the stock app in an iframe is FAR less work than wiring RFB myself, and it's a proven UI. But it's a whole separate UI inside the panel (with its own toolbar) — acceptable and arguably good.

But wait: noVNC's websocket must point to my bridge. noVNC connects to a WebSocket URL: by default `ws://host:port/websockify`. It can connect to any WS path if configured (`path` parameter in vnc.html: `path=api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc`). And the DSH web server's `registerUpgrade` gives me that WS endpoint on the same origin/port. 

So the architecture:
- Host: `webServer.registerUpgrade({kind:'exact', path:'/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc'})` → on upgrade, open a TCP socket to `127.0.0.1:<localPort>` where `<localPort>` is an **SSH tunnel** to the car's 5901 (or connect directly to the car's 5901 if reachable—but tunnel is better/secure). Pipe WS binary frames ↔ TCP.
- Host: serve noVNC static files under `/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/*` (read from a vendored directory, prevent path traversal).
- Client: panel with three views: VNC (iframe), Terminal (opens DSH terminal tab OR embeds?), Files (my own tree browser).

Hmm, but embedding a full noVNC app in an iframe inside DSH's main panel... the iframe needs auth? My API routes are fenced by loopback/connection.admit. An iframe request carries the same cookies/token? The DSH web app authenticates API calls with a token in the URL or header (connection.authenticatedUrl suggests token in URL). If my iframe URL lacks the token, my fence might reject it (403) — since `rejectionFor` uses `connection.admit` when available. Earlier, my curl without a token got 200, which means `connection.admit` is absent or permissive on the Host ctx. So iframe should pass. But assets (novnc JS/CSS) need to load too — same fence.

Risk: if `connection.admit` exists and requires a token, my iframe would 403. Mitigation: reuse DSH's `ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl(baseUrl)` to build the iframe src with the token! I saw that method: `authenticatedUrl(baseUrl: string): string`. That's exactly designed for this. I can call it from the client via... it's a *host* service (`ctx.connection` on host). The client can get it via my own API: `GET /status` could return `authenticatedUrl('/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/vnc.html')`. 

Let me keep that as a fallback if iframe loading fails.

Now, the **Files** view: browse the car's filesystem. Implementation via `ssh` commands:
- List: `ssh car "ls -la --time-style=+%s <path>"` — parse. Better: use a robust delimiter-based listing, or `find`/`stat` with a machine-readable format. Simplest robust: 
  `ssh car "LC_ALL=C ls -lA --time-style=long-iso --quoting-style=literal <path>"` and parse columns — parsing `ls` is fragile for filenames with spaces. Better approach: use `sftp`! Since sftp-server exists, and the OpenSSH client has `sftp` in batch mode:
  `sftp -b - duzhong@car` with commands like `ls -l /path`, `get`, `put`. In batch mode, `ls -l` output is still `ls`-formatted. Hmm.
  
  Cleaner: use `ssh car "python3 -c '...'"`? The car has python3 (a python3 listens on 8080). A remote python one-liner emitting JSON for a directory listing is robust and easy. But depends on python3 being present (it is, since the cam viewer runs).
  
  Even more robust: base64-encode a `find`-style output with NUL delimiters. E.g.:
  `ssh car "cd <path> && find . -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f\0%y\0%s\0%T@\0' | base64 -w0"` — but `find -printf` needs GNU find (present on Ubuntu). This handles arbitrary filenames safely (NUL-separated, base64-wrapped).
  
  I like the NUL+base64 approach — no parsing ambiguity, no python dependency. Let me use:
  ```
  cd -- "$path" 2>/dev/null && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%f\0%y\0%s\0%T@\0' | base64 -w0
  ```
  Then parse in Node: decode base64 → split on \0 in groups of 4.
  Also need to handle the root/parent navigation and permission errors.
  
  For file content preview: `ssh car "base64 -w0 -- <file>"` bounded by size check first (`stat -c %s`).
  Download: same as preview but streamed; for simplicity, provide a download that returns base64 with a size cap (e.g. 5 MB) — or a proper streaming route. Let me cap and also allow "copy path".
  Upload: `ssh car "cat > <path>"` with stdin=file bytes. Via my API POST with the body streamed. Nice-to-have; the user only asked to *access* the car's directories ("文件目录下可访问小车的文件目录" = can access the car's file dirs). Browsing + preview + download is the core; upload is a bonus. I'll implement browse + preview/download, and maybe upload if budget allows.

Now: how do these three views surface? The user says "进入该插件后，可以根据需要自由选择vnc界面窗口或是终端窗口，还有文件目录窗口".

Design: **a main panel** (`sidebar.panellist` icon + `main` keyed view) titled "小车" with a segmented switcher: VNC | 终端 | 文件.
- VNC view: iframe to noVNC (autoconnect, via my WS bridge).
- 终端 view: embed? Can't embed DSH's terminal in the main panel (it's a rightbar tab kind). Options: (a) a button "在右侧打开终端" that opens the DSH terminal tab (proven path), plus a small inline "quick command" area? (b) Implement my own terminal view in the panel by rendering DSH's terminal... not possible (xterm is bundled elsewhere).
   Best honest approach: the Terminal view in the panel shows the current SSH target, a big "打开终端" button that opens the native DSH terminal tab (the proven, full-fidelity path), plus recent connection info. I'll be explicit in the UI that the terminal opens in DSH's own terminal so it's the real thing.
   
   Hmm, but the user wants a *window* choice inside the plugin. Reusing DSH's terminal tab IS a window choice — it opens the terminal. I think that's acceptable and better than a worse terminal. But could I render an embedded terminal? Another idea: the DSH rightbar terminal is reachable via URL/layout — I could make the panel's Terminal option open a **floating** terminal pane (dockkit has float). `openTabFromTarget` with host 'float'... There's `ctx.sidebarRight.float`/`dock`/`split` in the service methods I saw: `split`, `toggleFullscreen`, `float`, `dock`. So I could offer "嵌入侧栏" vs... too deep.

   Decision: Terminal view = launcher + status (opens native terminal tab). Clear and reliable.

   Wait — actually, maybe better: since the panel is a *main* panel (center column), and DSH terminals live in the right sidebar, the "free choice" experience is: my panel = the car's cockpit with VNC embedded and Files embedded, and Terminal = a button that opens the right-sidebar terminal. I'll present it that way in the UI.

- Files view: my own tree/list browser with breadcrumb, click to enter dir, preview text files, download.

Given the size of this, let me plan carefully and use todos. Also, I must be careful about token budget — this is a big feature. Let me be efficient and methodical.

**Step 1**: Verify I can get noVNC (download from npm/GitHub). Check internet access.
**Step 2**: Build the Host side: VNC WS bridge (SSH tunnel + upgrade route), noVNC static serving, Files API (list/stat/read/download), all fenced.
**Step 3**: Client: main panel + panellist icon, three views.
**Step 4**: Test: host tests for files API + WS bridge; verify noVNC loads; user refresh.

Let me also decide about the VNC password: `Xtigervnc -SecurityTypes VncAuth,TLSVnc` with `-PasswordFile /home/duzhong/.vnc/passwd` → VNC auth requires a password. I need the VNC password to auto-connect. It's stored (hashed) in `~/.vnc/passwd` on the car — the plaintext isn't recoverable. Options:
- Ask the user for the VNC password and store it in settings (default empty).

- No websockify/noVNC on the car.
- **xrdp is installed** (0.9.17) — RDP, port 3389, but not listening (no xrdp process).
- VNC port 5901 is reachable from the network (0.0.0.0 bind).

**SFTP**: `/usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server` exists → SFTP works over SSH.

So for VNC in the browser I need:
1. A WebSocket↔TCP bridge on the Host (DSH side) to reach 5901 (ideally through an SSH tunnel so we don't depend on the VNC port being exposed, and to avoid the VNC password prompt... but VncAuth still requires the VNC password; the tunnel doesn't remove that).

Options for the bridge:

That's exactly what I need: my Host half can register a WS upgrade route at `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` and pipe frames to a TCP socket connected to the car's 5901. 

For noVNC: I need the client JS. Options:
(a) Download noVNC from npm/GitHub and vendor it into my plugin (served as a client asset). noVNC's modern package (`@novnc/novnc`) is an ES module ~ several hundred KB. I'd need to serve it from my plugin and load it in the browser.
(b) Write a **minimal RFB client myself** in the client half. RFB protocol with VncAuth (DES challenge-response) + raw/hextile encoding... Writing a VNC client from scratch is substantial (DES for VncAuth is the annoying part; but if I use **TLSVnc or None**... no, VncAuth needs DES). Actually implementing DES in JS is ~150 lines (or use WebCrypto? WebCrypto has no DES). doable but risky, plus framebuffer decoding, pointer/keyboard events, and those images can be big. Too much.
(c) Since noVNC is available on npm, I could `pnpm add @novnc/novnc` into the profile and load it... but client plugin assets are loaded via ModuleLoader — `require('@novnc/novnc')` would only work if it's in the client module graph, which is for `dsh.client` plugins, not arbitrary deps. Hand-written client.js can't import arbitrary npm packages.

Hmm, wait: how does the client module loader resolve `require('react')`? It's a shared module registry. Only shell-provided modules. So no noVNC.

(d) **Use the car's own xrdp + browser RDP?** No browser RDP client either.

(e) **Check the 8080 python3 process** — the docs said "网页 :8080（浏览器实时画面弹窗）". That's the project's own camera-viewer web page (`tools/cam_viewer.py` + `cam_viewer.html` in my workspace!). That's the vision window over HTTP — a live camera view. Not a full desktop.

Let me check: can I download noVNC? I have `web_fetch` (returns text) and PowerShell with internet. The machine has internet (the car connects via the phone hotspot; the laptop downloaded things?). Let me test connectivity to npm registry / GitHub via PowerShell.

If I can download `@novnc/novnc` (the npm tarball or GitHub release), I can vendor `lib/` (or the built `novnc.esm.js`?) into my plugin as static assets, serve them via my own HTTP route (`/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/...`), and load the ES module in an iframe or via dynamic import in my client half.

That's the pragmatic route. noVNC npm package structure: `@novnc/novnc` ships `lib/` (ES modules: `core/rfb.js`, etc.) plus `lib/vendor/...`. There's also a bundled single-file build? The npm package has `lib/` ES modules and requires an import map or bundler. {"command": "$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'
$tmp="$env:TEMP\novnc-get"; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $tmp | Out-Null
"=== registry reachable? ==="
try {
  $meta = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://registry.npmjs.org/@novnc/novnc" -TimeoutSec 25
  "OK  latest=$($meta.'dist-tags'.latest)"
  $v = $meta.'dist-tags'.latest
  $url = $meta.versions.$v.dist.tarball
  "tarball=$url"
  $tgz = "$tmp\novnc.tgz"
  Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $tgz -TimeoutSec 120
  "downloaded $((Get-Item $tgz).Length) bytes"
} catch { "registry FAILED: $($_.Exception.Message)" }", "description": "Download noVNC from npm registry", "timeoutMs": 200000}

content.text:
`this._wsProtocols = options.wsProtocols || []` — so by default no subprotocol is requested. I can pass `wsProtocols: ['binary']` to make the subprotocol explicit, and my bridge will echo it. Since default is `[]`, the WebSocket sends no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header. My bridge must therefore handle the no-subprotocol case (respond without the header) and treat frames as raw binary. 

Simplest correct design: my bridge does NOT require a subprotocol; it echoes `binary` only if the client asked for it. Data frames → raw bytes to TCP. That works with default noVNC usage and with `wsProtocols:['binary']`.

Let me look at RFB's constructor options and the important events/methods I'll use:
- `new RFB(target, url, options)` where options include `credentials: {password, username}`, `wsProtocols`, `shared`, `viewOnly`, `scaleViewport`, `resizeSession`, `qualityLevel`, `compressionLevel`, `showDotCursor`, `background`, `clipViewport`, `dragViewport`, `focusOnClick`, `touchButton`.
- Events: `connect`, `disconnect`, `credentialsrequired`, `securityfailure`, `desktopname`, `clipboard`, `bell`, `capabilities`.
- Methods: `disconnect()`, `sendCredentials()`, `sendCtrlAltDel()`, `focus()`.

For my React view:
```js
const rfb = new RFB(canvasEl, wsUrl, { credentials: { password: pw || '' }, wsProtocols: ['binary'], shared: true, scaleViewport: true, resizeSession: true, background: '#000' })
rfb.addEventListener('connect', ...)
rfb.addEventListener('disconnect', e => ...)
rfb.addEventListener('credentialsrequired', () => { show password prompt })
rfb.addEventListener('securityfailure', e => ...)
```

But there's a subtlety in websockify: if the client requests `binary` and the server doesn't echo it, some browsers fail the connection. To be safe, my bridge will echo the requested subprotocol if present.

content.text:
Now I have the exact contract:

```js
registerUpgrade(route) {
  if (this.upgrades.has(route.path)) throw ...
  this.upgrades.set(route.path, route)
  return () => this.upgrades.delete(route.path)
}
```
- Route: `{ path: string, handler: (req, socket, head) => void }`
- Handler owns negotiation + socket use: I get the **raw TCP socket** and the upgrade `req` + `head`.
- So I must implement the WebSocket handshake myself (compute `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` from `Sec-WebSocket-Key` via SHA-1 + base64), respond 101, then frame/unframe WS messages myself.

That's very doable: I need a minimal WebSocket server implementation (handshake + frame parse/encode). ~150 lines. Since the payload is binary and can be large (VNC framebuffer updates from server→client; input events client→server small), I need:
- Server→client: send binary frames (unmasked, opcode 2), handle fragmentation/payload length (7-bit, 16-bit, 64-bit).
- Client→server: parse masked frames (opcode 2 binary, 8 close, 9 ping, 10 pong), unmask.

Browser noVNC may also negotiate with `wsProtocols: ['binary']` → echo `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: binary`.

Also `permessage-deflate` — if the browser offers it and I don't accept, it won't be used (unless the client requires it). Browsers offer `permessage-deflate` by default; not accepting is fine (the server must include the extension header to enable it).

Let me check: does DSH already have a WebSocket library? `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` uses `ws` maybe. The `web-server` handler for `/api`... `registerUpgrade` exists for things like terminal streams (the terminal uses Remote streams over WebSocket!). So DSH's own gateway handles WS upgrades — maybe via a `ws` package. If I could reuse their WS handling that'd be nice, but the API gives me the raw socket, so I implement it myself (or reuse a library if present).

Is `ws` available in the app's node_modules? Let me check `app.asar.unpacked/dsh/node_modules` (23 entries, no `ws`). And the runtime deps? Let me check the primary-runtime node_modules for `ws`. If available, I could import it — but plugin code should avoid depending on non-declared deps. My own implementation is safer (no dependency).

Let me write a compact RFC6455 server module. I'll be careful with:
- Handshake: validate `Upgrade: websocket`, compute accept key.
- Frame parsing: FIN/opcode, mask required from client, lengths (126 → 16-bit, 127 → 64-bit), unmask.
- Continuation frames: noVNC sends small messages; VNC server→client messages can be large (updates). For *sending*, I must support 16/64-bit lengths and no fragmentation needed (I can send one frame per message).
- Control frames: ping → pong; close → close handshake.
- Backpressure: `socket.write` returns false → wait for drain.

Then the TCP side: `net.connect(port, host)` to the car's VNC (direct) or to the SSH-tunnel local port.

Let me now decide the final architecture for the VNC bridge:

```
browser (noVNC RFB) --ws--> /api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc (DSH webServer upgrade) 
   --> my WS server (handshake + framing)
   --> TCP → target (direct: duzhong.local:5901, or tunnel: 127.0.0.1:<localPort>)
```

For the tunnel mode, I'd spawn `ssh -N -L <localPort>:127.0.0.1:5901 user@host`. Let me implement it since it's genuinely more robust (works with localhost-bound VNC, encrypts traffic) — and the user's car currently binds 0.0.0.0 so direct works too. I'll default to `tunnel` because:
- It never requires the VNC port to be exposed on the network.
- It reuses the SSH we already verified.
Hmm, but tunnel adds a process per connection and potential port races. Let me default to **direct** (simplest, works now, zero moving parts) and offer `tunnel` as an option. Actually...

Let me think about which is more likely to "just work" for the user right now: direct to `duzhong.local:5901`. The car binds 0.0.0.0:5901 and the laptop resolves duzhong.local → 192.168.43.17. Direct TCP will work. Tunnel requires spawning ssh -L which also works (verified ssh). Both work.

I'll implement direct as the default with an optional tunnel, and test BOTH (I can test the bridge headlessly by connecting a raw WS client to my own handler and checking the RFB version banner comes back — that's a great test that doesn't need a browser!).

**Headless VNC bridge test**: in-process, boot the host half with a stub webServer that captures the upgrade route, start a real HTTP server with an `upgrade` listener wired to the route handler, then connect a Node WebSocket client... Node has a built-in `WebSocket` client (Node 22+ has global WebSocket!). Node 24 → `globalThis.WebSocket` exists. It's a client-side WS implementation. I can use it to connect to my bridge, then send the RFB handshake and read the server's `RFB 003.008` banner. That proves the entire chain: WS framing, TCP connect to the car, and piping.

Even better: I can do a full noVNC-level test by... no, that needs DOM. The banner test is enough to prove the bridge.

   - `src/ws.js` — minimal RFC6455 server (handshake + frames).

Then the footer button opens it in the right sidebar (where terminals live), and a `sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry` gives it a card in the guide. That's closer to how DSH surfaces auxiliary tools, and it keeps the main column for conversation.

- Main panel: full width, dedicated "car station" — good for VNC (needs space) and file browsing.
- Rightbar tab: narrower, alongside terminal.

All host checks pass now. Note the traversal check returned 404 — because Node's http.request with an encoded path... it returned 404 rather than 403. Either way it's refused (not served). Good — but let me consider: did it 404 because `%2e%2e` was normalized by Node's client too (some clients normalize)? Node's `http.request` sends the path verbatim, so the server received `/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/package.json`. My handler: `route.startsWith('/novnc/')` → yes; `decodeURIComponent('..%2f..' )`... wait, my decode gives `../../package.json`; `path.resolve(NOVNC_DIR, '../../package.json')` → escapes → not inside → return 403. But I got 404.

Hmm, so maybe the request didn't reach my `/novnc/` branch. Why? `route` is computed as `url.pathname.replace(/^\/api\/dzrobot-ssh/, '')`. For the encoded path, `url.pathname` would be `/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/package.json` (WHATWG URL does NOT decode %2e in pathname... actually WHATWG URL DOES normalize `%2e%2e` in path segments! The URL spec treats `%2e` as `.` for path normalization purposes. So `new URL(...)` normalized it to `/api/dzrobot-ssh/package.json`. Then route = `/package.json` → no match → 404.

So the URL parser itself normalized the traversal before my guard — which is why it's 404. That's still a correct refusal (defense in depth: the platform normalized it), and my explicit guard remains as a second layer. The test asserts refusal, which is the security property that matters.

- Switcher (segmented): VNC | 终端 | 文件.
- Body area per view.

- A `<canvas>` (RFB creates its own canvas inside the target element actually — RFB's first arg is a target element; it creates a canvas child). So I pass a div ref.
- Dynamic import: `const { default: RFB } = await import('/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/core/rfb.js')`.
- Connect: `new RFB(div, wsUrl, { credentials: { password }, wsProtocols: ['binary'], shared: true, resizeSession: true, scaleViewport: true, background: '#000' })`.
- wsUrl: `(location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss:' : 'ws:') + '//' + location.host + '/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc'`.
- Events: connect/disconnect/credentialsrequired/securityfailure/desktopname.
- Toolbar: reconnect, fullscreen (via `rfb.clipViewport`/scale), Ctrl+Alt+Del (`rfb.sendCtrlAltDel()`), password field when required, status text.

**Terminal view**: same as before (open the DSH terminal tab) + status + the command line + copy. I'll also show "在右侧打开终端" button and note it uses DSH's native terminal.

- Breadcrumb of the current path (clickable segments).
- Shortcut chips (from `/status`.files.shortcuts).
- Entry list: icon (dir/file), name, size, mtime; click dir → navigate; click file → preview panel.
- Preview: text in a <pre>, binary → offer download; download button (anchor to `/download?path=`), upload button (file input → POST /upload?path=).
- Error display.

State per view; probe/status from the shared store (reuse createStore? The panel is a separate registration from the footer button; I'll reuse the same store instance so the dot and panel share state).

- `makeCarPanel(ctx, store, t)` returning the panel component.
- VNC hook: `useVnc(...)`.
- Files: `useFiles(...)`.
- Register panellist + main.

Important: the panel is root-scoped (main slot, no session binding) — so `commandTarget` for the terminal still resolves from the on-screen session. Fine.

{"content": "# dsh-dzrobot-ssh

在 DeepSeek Harness 里操作 **dzrobot 小车**（RK3588 / `duzhong.local`）：侧边栏图标进入小车面板，
面板里可以**自由切换三种窗口**——VNC 桌面、终端、文件目录。

| 窗口 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| **VNC 桌面** | 在面板里直接看到小车真实的 X 桌面（noVNC + WebSocket 隧道到小车的 TigerVNC :1） |
| **终端** | 一键在 DSH 自带终端里 `ssh` 登入小车——回显、Tab 补全、Ctrl-C、缩放都是原生的 |
| **文件目录** | 浏览小车的文件系统，看文本、下载、上传（走同一条已信任的 SSH 通道） |

另外侧栏底部（Settings 旁）还有一个**一键连终端**的小车按钮，不必先进入面板。

## 设计要点

**为什么终端不自己实现**：DSH 的终端服务在 Host 侧只允许用「已发现的 shell」启动进程，
所以插件不能把 `ssh` 当成 shell 塞进去。做法是：Host 拼好命令行，Client 打开 DSH 的终端标签页
并把命令写进去——于是你得到的是应用自带的那套终端，而不是一份仿制品。

**VNC 为什么要桥**：浏览器不能开裸 TCP 连到 5901，而小车上没有 websockify/noVNC。
所以 Host 半身做了两件事——在 `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` 注册一个 WebSocket upgrade 座位，
自己完成 RFC 6455 握手与分帧，然后把它和小车的 VNC 端口对接：

```
浏览器 noVNC  ──WebSocket──▶  /api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc  ──TCP──▶  小车 5901 (TigerVNC :1)
```

- `vncMode: direct`（默认）直接连 `<host>:5901`——小车当前就是 `0.0.0.0:5901`。
- `vncMode: tunnel` 走 `ssh -N -L`，当 VNC 只监听本地时只有这个模式能用，且复用已信任的 SSH。

桥是纯字节泵，不解析 RFB 流：编码方式、扩展、未来协议版本都归 noVNC 管。

**文件为什么要用 ssh 而不是 SFTP**：Host 没有 SFTP 客户端库，而 `ssh` 已经装好、已经认证、
已经验证过能连上这台车。所以每个操作就是一条 `ssh …命令`，答案用机器可读的格式回传：
目录列表用 `find -printf` 的 NUL 分隔字段再 base64 包裹（`ls` 解析会在机器人项目真实存在的
奇怪文件名上崩掉——名字里有空格、引号也能原样往返，`scripts/check-files.mjs` 就在测这个），
读取用 `base64 -w0`，下载用 `cat` 流式吐，上传用 `cat >` 流式收。

**安全**：所有路由只接受本机回环；装了 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断。
文件名与路径在进入远程 shell 之前，只经过 `src/files.js` 的 `quote()` 一个收口点。

## 安装位置

已经在 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop` 里注册好了：

- `node_modules/dsh-dzrobot-ssh` → 指向本目录的 **junction**（改这里的代码立刻生效）
- `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里加了 `dsh-dzrobot-ssh`
- 本包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 负责挂载 Host 半身；浏览器半身由 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client` 声明

## 改代码后怎么生效

| 改的是 | 生效方式 |
| --- | --- |
| `client.js`（浏览器半身） | 刷新页面 |
| `index.js` / `src/*`（Host 半身） | `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dzrobot-ssh/reload` |

Host 半身是 Node 的 ES 模块，进程按 URL 缓存，**改文件不会自动生效**。所以插件自带
`src/reload.js`：把本包从 loader 的模块缓存里逐出、重新 import、再注册到同一个 fiber 上，
失败会回滚到旧版本。也可以在该插件条目的 config 里写 `watchSources: true`，改文件自动重载。

> 新增 `src/*.js` 或改 `package.json` 的 exports 之后，第一次仍需重启应用一次
> （模块解析本身也被缓存）；之后普通改动都是 `POST /reload` 秒级生效。

## 配置

设置页（Settings → 小车 SSH）：主机/IP、用户名、端口、`ssh` 别名（填了优先用别名）、
附带的 `ssh` 参数，以及 VNC 主机/端口/通道/密码、文件浏览起始目录。
存在 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/settings.json`。

默认值取自这台机器上已有的 `~/.ssh/config`：`duzhong.local` / `duzhong` / 22 / `~/.ssh/id_rsa` 免密；
VNC 默认直连 5901（TigerVNC 在显示 `:1`）。

## HTTP API

前缀 `/api/dzrobot-ssh`，仅本机回环可访问。

| 方法 | 路径 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/status` | 配置、上次探测、小车信息、等价命令行、VNC 目标 |
| POST | `/probe[?car=0]` | 探测可达性与免密登录 |
| POST | `/describe` | 采集小车信息（用户/主机名/内核/运行时长） |
| GET/POST | `/config` | 读取 / 保存配置 |
| GET | `/files?path=` | 列目录（NUL+base64，名字里带空格/引号也不怕） |
| GET | `/file?path=` | 读文本（二进制会被识别出来而不是渲染成乱码） |
| GET | `/stat?path=` | 取大小/类型/时间 |
| GET | `/download?path=` | 流式下载 |
| POST | `/upload?path=` | 流式上传 |
| GET | `/novnc/*` | 本插件自带的 noVNC 静态资源（原生 ES 模块） |
| WS | `/vnc` | VNC 字节隧道（upgrade 座位） |
| GET/POST | `/reload` | 查看上次热重载 / 立即热重载 Host 半身 |
| GET/POST | `/diag` | 诊断日志（浏览器半身上报，落 `diag.jsonl`） |
| GET/POST | `/selftest` | 一次性自检开关 |

## 自检脚本

```bash
node scripts/check-ssh.mjs      # SSH 层：真实免密登录、描述
node scripts/check-files.mjs    # 文件层：列举/读取/二进制识别/奇怪文件名往返
node scripts/test-host.mjs      # Host 半身：全部路由 + noVNC 资源 + 真实 VNC 隧道握手
node scripts/test-client.mjs    # Client 半身：四个座位注册与渲染 + 完整连接流程
node scripts/probe-car.sh       # 小车侧勘察：VNC/桌面/监听端口（需要 ssh 到小车）
```

`test-host.mjs` 会真的握一次手：用 WebSocket 客户端发 `RFB 003.008`，要求收到小车 TigerVNC
回的版本横幅——这一步通了，就说明 upgrade、分帧、TCP 拨号、字节泵整条链路都是活的。

测试都用临时 `DSH_HOME`，**不会**动你真实的 `settings.json`。

## 关于自带的 noVNC

`novnc/` 是从 npm 上 `@novnc/novnc`（1.7.0）**原样**拷来的 `core/` 与 `vendor/`，未做任何修改，
因为浏览器半身是把它当原生 ES 模块直接 `import()` 的（56 个文件的依赖图由浏览器自己解析，
所以不需要打包步骤）。许可证 MPL-2.0，见 `novnc/LICENSE.txt`，升级时整目录替换即可。

## 排错

- **侧栏图标是红点**：小车不可达。确认它上电、连上同一 WiFi（本机与它同在 `192.168.43.x`），
  `ping duzhong.local`。
- **黄点 / "需要密码"**：能连上但免密不成立，把公钥装到小车：
  `ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub duzhong@duzhong.local`。
- **VNC 连不上**：先确认车上的 `vncserver@:1.service` 在跑（`systemctl status vncserver@:1`），
  端口是 **5901**（不是 5900）。若 VNC 只监听本地，把设置里的通道改成「走 SSH 隧道」。
- **面板点了没反应**：看 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/diag.jsonl`，每一步都有记录；
  也可以在设置页复制等价命令，直接在终端里粘贴。

**VNC 为什么要桥**：浏览器不能开裸 TCP 连到 5901，而小车上没有 websockify/noVNC。
所以 Host 半身做了两件事——在 `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` 注册一个 WebSocket upgrade 座位，
自己完成 RFC 6455 握手与分帧，然后把它和小车的 VNC 端口对接：

```
浏览器 noVNC  ──WebSocket──▶  /api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc  ──TCP──▶  小车 5901 (TigerVNC :1)
```

桥是纯字节泵，不解析 RFB 流：编码方式、扩展、未来协议版本都归 noVNC 管。

**文件为什么要用 ssh 而不是 SFTP**：Host 没有 SFTP 客户端库，而 `ssh` 已经装好、已经认证、
已经验证过能连上这台车。所以每个操作就是一条 `ssh …命令`，答案用机器可读的格式回传：
目录列表用 `find -printf` 的 NUL 分隔字段再 base64 包裹（`ls` 解析会在机器人项目真实存在的
奇怪文件名上崩掉——名字里有空格、引号也能原样往返，`scripts/check-files.mjs` 就在测这个），
读取用 `base64 -w0`，下载用 `cat` 流式吐，上传用 `cat >` 流式收。

**安全**：所有路由只接受本机回环；装了 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断。
文件名与路径在进入远程 shell 之前，只经过 `src/files.js` 的 `quote()` 一个收口点。

已经在 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop` 里注册好了：

| 改的是 | 生效方式 |
| --- | --- |

| 方法 | 路径 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/status` | 配置、上次探测、小车信息、等价命令行、VNC 目标 |

| GET/POST | `/config` | 读取 / 保存配置 |
| GET | `/files?path=` | 列目录（NUL+base64，名字里带空格/引号也不怕） |
| GET | `/file?path=` | 读文本（二进制会被识别出来而不是渲染成乱码） |
| GET | `/stat?path=` | 取大小/类型/时间 |
| GET | `/download?path=` | 流式下载 |
| POST | `/upload?path=` | 流式上传 |
| GET | `/novnc/*` | 本插件自带的 noVNC 静态资源（原生 ES 模块） |
| WS | `/vnc` | VNC 字节隧道（upgrade 座位） |
| GET/POST | `/reload` | 查看上次热重载 / 立即热重载 Host 半身 |
| GET/POST | `/diag` | 诊断日志（浏览器半身上报，落 `diag.jsonl`） |
| GET/POST | `/selftest` | 一次性自检开关 |

```bash
node scripts/check-files.mjs    # 文件层：列举/读取/二进制识别/奇怪文件名往返
```

# dsh-dzrobot-ssh

在 DeepSeek Harness 的**侧边栏一键 SSH 连上小车**（RK3588 / `duzhong.local`）。

点一下侧栏底部（Settings 旁边）的小车图标，插件会先探测小车是否可达、免密登录是否可用，

Tab 补全、Ctrl-C、窗口缩放、回滚缓冲全都是应用自带的那一套，不是另做一份仿制品。

## 为什么这样做

DSH 的终端服务在 Host 侧只允许用**已发现的 shell** 启动进程（`shellPath` 必须是
`subprocess.resolveExecutable` 能解析出来的候选 shell），所以插件不能直接把
`ssh` 当成一个 shell 塞进去。于是分成两半：

| 半身 | 负责 |
| --- | --- |
| Host (`index.js`) | 配置、探测（`ssh -o BatchMode=yes`）、小车信息、本地 JSON API |
| Client (`client.js`) | 侧栏按钮、设置页；打开终端标签页并把命令行写进去 |

交互式终端由 DSH 终端服务承载，插件只负责"打开 + 输入命令"，因此不重复实现终端。

关键取舍：探测路径一律带 `BatchMode=yes`。它关掉所有交互式提问，所以需要密码的小车会
**明确报"需要密码"**，而不是卡在一个看不见的提示符上。真正打开的交互式终端不带这个限制，
所以需要密码的小车照样能用——在终端里手输一次密码即可。

## 安装

已经在 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop` 里注册好了：

- `node_modules/dsh-dzrobot-ssh` → 指向本目录的 **junction**（改这里的代码立刻生效）
- `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里加了 `dsh-dzrobot-ssh`
- 这个包的 `cordis.patch.yml` 负责挂载 Host 半身；浏览器半身由 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client` 声明

Host 半身是热加载的（改完立刻生效）。**浏览器半身需要刷新页面**——页面的启动清单是在
加载时注入的，新插件不会自己出现在已经打开的页面上。

## 配置

默认值来自这台机器上已有的 `~/.ssh/config`：主机 `duzhong.local`、用户 `duzhong`、
端口 22、走 `~/.ssh/id_rsa` 免密。

设置页（Settings → 小车 SSH）可以改：主机/IP、用户名、端口、`ssh` 别名（填了优先用别名）、
附带的 `ssh` 参数。配置存在 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/settings.json`。

## HTTP API

前缀 `/api/dzrobot-ssh`（仅本机回环可访问；有 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断）。

| 方法 | 路径 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/status` | 配置、上次探测结果、小车信息、等价命令行 |

```bash
node scripts/test-host.mjs            # Host 半身：路由 + 真实探测 + 配置校验
```
