tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

1. 在 `client.js` 的 `TOOLS` 数组加一行 `{ id, kind, mode: 'tab', titleKey, descKey }`；

   `ctx.slots.inject('sidebar.right.pane.tab', ...)` 以 **类型 id 为 key** 注册标签体
   （`TabSlot` 按 `entryKey: definition.id` 分发，key 写错会渲染"类型不可用"占位）；
3. 字典里加两条文案。
右栏会经 `openContent → expanded → RightbarSeat syncPresentation → openRightbar` 自动展开，
无需自己开栏。VNC 标签设了 `keepMounted: true`——iframe 不随切换卸载，桌面不断线。

## 新架构：小车面板 = 工具列表

面板里原来的三个切换标签（VNC/终端/文件）撤掉了，改成**工具列表**——每个工具一行卡片（图标 + 名称 + 说明 + "打开"按钮），点打开就在**右栏开成标签页**（和你图2里的终端一模一样的窗口模式：可切换、可关闭、有自己的标签标题）。列表顶部写明："打开后主视图切到会话，工具窗口显示在会话右侧"。

## 三个工具的打开方式

| 工具 | 标签类型 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| SSH 终端 | 复用内置 `terminal` | 和现在一样：切到会话 → 右栏开终端 → 写入 ssh 命令 |
| 文件目录 | 新注册 `dzr-files` | 插件自有标签体，从 `/status` 自取配置渲染 |
| VNC 桌面 | 新注册 `dzr-vnc` | 同上；**`keepMounted: true`**——切走标签页 iframe 不卸载，桌面不断线 |

关键机制（都是从 DSH 源码确认的，不是猜的）：

- **标签体分发走 `entryKey: definition.id`**——槽 key 必须等于类型 id（`dsh-dzrobot-ssh/vnc`），写错会渲染"类型不可用"占位。测试里专门断言了这两个 key。
- **`multiple: false`** → 固定 contentId → 重复点"打开"**聚焦已有标签**，不会堆一排。
- **右栏自动展开**走内置链 `openContent → expanded → RightbarSeat syncPresentation → openRightbar`——面板不用自己开栏。
- **`ensureConversation`**（从原 `connect` 抽出）成为所有工具共用的"切回会话"逻辑，含失败时把面板切回去显示错误。

## 以后加新工具（你的核心诉求）

三步，在 [client.js](dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh/client.js) 里：

1. `TOOLS` 数组加一行 `{ id, kind, mode: 'tab', titleKey, descKey }`
2. `apply()` 里 `register()` 标签类型 + `inject()` 标签体（README 里写了完整步骤和容易踩的 key 坑）
3. 字典加两条文案

## 测试

Client 套件扩展了新断言：两个类型 id/kind/标志位正确、两个标签体 key 正确、`openToolTab('dzr-files')` 真的走了"切会话 → 开标签"路径、工具表恰好 3 行、4 个座位 + 2 个标签体全部渲染通过。Host/Files 套件不受影响，全过。

这次**只改了浏览器半身**，Host 没动——刷新页面就行。

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_list
tools.description: List every Cordis Inspect Provider currently known to the Host, including local Host Providers and the latest manifests synchronized from the Client. Each entry includes its platform, purpose, read-only methods, and input/output schemas. Call this Tool before writing or configuring a plugin, then select the provider and method for cordis_inspect_query from its result. Do not guess names or treat an Inspect method as a business Service that Plugin code can call.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_query
tools.description: Run a read-only query declared by an Inspect Provider. platform, provider, and method must come from cordis_inspect_list, and input must satisfy that method's schema. Use this Tool before writing plugin code to read exact Service methods, Event modes, plugin Config schemas, Tool schemas, theme tokens, or live Slot trees and props. Host queries run locally. A Client query waits for the first valid page response within the configured timeout; otherwise it reports a Client failure or asks you to reconnect and retry. This Tool cannot invoke business Service methods or modify the runtime.

platform.description: Runtime platform that owns the Provider.

provider.description: Exact Provider ID returned by cordis_inspect_list.

method.description: Exact method name declared by the Provider manifest.

input.description: Optional query input; it must satisfy the method input schema.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent

target.description: Teammate target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents.

tools.name: job_kill

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list

tools.name: job_output

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

## 直接回答：VNC 工具没坏，**是小车此刻不在线**

证据链（这轮诊断埋点之后，失败原因不再靠猜）：

**1. 车在线时，桥是通的** —— 就在这一轮开始时（19:29），我通过插件的 WS 端点拿到了车的真实横幅：

```
+31ms OPEN → MESSAGE 12B: "RFB 003.008\n"   ← 车的 TigerVNC 正常应答
```

**2. 失败时，桥自己说出了原因** —— 几分钟后同样的测试：

```
CLOSE code=1011 reason="无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）：connect timeout (240a:...)"
```

这是 Host 半身拨号失败后带出来的**服务端原话**：5 个解析出来的地址全部连接超时——不是黑名单、不是协议错、不是前端 bug，是**车够不着**。

**3. 旁证：整个 SSH 都断了** —— `ssh duzhong@duzhong.local` 报 `Unknown error`，随后轮询 **4 分多钟仍未回来**。你截图里 19:25 那 5 次 2ms 断开，就是当时 mDNS 解析直接失败的瞬间形态（DNS 负缓存 → 拨号立即失败 → 1011 关闭）。

这台车今天在这部手机热点上**反复掉线**，我全程都撞到过：mDNS 5 次查 3 次失败、IP 从 `192.168.43.17` 变成 `10.230.128.188`、多次 `car OFFLINE` 轮询。VNC 只是第一个被你按到的按钮，按 SSH 终端或文件目录，同一时刻也会失败。

## 这轮修的：让失败自己说话

以前你只看到笼统的"连接异常中断"，因为 noVNC 的 `disconnect` 事件**只带 `{clean}`，把关闭码和原因全丢了**。两处改动：

- **iframe 埋点**：包装 `WebSocket`，记录精确 URL 和 open/error/close 的 code+reason，连同文档地址随每次上报带出
- **面板**：断线时优先显示**桥的关闭原因**（1011 的中文原文），没原因则显示 `WebSocket code N`；diag 记录完整线证

现在你截图里那句话会直接变成类似"无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）：connect timeout"——**一眼能看出是车掉线还是插件问题**。

## 你需要做的

**刷新页面**（client 改动），等车回来后再点一次"连接桌面"。如果还失败，界面和 `diag.jsonl` 里会有关闭码+服务端原因，直接发我。

另外车侧反复掉线值得让**负责人那边**查一下：大概率是热点问题（信号/信道）或车的 WiFi 省电模式（`iw dev wlan0 get power_save`）——我这边 ssh 断着，查不了。

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_list
tools.description: List every Cordis Inspect Provider currently known to the Host, including local Host Providers and the latest manifests synchronized from the Client. Each entry includes its platform, purpose, read-only methods, and input/output schemas. Call this Tool before writing or configuring a plugin, then select the provider and method for cordis_inspect_query from its result. Do not guess names or treat an Inspect method as a business Service that Plugin code can call.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_query
tools.description: Run a read-only query declared by an Inspect Provider. platform, provider, and method must come from cordis_inspect_list, and input must satisfy that method's schema. Use this Tool before writing plugin code to read exact Service methods, Event modes, plugin Config schemas, Tool schemas, theme tokens, or live Slot trees and props. Host queries run locally. A Client query waits for the first valid page response within the configured timeout; otherwise it reports a Client failure or asks you to reconnect and retry. This Tool cannot invoke business Service methods or modify the runtime.

platform.description: Runtime platform that owns the Provider.

provider.description: Exact Provider ID returned by cordis_inspect_list.

method.description: Exact method name declared by the Provider manifest.

input.description: Optional query input; it must satisfy the method input schema.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt one teammate's current turn while preserving its pending inbox. Team Lead only.

target.description: Teammate target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the Lead and every durable teammate with an addressable target and current availability. inactive means no turn is executing, not a task result. provisioning and failed describe member creation.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: plugin_manager
tools.description: List plugins or bundles in the current profile, enable or disable them, install a bundle, or remove an installed bundle. Every action requires danger-full-access permission or approval for this call. Approval does not change the session permission mode. Changes affect every session in this profile. List first to obtain exact identifiers. Package installation can execute allowed build scripts. Live profiles apply changes immediately; startup profiles require restart. Incompatible DSH peer dependencies block installation and activation. Version exemptions risk crashes and data loss: warn the user and obtain explicit permission for the exact plugin and runtime versions before granting one.

target.description: Plugin entry id, bundle package name, or installation spec, according to action.

enabled.description: Required for set operations; defaults to true for installation. For set_version_exemption, true grants and false revokes.

runtimeVersion.description: For set_version_exemption: exact DSH version from list_version_exemptions. Target must be the manifest package-name@version, not an alias or version range.

acceptRisk.description: For granting an exemption: true only after warning the user about possible crashes and data loss and receiving explicit permission for this exact plugin/runtime pair. General installation permission is not enough.

approvedBuilds.description: For install_bundle: pass names from pendingBuilds only after the user explicitly approves running their install scripts in the conversation. This grants persistent permission for this profile.

registry.description: For install_bundle: the npm registry URL asked first, when the user names one; otherwise the configured registry is asked, and its configured fallbacks while a registry is unreachable.

offset.description: Zero-based list offset; defaults to 0.

limit.description: List page size, from 1 to 100; defaults to 25.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

Each entry includes its platform, purpose, read-only methods, and input/output schemas. Call this Tool before writing or configuring a plugin, then select the provider and method for cordis_inspect_query from its result. Do not guess names or treat an Inspect method as a business Service that Plugin code can call.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_query
tools.description: Run a read-only query declared by an Inspect Provider. platform, provider, and method must come from cordis_inspect_list, and input must satisfy that method's schema. Use this Tool before writing plugin code to read exact Service methods, Event modes, plugin Config schemas, Tool schemas, theme tokens, or live Slot trees and props. Host queries run locally. A Client query waits for the first valid page response within the configured timeout; otherwise it reports a Client failure or asks you to reconnect and retry. This Tool cannot invoke business Service methods or modify the runtime.

platform.description: Runtime platform that owns the Provider.

provider.description: Exact Provider ID returned by cordis_inspect_list.

method.description: Exact method name declared by the Provider manifest.

input.description: Optional query input; it must satisfy the method input schema.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt one teammate's current turn while preserving its pending inbox. Team Lead only.

target.description: Teammate target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the Lead and every durable teammate with an addressable target and current availability. inactive means no turn is executing, not a task result. provisioning and failed describe member creation.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: plugin_manager
tools.description: List plugins or bundles in the current profile, enable or disable them, install a bundle, or remove an installed bundle. Every action requires danger-full-access permission or approval for this call. Approval does not change the session permission mode. Changes affect every session in this profile. List first to obtain exact identifiers. Package installation can execute allowed build scripts. Live profiles apply changes immediately; startup profiles require restart. Incompatible DSH peer dependencies block installation and activation. Version exemptions risk crashes and data loss: warn the user and obtain explicit permission for the exact plugin and runtime versions before granting one.

target.description: Plugin entry id, bundle package name, or installation spec, according to action.

enabled.description: Required for set operations; defaults to true for installation. For set_version_exemption, true grants and false revokes.

runtimeVersion.description: For set_version_exemption: exact DSH version from list_version_exemptions. Target must be the manifest package-name@version, not an alias or version range.

acceptRisk.description: For granting an exemption: true only after warning the user about possible crashes and data loss and receiving explicit permission for this exact plugin/runtime pair. General installation permission is not enough.

approvedBuilds.description: For install_bundle: pass names from pendingBuilds only after the user explicitly approves running their install scripts in the conversation. This grants persistent permission for this profile.

registry.description: For install_bundle: the npm registry URL asked first, when the user names one; otherwise the configured registry is asked, and its configured fallbacks while a registry is unreachable.

offset.description: Zero-based list offset; defaults to 0.

limit.description: List page size, from 1 to 100; defaults to 25.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send one durable message to another Team member. A running target receives it at the nearest step boundary; an inactive target starts or resumes a turn.

target.description: Member target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents, including lead.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: spawn_teammate
tools.description: Create one named, durable teammate. Only the Team Lead may call this tool.

description.description: Short description of the delegated responsibility.

prompt.description: Complete initial task for the teammate.

context.description: fresh starts without Lead history; fork inherits completed Lead turns. Defaults to fresh.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: team_task_create
tools.description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

tools.name: team_task_get
tools.description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

tools.name: team_task_list
tools.description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

owner.description: Optional member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents, matching ownerName; use unowned for tasks without an owner.

limit.description: Number of rows, 1 through 100. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: team_task_update
tools.description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

description.description: Replacement details for edit.

blocked_by.description: Complete blocker list for set_dependencies.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents for Lead-only reassign; omit to unassign.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, mailbox, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Build a DSH plugin, in sidebar, that SSH-connects to the robot car (RK3588, `duzhong.local`, user `duzhong`); later expanded to a full car panel with three switchable views: VNC desktop, terminal, and file directory. Chinese-language user; respond in Chinese.
- User answered a question with "你不能和负责人形成一个智能体团队吗" — clarified: cannot connect to another DSH conversation window; detected the car was already reachable instead.
- VNC password: user said "小车的密码是duzhong" (verified: `duzhong` is Linux/sudo password, but VNC password file stores a different value; plugin defaults to prompting).
- VNC resolution: user first asked "vnc的桌面分辨率设置为720p" (720p), then later pasted `vncserver -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no :1` / `sudo ufw allow 5901/tcp` / `vncserver -kill` / restart and, via question, chose "重启并改成 1920x1080" — 1080p is now the persisted resolution.
- Latest request (in progress): fix SSH terminal view ("这个ssh终端也用不了，点开之后在右边是一片空白") — click shows blank right side; root cause identified, fix written but not yet verified/committed.

## Key Technical Concepts
- DSH = DeepSeek Harness; plugin structure: `package.json` (`dsh.bundle.patch`, `dsh.client` web), `cordis.patch.yml` (insert entry `dzrobot-ssh`), Host half `index.js` (ESM, exports `apply`/`inject`/`name`), Client half `client.js` (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`, `require('react')`, exports `apply`/`inject`/`name`/`__test`).
- Profile: `C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\profiles\desktop` — junction `node_modules\dsh-dzrobot-ssh` → `D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05\dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh`; `package.json` `dsh.profile.bundles` + dependency `"dsh-dzrobot-ssh": "file:D:/User/Desktop/dzrobot_v10.05/dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh"`.
- Client slots: `sidebar.panellist` (id `dzrobot-car`) + `main` (key `dzrobot-car`) = panel icon + central panel; `settings.section` id `dzrobot-ssh`. Removed earlier `sidebar.footer.action` button per user request ("把这个按钮给去掉吧").
- Terminal is Session-owned: `webTerminals.view(sessionId, key, contentId)` + `sidebarRight.commandTarget(element)` → `openTabFromTarget('terminal', target)` → `view.write(command + '\r')`. `commandTarget` reads `screen()` = `mounted` (on-screen Session) + adopted surface.
- **Root cause of terminal bug**: `sb-right-client.js` line 9062 `show(activePanelId === null ? selected?.sessionId : void 0)` — on-screen Session only exists when Conversation is the active main panel (`activePanelId === null`). While `dzrobot-car` panel active → `screen()` undefined → `commandTarget` undefined → `no-session`. `layout.selectPanel(null)` returns to Conversation (ui-layout line 118, 462-466).
- VNC: page runs under custom `dsh-app://` scheme — `import()` of noVNC fails there ("Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: dsh-app://app/api/..."), `location.host` = "app". Fixed via separate `vnc-app.html` served over http, embedded in iframe, postMessage protocol (`source: 'dzrobot-panel'`/`'dzrobot-vnc'`, types: connect/connected/credentials/disconnected/failed/cad/ready/password/credentials-sent). Origin from `req.socket.localPort` → `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.
- VNC WebSocket bridge: `webServer.registerUpgrade({path:'/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc'})` hands raw TCP socket; plugin implements RFC6455 handshake (`src/ws.js` `acceptUpgrade`/`WebSocketChannel`) + byte pump to car 5901 (`src/vnc.js` `VncBridge`). noVNC 1.7.0 vendored verbatim at `novnc/` (MPL-2.0), served as ES modules.
- IPv4-first dial (fix for TigerVNC blacklist): `dialOrdered()` sorts DNS candidates IPv4-first; blacklist entries were all IPv6 (Windows temporary IPv6 rotates).
- TigerVNC blacklist: per-source-address, abandoned/unauth connection counts; `-BlacklistThreshold`/`-BlacklistTimeout` (default=10); cleared by VNC restart. `test-host.mjs` uses a local TCP stand-in to avoid probing the car (opt-in `DZR_TEST_CAR_VNC=1`).
- File browsing via `ssh` + `find -printf` NUL/base64 framing (`src/files.js`); `-L` dereferences symlinks (fixed `%s` size bug on symlinks).
- Self hot-reload: `src/reload.js` (`selfReload`, `POST /api/dzrobot-ssh/reload`) — evicts ESM cache, re-imports, re-registers; works (`{"ok":true,"fibers":1,"evicted":8,"busted":false}`).
- Node: `C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe` (v24). pwsh tool intermittently rejects `timeoutMs` ("invalid arguments: timeoutMs must be a number") and PowerShell→ssh heredocs/`$(...)`/`$L`/`$r[0]` get mangled; reliable pattern = normalize `.sh` to LF then `scp` + `bash file`.

## Files and Code
- `D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05\dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh\package.json` — name `dsh-dzrobot-ssh`, version `0.2.0`, `type: module`, exports `./index.js`/`./client`/`./locale/*.json`, `dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — `- insert: - id: dzrobot-ssh, name: 'dsh-dzrobot-ssh', config: {}`.
- `index.js` (Host half) — imports store/ssh/trust/reload/vnc/ws/files; routes `/status`(now returns `origin`), `/probe`, `/describe`, `/config`, `/files`, `/file`, `/stat`, `/download`, `/upload`, `/vnc.html`, `/novnc/*`, `/reload`, `/diag`, `/selftest`, `/graph`; `registerUpgrade('/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc')`; `openVncTunnel(req, socket, head, settings, {logger})`; `requestOrigin(req)` from `req.socket.localPort`; `serveFile`/`serveNovnc` (novnc adds `access-control-allow-origin: *`).
- `client.js` (Client half) — `PANEL_ID='dzrobot-car'`; `connect(ctx, element, onPhase)` + `openInTerminal(...)`; `makeVncView` (iframe + postMessage, phase machine idle/connecting/auth/connected/disconnected/failed, status pill, hero card overlay), `makeFilesView`, `makeCarPanel`, `makeSettingsPage`, `CarGlyph`; DICT zh/en. **Latest edit**: `connect()` now, when `target===undefined`, checks `ctx.get('uiSession')?.adapter?.current?.getSnapshot?.().key` for `hasSession`, requires `layout.selectPanel`, calls `layout.selectPanel(null)`, polls `settings.commandTarget()` up to 20×100ms, then `openInTerminal`; no longer calls `openRightbar` (was causing blank right column).
- `src/vnc.js` — `dialOrdered(targetHost, targetPort, {timeoutMs, signal})` IPv4-first; `VncBridge` class; `vncTarget()`; `normalize()` reads vncHost/vncPort/vncMode/ssh fields.
- `src/ws.js` — RFC6455 `acceptUpgrade(req,socket)`, `WebSocketChannel(socket, protocol, head)` with `send/onMessage/onClose/close`, frame encode/decode incl. 7/16/64-bit lengths, masking.
- `src/files.js` — `listDirectory`, `statPath` (uses `find -L ... -printf '%y\0%s\0%T@\0'`), `readTextFile` (NUL + UTF-8/control-char binary detection), `downloadFile`, `uploadFile` (watchdog timeouts), `quote()`, `remoteArgv()`, `FAILURES` friendly error map.
- `src/store.js` — `SETTINGS_INITIAL` (host duzhong.local, port 22, user duzhong, sshAlias '', vncHost '', vncPort 5901, vncMode direct, vncPassword '', filesRoot /home/duzhong), `JsonStore`, `sanitize()`.
- `src/trust.js` — `rejectionFor(req, connection)`, `isLoopback`.
- `src/reload.js` — `selfReload(ctx, options)`, `purgeCaches`, `packageCacheKeys`, `watchPackage`.
- `vnc-app.html` — standalone VNC doc; `embedded = window.parent !== window`; chromeless stage (removed top bar); password ask only when NOT embedded; report('failed',{kind:'security'|'start'}); securityfailure sets `blacklisted` flag.
- `scripts/` — `check-ssh.mjs`, `check-files.mjs`, `test-host.mjs` (stand-in WS bridge test, 70300-byte byte-for-byte across frame lengths, `/vnc.html` + origin + cross-origin assertions), `test-client.mjs` (renders 4+ slots/views; `__test` seam; asserts connect flow), `test-live-ws.mjs` (probes live `ws://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc`), `debug-files.mjs`, `restart-vnc-1080p.sh`, `check-vnc-suggestion.sh`, `vnc-log-families.sh`, `vnc-log-1617b.sh`, `probe-car.sh`, `probe-vnc-config.sh`.
- `README.md` — updated for 1080p, `-localhost no` already on, ufw inactive, VNC password separate, blacklist behavior, hot-reload, dsh-app:// iframe rationale.
- Car files changed: `/etc/systemd/system/vncserver@:1.service` `ExecStart=/usr/bin/vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24`; `~/.vnc/config` `geometry=1920x1080`, `localhost=no`; ufw rule 5901/tcp exists (ufw inactive).

## Errors and Fixes
- `screen()`/`commandTarget` returns undefined while plugin panel active → terminal "no-session" + blank right side. Previous fix (call `openRightbar(true,false)` then retry) was WRONG — opened empty right column (white blank) but `screen()` still undefined. Correct fix: `layout.selectPanel(null)` → poll `commandTarget()`; pre-check `uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot().key` for `hasSession`. (Just written to client.js, NOT yet re-run/tested.)

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

So the banner gate would run on EVERY connection, not just cached ones. That's actually fine/safe but adds a small latency. Actually it's arguably good — always verify. But the comment says "cached address can belong to something else". Let me be precise: run the gate whenever the address came from the cache. Let me track that properly with a flag.

Actually, simplest and most robust: always verify the banner. But that adds a delay for every normal connection and complicates data flow (buffering). Hmm, but actually the banner check has a subtle problem: if data arrives in the same chunk as other data... no, banner is first.

But there's a real issue: if I gate always, then for the normal path the socket 'data' handler registered earlier (this.#onData?.(chunk)) will ALSO receive the banner chunk! Because socket.on('data', chunk => this.#onData?.(chunk)) was registered before #awaitBanner. So the banner would be forwarded to the browser twice — once by the general handler and once... no wait, #awaitBanner doesn't forward; it only reads. But the general handler already forwarded the banner to the browser. So the gate is meaningless — bytes already leaked.

This is a critical ordering bug. I must register the banner gate's own listener BEFORE the forwarding handler, and buffer. Better approach: do the banner check on the *probe socket* before wiring up forwarding — but the probe socket is the same socket.

Cleanest: gate before installing the forwarding handler. So:
1. dial → socket
2. if address is a cached literal → await banner (no forwarding handler installed yet)
3. then install socket.on('data', ...)

That way no bytes leak. Let me restructure. And to keep it simple + safe, I'll verify the banner for cached addresses only (that's the actual risk), and pass a flag from dialOrdered indicating "this address came from cache".

/**
 * The cached-address guard.
 *
 * `dialOrdered` remembers the address that answered, so an mDNS flake degrades to
 * "use what worked" instead of "give up". This car roams between networks
 * (observed: 192.168.43.17 and 10.230.128.188 on one day), so a cached address
 * can name a *different* host once the car moves. The bridge pumps raw desktop
 * bytes, so it must not forward a single one to a peer that fails the RFB banner
 * check — and a failed check must retire the cache entry.
 *
 * The cache is keyed by host and private to `src/vnc.js`, so every case primes
 * it the only way the product can: a real successful dial first, then a dial
 * against a name that cannot resolve (`*.invalid`), which is what sends
 * `dialOrdered` down the cache branch.
 *
 * Run: node scripts/test-vnc-guard.mjs
 */

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Build a DSH plugin, in sidebar, that SSH-connects to the robot car (RK3588, `duzhong.local`, user `duzhong`); expanded to a car panel with VNC desktop, terminal, and file directory views. Chinese-language user; **respond in Chinese**.
- VNC resolution: user chose "重启并改成 1920x1080" —1080p persisted (`vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24`).
- Fixed SSH terminal bug (blank right column) — completed and verified.
- Latest completed request: "点开图1左侧的小车后，把里面做成一个工具列表的模式吧，原本里面的文件管理啊，ssh终端啊，vnc界面啊，都做成图2这种右侧的页面窗口模式，这样我也能更好地调试修改，以后也方便加别的工具" — **DONE** (tool list panel + right-column tab types).

## Key Technical Concepts

- Profile: `C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\profiles\desktop`; junction `node_modules\dsh-dzrobot-ssh` → `D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05\dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh`.
- **Right-column tab architecture (verified in `sb-right-client.js`)**: slot key for a tab body = `definition.id` (`TabSlot` line 5550: `entryKey: definition?.id ?? tab.kind`); `placeTab` (6451) uses `pageAddress(kind)` = `sidebar://${kind}` when `multiple !== true` (second click focuses existing tab); right column auto-reveals via `openContent → expanded → RightbarSeat syncPresentation → openRightbar`; `keepMounted: true` keeps body mounted.
- `SidebarRightTabRegistry` at line 8665; `register(definition)` requires `{id, kind, priority?, multiple?, keepMounted?, title}`; service id `sidebarRightTabs` on client ctx.
- Right column belongs to Conversation only: `show(activePanelId === null ? selected?.sessionId : undefined)` → `commandTarget` undefined while plugin panel active → `layout.selectPanel(null)` required.
- VNC: custom `dsh-app://` scheme breaks `import()` of noVNC → served over http via `vnc-app.html` iframe + postMessage (`source: 'dzrobot-panel'`/`'dzrobot-vnc'`). noVNC 1.7.0 vendored at `novnc/` (MPL-2.0).
- Host WS bridge: `webServer.registerUpgrade({path:'/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc'})` + hand-written RFC6455 (`src/ws.js`) + byte pump (`src/vnc.js` `VncBridge`).

- noVNC `disconnect` CustomEvent detail = `{ clean: this._rfbCleanDisconnect }` only (rfb.js line 944-945) — **no close code forwarded**; `websock.js` lines 284-293 only Log the close event.
- Self hot-reload: `POST /api/dzrobot-ssh/reload`.
- Node: `C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\dsh-runtimes\dsh-primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe`. pwsh tool intermittently rejects `timeoutMs`; PowerShell→ssh quoting mangling → write `.sh`, normalize CRLF, `scp` + `bash`.

- `dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh\client.js` (~1540 lines) — **new tool-list architecture**:
  - `ensureConversation(ctx, element, step)` — shared switch-to-Conversation + poll `commandTarget` (20×100ms), restores previous panel on failure. Returns target or undefined.
  - `openToolTab(ctx, kind, element)` — `ensureConversation` → `settings.openTab(kind)`.

  - `makeVncTabShell` / `makeFilesTabShell` — self-fetch `/status`, wrap in `.dzr_tabroot`.
  - `makeCarPanel` — tool list rows (`.dzr_toolrow`, `.dzr_toolglyph`, `.dzr_toolinfo`, `.dzr_tooltitle`, `.dzr_tooldesc`), `ToolGlyph` SVG set, `explain(result)`.
  - `apply()` registers: `sidebar.panellist`, `main` (key `dzrobot-car`), `settings.section`, plus `sidebarRightTabs.register({id:'dsh-dzrobot-ssh/vnc', kind:'dzr-vnc', multiple:false, keepMounted:true, title})`, same for `dsh-dzrobot-ssh/files`, and two `ctx.slots.inject('sidebar.right.pane.tab', ...)` keyed by those ids.
  - `inject = ['slots','locale','sidebarRight','webTerminals','sidebarRightTabs']`
  - VNC `disconnected` handling: `userStopped` ref distinguishes explicit 断开 (→ idle, no error) from unexpected drop (→ `vncDropped` message); `connect()` resets flag.
  - New dict keys (zh+en): `toolOpen`, `toolNote`, `filesToolDesc`, `vncToolDesc`, `vncDropped`.
  - `__test` exports: `connect, ensureConversation, openToolTab, waitFor, describeService, surveyServices, DICT, STATE_KEY, TOOLS, makeVncView, makeFilesView, makeCarPanel, makeVncTabShell, makeFilesTabShell`.
- `dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh\src\vnc.js` — `dialOrdered()` with `lastGoodAddress` Map + `ADDRESS_CACHE_TTL_MS = 10*60_000`; caches only literal addresses that completed TCP connect; on DNS failure candidates = `[cached.address, targetHost]`.
