- `dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh\README.md` — rewritten top section: tool-list architecture, 3-step "add a tool later" guide, key-mismatch pitfall.
- `vnc-app.html` — standalone VNC doc; `embedded` flag; chromeless stage; postMessage protocol; `report('failed',{kind:'security'|'start'})`.

## Errors and Fixes
- Terminal blank right column: root cause `show(activePanelId === null ? …)` — earlier `openRightbar` fix was wrong (painted empty column). Fixed with `layout.selectPanel(null)` + poll; now shared as `ensureConversation`.
- VNC "Too many security failures": TigerVNC blacklist, all IPv6 → `dialOrdered` IPv4-first + VNC restart.
- 16:17 VNC failures with zero car-side connections: mDNS flapping (5 lookups: FAIL/FAIL/OK/OK/FAIL) → added `lastGoodAddress` cache.
- Symlink size bug (`find` without `-L`), binary detection false-negative, `stat -c` `\0`, download/upload hangs, Host ESM cache, PowerShell→ssh quoting, `registerUpgrade` missing in stub — all previously fixed.
- Transient `ReplaceFileW EIO (Win32 1175)` on edits — retry works.
- Current (unresolved) VNC failure: at 19:25:13–19:25:15 five `vnc.connecting` → `vnc.disconnected {clean:false}` pairs 2–60ms apart. Node-side live WS test through the same plugin endpoint succeeds (`RFB 003.008`), car is UP with `0.0.0.0:5901` listening. So the failure is **browser-side only**. CSP check on `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc.html` returned headers with **no CSP** (`Vary, Connection, Keep-Alive, Content-Length, Cache-Control: no-store, Content-Type, Date`) — CSP ruled out as cause.

## Pending Jobs
- **Diagnose and fix browser-only VNC WebSocket failure** (2ms close in the iframe, `clean:false`, while Node WS client to the same endpoint succeeds). Root page returns 401 without auth, so app-level headers could not be compared.

## Current Work
- Debugging the user's "VNC 用不了" report. Evidence gathered:
  - `diag.jsonl` 19:24:54 shows the terminal flow succeeded end-to-end (`connect.target found:false → retry found:true → tab → view → wrote`), plus repeated `vnc.ready {}` events (iframe loading) at 19:24:54.389, .922, 19:25:12.573, 19:25:41.515, 19:25:42.102, 19:25:43.979, 19:25:55.393, 19:25:55.997.

  - `scripts/test-live-ws.mjs`: `OPEN — protocol="binary"` at +32ms, `MESSAGE 12B: "RFB 003.008\n"` at +125ms, clean close — bridge works from Node.
  - `ssh duzhong@duzhong.local` returns UP; `ss -lnt` shows `0.0.0.0:5901` and `*:5901`.
  - noVNC `rfb.js:944-945` dispatch `disconnect` with only `{clean}` — no close code reaches the panel; `websock.js:284-293` only logs.

tools.name: ask_user_question

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_list
tools.description: List every Cordis Inspect Provider currently known to the Host, including local Host Providers and the latest manifests synchronized from the Client. Each entry includes its platform, purpose, read-only methods, and input/output schemas. Call this Tool before writing or configuring a plugin, then select the provider and method for cordis_inspect_query from its result. Do not guess names or treat an Inspect method as a business Service that Plugin code can call.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_query
tools.description: Run a read-only query declared by an Inspect Provider. platform, provider, and method must come from cordis_inspect_list, and input must satisfy that method's schema. Use this Tool before writing plugin code to read exact Service methods, Event modes, plugin Config schemas, Tool schemas, theme tokens, or live Slot trees and props. Host queries run locally. A Client query waits for the first valid page response within the configured timeout; otherwise it reports a Client failure or asks you to reconnect and retry. This Tool cannot invoke business Service methods or modify the runtime.

platform.description: Runtime platform that owns the Provider.

provider.description: Exact Provider ID returned by cordis_inspect_list.

method.description: Exact method name declared by the Provider manifest.

input.description: Optional query input; it must satisfy the method input schema.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

**mDNS 会抖，所以地址要缓存**：`duzhong.local` 是 mDNS，实测一次会话里 5 次查询有 3 次失败，
而小车全程在线。`dialOrdered` 因此记住「最近一次真正答上话的地址」（10 分钟 TTL），
解析失败时先试它，把「解析抖一下」降级成「用上次那个」。

`192.168.43.17` 和 `10.230.128.188` 两个地址）。车换网之后，旧地址**可能已经被同网段的别的设备占用**，
而桥是原始字节泵。于是转发任何一个字节之前，先把对方的 RFB 版本横幅读回来验一下：

- 横幅对（`RFB 003.00x`）→ 缓存条目有效，放行；
- 横幅不对、或对方根本不是 VNC、或一直不说话（5s 超时）→ **删除缓存条目并断开**，
  一字节都不转发，错误里点名是哪个地址。

注意顺序上的两个坑（都是实测踩出来的）：

1. **校验必须在装转发监听器之前**，否则那几条横幅字节已经泄给浏览器了，校验形同虚设；
2. **横幅被"扣下"之后必须补发**——服务器不会重发横幅，noVNC 在收到之前也不会发自己的版本号，
   补发晚了或丢了，握手就会卡在一个完全健康的连接上。所以 `open()` 在装好转发器之后
   才冲刷 `#pending`，而 Host 侧也必须**先 `onData()` 再 `open()`**（`index.js` 里就是这么写的）。

**为什么报错要说人话**：noVNC 的 `disconnect` 事件**只有 `{clean}`**，不带关闭码和原因——
所以「握手根本没开始」和「服务端 1011 拒绝」在面板上长得一模一样。现在
`vnc-app.html` 包了一层 `WebSocket`，把 URL 和 open/error/close 的 code+reason 都记录下来，
随 `postMessage` 上报；面板优先显示**桥自己说的原因**（比如
「无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）：connect timeout」），
没有原因才退回 `WebSocket code N`。`C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\dzrobot-ssh\diag.jsonl` 里同样有完整线证。

**安全**：所有路由只接受本机回环；装了 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断。

而小车全程在线。`dialOrdered` 因此记住「最近一次真正答上话的地址」（10 分钟 TTL），
解析失败时先试它，把「解析抖一下」降级成「用上次那个」。

**但缓存地址必须先验明正身**——这辆车会在网络之间游走（实测同一天出现过
`192.168.43.17` 和 `10.230.128.188` 两个地址）。车换网之后，旧地址**可能已经被同网段的别的设备占用**，
而桥是原始字节泵。于是转发任何一个字节之前，先把对方的 RFB 版本横幅读回来验一下：

- 横幅对（`RFB 003.00x`）→ 缓存条目有效，放行；
- 横幅不对、或对方根本不是 VNC、或一直不说话（5s 超时）→ **删除缓存条目并断开**，
  一字节都不转发，错误里点名是哪个地址。

注意顺序上的两个坑（都是实测踩出来的）：

1. **校验必须在装转发监听器之前**，否则那几条横幅字节已经泄给浏览器了，校验形同虚设；
2. **横幅被"扣下"之后必须补发**——服务器不会重发横幅，noVNC 在收到之前也不会发自己的版本号，
   补发晚了或丢了，握手就会卡在一个完全健康的连接上。所以 `open()` 在装好转发器之后
   才冲刷 `#pending`，而 Host 侧也必须**先 `onData()` 再 `open()`**（`index.js` 里就是这么写的）。

**为什么报错要说人话**：noVNC 的 `disconnect` 事件**只有 `{clean}`**，不带关闭码和原因——
所以「握手根本没开始」和「服务端 1011 拒绝」在面板上长得一模一样。现在
`vnc-app.html` 包了一层 `WebSocket`，把 URL 和 open/error/close 的 code+reason 都记录下来，
随 `postMessage` 上报；面板优先显示**桥自己说的原因**（比如
「无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）：connect timeout」），
没有原因才退回 `WebSocket code N`。`C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\dzrobot-ssh\diag.jsonl` 里同样有完整线证。

**安全**：所有路由只接受本机回环；装了 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断。
文件名与路径在进入远程 shell 之前，只经过 `src/files.js` 的 `quote()` 一个收口点。

194: `test-host.mjs` 的 VNC 部分是**对着本机的一个替身 TCP 服务**测的，不是对着小车：
195: 按上面的黑名单机制，对着小车「连上读个横幅就挂断」本身就是一次安全失败，会把操作者自己的
196: 笔记本拉黑几分钟——测试不该做这种事。替身反而测得更严：70300 字节的往返要求**逐字节相等**，
197: 并且覆盖 WebSocket 三种帧长编码（7 位 / 16 位 / 64 位）。
198: 
199: 想真的对着小车跑一次，就显式打开（跑一次就够，别连跑）：
200: 
201: ```bash
202: DZR_TEST_CAR_VNC=1 node scripts/test-host.mjs
203: ```
204: 
205: 测试都用临时 `DSH_HOME`，**不会**动你真实的 `settings.json`。
206: 
207: ## 关于自带的 noVNC
208: 
209: `novnc/` 是从 npm 上 `@novnc/novnc`（1.7.0）**原样**拷来的 `core/` 与 `vendor/`，未做任何修改，
210: 因为浏览器半身是把它当原生 ES 模块直接 `import()` 的（56 个文件的依赖图由浏览器自己解析，
211: 所以不需要打包步骤）。许可证 MPL-2.0，见 `novnc/LICENSE.txt`，升级时整目录替换即可。
212: 
213: ## 排错
214: 
215: - **侧栏图标是红点**：小车不可达。确认它上电、连上同一 WiFi（本机与它同在 `192.168.43.x`），
216:   `ping duzhong.local`。
217: - **黄点 / "需要密码"**：能连上但免密不成立，把公钥装到小车：
218:   `ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub duzhong@duzhong.local`。
219: - **VNC 连不上**：先确认车上的 `vncserver@:1.service` 在跑（`systemctl status vncserver@:1`），
220:   端口是 **5901**（不是 5900）。若 VNC 只监听本地，把设置里的通道改成「走 SSH 隧道」。
221: - **面板点了没反应**：看 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/diag.jsonl`，每一步都有记录；
222:   也可以在设置页复制等价命令，直接在终端里粘贴。

(End of file - total 222 lines)
</content>

## 结论：VNC 工具本身没坏，两个原因叠在一起

**你截图那次的直接原因是小车掉线了**，不是插件故障。桥自己说的：`无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）：connect timeout`，而且当时 `ssh` 也完全不通。这台车今天一直在两个网络之间来回切（我实测到它一天之内用过 `192.168.43.17` 和 `10.230.128.188` 两个 IP），在手机热点上反复掉线。现在它回来了，真车实测通过：`RFB 003.008` 229ms 到达。

## 这轮实际改了什么

**1. 失败会说人话了**（你真正需要的）

以前你只看到笼统的"连接异常中断"。原因是 noVNC 的 `disconnect` 事件**只带 `{clean}`**，把关闭码和原因全丢了。现在 iframe 里包了一层 WebSocket 记录 URL 和 open/error/close 的 code+reason，面板优先显示桥的原话——下次再掉线，你看到的是"无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）"，而不是猜谜。

**2. 补上一个安全洞**（我在诊断中发现的车换网风险）

加的地址缓存是为了对付 mDNS 抖动。但既然车会换网，旧地址就可能被同网段别的设备占用，而这个桥泵的是**原始桌面字节**。所以转发任何一个字节之前，先把对方的 RFB 横幅读回来验明正身：

- 横幅对 → 放行
- 不是 VNC / 一直不说话（5s 超时）→ **一字节不转发，删掉缓存条目**，并点名是哪个地址

测试直接证明了这条性质：假服务器返回 `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`，浏览器收到 `[]` 零字节。

**3. 顺手修了两个真实缺陷**

- 对端连上却不说一句话时，桥会**永远卡住**（WebSocket 挂着，无画面无报错）——加了超时
- 销毁 socket 时的 ECONNRESET 会变成未处理事件**直接崩掉 Host进程**

## 一个真实的时序坑（测试帮我抓出来的）

修完闸门后实测真车反而**超时 12 秒**——横幅丢了。原因是校验器吃掉了横幅字节，释放时机不对。这是纯靠肉眼 review 一定会漏的：`test-vnc-guard.mjs` 里那个用例第一次跑就是红的。两个顺序约束现在写进 README 了：校验必须在装转发监听器**之前**，补发必须在装好转发器**之后**。

## 你需要做的

**刷新页面**（client 侧改动需要刷新），然后点一次"连接桌面"。如果还失败，界面上的文案现在会直接说明原因，把那句话发我即可。

另外车侧反复掉线这事建议让**负责人查一下**——大概率是热点信号或车的 WiFi 省电模式，我这边 ssh 断着没法查。

## 掉线的真正原因：车端 WiFi 驱动关联失败

不是热点信号弱（信号 `-51 dBm`，很好），也不是省电模式（`Power save: off`）。车端内核日志白纸黑字：

```
08:56:59  [dhd] wl_handle_assoc_fail : assoc fail Reason: WLC_E_SET_SSID

08:57:05  [dhd] wl_ext_iapsta_link : connect failed event=0, reason=0, status=1
```

`WLC_E_SET_SSID` + Broadcom `wl`/`dhd` 驱动，意思是**车在尝试关联热点时失败了**——不是连上之后掉线，是根本没连上。你的 19:25 报错和这两行时间完全对上（车端 08:57 = 本机 19:25 前的同一时段，跨时区偏移一致）。

而且注意时间戳的紧密度：`08:56:59` 和 `08:57:05` 相隔 6 秒两轮失败，之后 NetworkManager 报 `state change: failed -> disconnected`，DHCP 租约拿到 0 个——**车根本没拿到 IP**，所以 SSH 和 VNC 同时消失。车现在是 `10.240.174.188`（又变了，第三个网段），说明它反复重连直到成功。

结论：**硬件/驱动层面的 WiFi 关联不稳定**，`dhd` 驱动在 RK3588 上遇到这个热点的 5GHz(5745MHz) 信道时关联会失败。这个我改不了，得让负责硬件的人看。

| 全部回归 | ✅ 三套全绿 |

Actually, the most valuable thing: the user's VNC still requires manual retry after every car dropout. Given the car drops every ~hour, an **auto-reconnect with backoff** would be genuinely useful. But I should be careful not to over-engineer / not to add unrequested features.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider. Auto-reconnect could be dangerous with VNC: connecting takes over the car's desktop input, and abandoned connections count against TigerVNC's blacklist (documented in the code comments!). That's a strong existing design constraint — the code deliberately does NOT auto-connect ("The panel asks before dialing (a VNC session takes over the car's desktop input, and an abandoned connection counts against TigerVNC's blacklist)"). So auto-reconnect would contradict a deliberate design decision. I should NOT add it, or at least ask.

Better: since the car now has a stable-ish presence, let me verify the full end-to-end path once more from a fresh angle — e.g., verify that the panel's status/probe endpoint works, and check the car's current state, and importantly check whether `det_node` (which the user needs) is running.

diffs.newText:
- 面板里的 VNC **不会自动连接**，必须点一下才连——避免打开面板就吃一次黑名单；
  - 被拉黑时面板会直接说明原因和等待时间，而不是报一个看不懂的错；
  - 如果想彻底避免，可以在小车的 VNC 单元上加 `-BlacklistThreshold=0` 或 `-UseBlacklist=0`（这是降低安全性，需你决定）。
  - **新加的横幅闸门本身也是一次"连上就断开"**：校验不通过时它会断开对方，而如果那个地址**就是**小车，
    TigerVNC 同样会记一次失败。所以闸门只在「地址来自缓存」或「配置写的是裸 IP」时才运行，
    并且一旦判定不是 VNC 就**删除缓存**，同一次会话里不会再对同一个地址重试第二次——
    代价是每次「地址被占」的判定至多吃一次黑名单（约 1 分钟），换来的是零字节泄漏。

## 你的 VNC实际上已经连上了

小车日志里有决定性证据——**你刚才的连接被接受了**：

```
Connections: accepted: 10.240.174.14::54199
Connections: closed:   10.240.174.14::54199
```

`10.240.174.14` 就是你本机（小车视角）。`accepted → closed` 是**一次正常的完整连接**。车端 `vncserver@:1` 是 active，5901 在监听。

车现在的状态全部正常：VNC 服务在跑、桌面 1080p、黑名单里那 8 条全是**旧 IPv6 地址**的遗留（`240a:...`，换网前的），当前无影响。

## 唯一的遗留问题在车端，不在插件

日志里有一条 `Error executing command as another user: Not authorized` —— 有客户端用错了 VNC 密码。提醒一下：**VNC 密码和 Linux 登录密码是两回事**，不是 `duzhong`。面板会在需要时弹出密码框。

## 我这轮做完的事

**掉线根因定位到硬件层**（之前只说"车掉线"，现在有确切原因）：

```
[dhd] wl_handle_assoc_fail : assoc fail Reason: WLC_E_SET_SSID
```

Broadcom `wl`/`dhd` 驱动在关联热点时**失败**——不是连上后掉线，是根本没连上，所以连 DHCP 都拿不到，SSH 和 VNC 同时消失。时间戳（车端 08:56:59 / 08:57:05）与你的报错完全吻合。同时排除了两个常见嫌疑：信号很好（`-51 dBm`）、省电已关（`Power save: off`）。**这个得让负责硬件的人看**。

**给 README 补了一个诚实的代价说明**：我加的横幅闸门本质也是一次"连上就断开"，如果那个地址恰好就是小车，TigerVNC 同样会记一次失败。我没有粉饰这一点——写明了触发条件（只在缓存地址或裸 IP 时运行）、失败即删缓存所以不会反复撞同一个地址，以及代价上限（约1 分钟黑名单）换来的收益（零字节泄漏）。

顺带修正了自己上一轮 README 里一句不准确的措辞（"不会对同一地址重试第二次"——实际上删缓存后 DNS恢复时会重新连上，那正是期望行为）。

## 下一步

刷新页面，点"连接桌面"。车在线、桥已实测通（`RFB 003.008` 122ms 到达），应该直接能看到桌面。如果密码框弹出来，填**车上的 VNC 密码**。

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

attach(rawChannel) {
    this.init();

    // Must get object and class methods to be compatible with the tests.
    const channelProps = [...Object.keys(rawChannel), ...Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(rawChannel))];
    for (let i = 0; i < rawChannelProps.length; i++) {
        const prop = rawChannelProps[i];
        if (channelProps.indexOf(prop) < 0) {
            throw new Error('Raw channel missing property: ' + prop);
        }
    }
    ...
}
```

Wait — `rawChannelProps` is NOT defined in this function! It references `rawChannelProps` but the local variable is `channelProps`. So `rawChannelProps` must be... a global? Let me check. In noVNC 1.7, there's a module-level const:

```js
const rawChannelProps = ["send", "close", "addEventListener", "removeEventListener"];
```

Hmm, actually let me look. The error says "missing property: send" — so `rawChannelProps` includes "send" and `channelProps` doesn't include "send".

Now — `my wrapper` is `class extends NativeWebSocket`. So `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(rawChannel))` on a subclass instance returns the **subclass prototype's own properties**, NOT the inherited NativeWebSocket prototype's properties! Because `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` only returns own properties — and for a subclass, `Object.getPrototypeOf(instance)` is `MyWrapper.prototype`, whose own properties are only what I defined (constructor). `send`, `close`, `addEventListener` live on `WebSocket.prototype`, which is the *prototype of the prototype*.

So `channelProps` = own keys of instance + own props of `MyWrapper.prototype` = only my own stuff, **missing `send`** (and possibly close/addEventListener).

THAT'S THE BUG. My instrumentation wrapper (a subclass) breaks noVNC's duck-typing check, which only looks one level up the prototype chain.

But wait — how is my wrapper even passed to noVNC? Line 127: `rfb = new RFB(screen, url, {...})` — it passes a **URL string**, not the wrapper! So noVNC does `this._sock.open(url, protocols)` → `attach(new WebSocket(uri, protocols))` → line 255, which constructs `new WebSocket(...)` = MY WRAPPER (because I overwrote `window.WebSocket`).

So my diagnostic wrapper is what BREAKS the connection! Before I added the wrapper, this worked. My instrumentation introduced the failure. That's a self-inflicted regression that I introduced in the previous turn when I added the wsLog wrapper.

const NativeWebSocket = window.WebSocket
// A Proxy, not a subclass: noVNC's Websock.attach() duck-types the channel with
// Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(channel)), which only looks

// with "Raw channel missing property: send" — a subclass literally cannot be
// passed to it. The construct trap returns a genuine native instance, so its
// prototype is unchanged and the check sees exactly what it would without this
// wrapper.
window.WebSocket = new Proxy(NativeWebSocket, {
  construct(target, args) {
    const socket = Reflect.construct(target, args)
    try {
      wsLog.push({ e: 'ctor', at: Date.now(), url: String(args[0]), protocols: ... })
      socket.addEventListener('open', ...)
      ...
    } catch { /* logging must never break the socket */ }
    return socket
  }
})
```

The WebSocket object created in `open()` is passed as an argument; after `attach` throws, the only references are: (a) the listener closures registered on the socket itself (self-references, and a cycle with itself — collectable by GC!), and (b) the browser's internal connection list.

Modern browsers CAN garbage-collect a WebSocket that has no external references? Per spec, an open WebSocket with no references can still be GC'd (the spec says the connection may be closed by GC). Chrome does GC WebSockets that are unreferenced. 1: /**
2:  * Self hot-reload: replace the running plugin with the code now on disk, without
3:  * restarting the application.
4:  *
5:  * Why this exists: Node caches an ES module by resolved URL for the life of the
6:  * process, so editing this package's host half changes nothing until the app is
7:  * restarted. The kernel's HMR service reloads *its own* packages by watching
8:  * files; it ships with that watching off and offers no "reload this plugin now"
9:  * API. So the sequence is performed here, against the same primitives the HMR
10:  * service itself uses:
11:  *
12:  *   1. snapshot the fiber(s) of this runtime and the config each was created with;
13:  *   2. evict this package's entries from the loader's ESM load cache (and from
14:  *      `require.cache`, where a module also exists on the CJS side);
15:  *   3. re-import the entry file so the new sources evaluate — falling back to a
16:  *      one-off query string when the eviction did not take, which is the case on
17:  *      Node versions whose load cache is no longer a plain Map;
18:  *   4. dispose the old fibers and register the replacement under the same config;
19:  *   5. on any failure, restore the caches and the previous registration, so the
20:  *      swap ends with either the old version or the new one running, never neither.
21:  *
22:  * @module src/reload.js
23:  */
24: 
25: import fs from 'node:fs'
26: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
27: import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
28: 
29: let inFlight = null
30: 
31: /** Whether a reload is currently running; guards against overlapping swaps. */
32: export function isReloading() {
33:   return inFlight !== null
34: }
35: 
36: /** This package's directory, as a `file://` URL with a trailing slash. */
37: export function packageUrlOf(entryModuleUrl) {
38:   return new URL('../', entryModuleUrl).href
39: }
40: 
41: /** This package's entry file, as an absolute `file://` URL. */
42: export function entryUrlOf(entryModuleUrl) {
43:   return new URL('../index.js', entryModuleUrl).href
44: }
45: 
46: /**
47:  * Every load-cache key living inside the package.
48:  *
49:  * Comparison tolerates case and percent-encoding drift between Node's resolver
50:  * and `new URL`, because a key that does not match is a module that silently
51:  * stays cached — the reload would then appear to succeed while running old code.
52:  */

> 资源全部 404**。所有从源码树启动的测试都是绿的，因为它们测的是源码树，不是浏览器真正加载的那份。

| --- | --- |

Host 半身是 Node 的 ES 模块，进程按 URL 缓存，**改文件不会自动生效**；而 `POST /reload` 是从

`src/reload.js` 负责把本包从 loader 的模块缓存里逐出、重新 import、再注册到同一个 fiber 上，

> 新增 `src/*.js` 或改 `package.json` 的 exports 之后，第一次仍需重启应用一次
> （模块解析本身也被缓存）；之后普通改动都是 `deploy` + `POST /reload` 秒级生效。

所以「握手根本没开始」和「服务端 1011 拒绝」在面板上长得一模一样。现在
`vnc-app.html` 包了一层 `WebSocket`，把 URL 和 open/error/close 的 code+reason 都记录下来，
随 `postMessage` 上报；面板优先显示**桥自己说的原因**（比如
「无法连接 duzhong.local:5901（5 个地址均失败）：connect timeout」），
没有原因才退回 `WebSocket code N`。`C:\Users\TestFox\.dsh\dzrobot-ssh\diag.jsonl` 里同样有完整线证。

**这个包装器只能用 Proxy，不能写成子类**（踩过的坑，代价很大）。noVNC 的 `Websock.attach()`
用下面这种方式做鸭子类型检查：

```js
const channelProps = [...Object.keys(rawChannel),
                      ...Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(rawChannel))];
```

`getOwnPropertyNames` **只看一层原型**。写成 `class extends WebSocket` 的话，`send` / `close` /
`binaryType` / `readyState` 都留在 `WebSocket.prototype`（原型链第二层），于是 noVNC 直接抛
`Raw channel missing property: send`。更麻烦的是这个异常从 `RFB` 构造函数里冒出来，那个 socket
随即失去所有可达引用、被 GC 回收、连接被中止——浏览器侧表现为**只有 `error` + close code 1006、
从不出现 `open`**，跟「小车掉线」长得几乎一样，极难分辨。

所以现在用 `new Proxy(NativeWebSocket, { construct })`，陷阱里返回的是**原生实例**，原型链一层不变。
`scripts/test-vnc-wrapper.mjs` 把 `vnc-app.html` 里那段真实代码（靠 `/* ws-log:start */` 标记提取）
喂给 noVNC **真实的** `Websock.attach()` 跑一遍，并且额外断言「子类确实会被拒绝」——
保证这个测试不会退化成空转。

**安全**：所有路由只接受本机回环；装了 `connection` 服务时走它自己的准入判断。", "old_string": "**为什么报错要说人话**：noVNC 的 `disconnect` 事件**只有 `{clean}`**，不带关闭码和原因——

**这个包装器只能用 Proxy，不能写成子类**（踩过的坑，代价很大）。noVNC 的 `Websock.attach()`
用下面这种方式做鸭子类型检查：

```js
const channelProps = [...Object.keys(rawChannel),
                      ...Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(rawChannel))];
```

`getOwnPropertyNames` **只看一层原型**。写成 `class extends WebSocket` 的话，`send` / `close` /
`binaryType` / `readyState` 都留在 `WebSocket.prototype`（原型链第二层），于是 noVNC 直接抛

从不出现 `open`**，跟「小车掉线」长得几乎一样，极难分辨。

所以现在用 `new Proxy(NativeWebSocket, { construct })`，陷阱里返回的是**原生实例**，原型链一层不变。

保证这个测试不会退化成空转。

我先纠正上一轮的错误判断：我说"你的 VNC 已经连上了"，依据是日志里 `accepted: 10.240.174.14` —— **那是我自己跑的测试连接**（跑了 4 次，日志里正好 4 对）。不是你的浏览器。抱歉，这个结论下得太快。

## 真正的两个原因，都是我这边的错

**原因一：我的诊断代码本身把连接弄坏了**

我为了抓失败原因，把 `WebSocket` 包了一层。我用了 `class extends WebSocket`——而 noVNC 的通道检查是：

```js
Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(rawChannel))   // 只看一层原型
```

子类把 `send`/`close`/`binaryType` 留在了原型链**第二层**，于是 noVNC 直接抛 `Raw channel missing property: send`。更糟的是这个异常从 `RFB` 构造函数里冒出来，那个 socket 随即**失去所有可达引用、被 GC 回收、连接中止**——浏览器侧就表现为"**从不出现 open，只有 error + 1016/1006**"，跟"小车掉线"几乎无法分辨。

`diag.jsonl` 里 18 条 `vnc.failed` 全是这一条。**换成 `new Proxy(NativeWebSocket, { construct })`**（陷阱返回原生实例，原型链一层不变）后解决。

**原因二：真正在跑的那份插件缺了整个 VNC 资源**

Profile 用 `file:D:/…` 依赖本目录，安装时被打包成**副本**，而打包遵循 `package.json#files`——那份清单里**没有 `novnc/` 和 `vnc-app.html`**。所以安装后 `/vnc.html`、`/novnc/core/rfb.js` 全部 **404**。

我还发现 README 里写着"是指向本目录的 junction，改代码立刻生效"——**这是错的**，实际是打包副本。这就是为什么我前面几轮的修改一直没到浏览器：源码树改了、`POST /reload` 也回了 `ok`，但 reload 是从**安装位置**重新 import 的，它忠实地重载了那份旧副本。

## 我的测试为什么没抓到

这是我的盲区，值得说明：`test-host.mjs`、`test-live-ws.mjs` 都从**源码树**启动，测的是源码树，不是你浏览器真正加载的那份产物。所以两处都绿，功能却全废。

补了两个专门堵盲区的测试：

- **`test-vnc-wrapper.mjs`** — 把 `vnc-app.html` 里那段**真实代码**（靠标记提取）喂给 noVNC **真实的** `Websock.attach()`；并且额外断言"**子类确实会被拒绝**"，保证它不会退化成空转。
- **`test-package-files.mjs`** — 断言运行时资源既被 `files` 声明、又确实存在于**安装副本**，且与源码树逐字节一致。它当场复现了故障，修完变绿。

另外加了 `scripts/deploy.mjs`（同步到安装位置，`--dry-run` 可预览）和 `scripts/debug-ws-handshake.mjs`（用浏览器同款请求头打握手，打印原始响应）。README 里那句错误说明已改正。

## 已验证 / 未验证

| 已验证 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 浏览器要访问的 4 个 URL | 全部 200 |
| 伺服页面是修复版 | 是（Proxy，非子类） |
| 浏览器同款握手 | accept key 正确、子协议合法、扩展正确拒绝 |
| 真车 RFB 横幅 | `RFB 003.003` 126ms 到达 |
| 五套回归 | 全绿 |

**未验证的是实际桌面渲染**——那需要浏览器，我这边没法点。所以请你**刷新页面，点一次"连接桌面"**。

如果还有问题，现在 `diag.jsonl` 会给出确切原因（我给探针加了时间戳，因果顺序不再含糊）。

## 车侧那个问题仍然存在

`dhd` 驱动关联热点失败（`WLC_E_SET_SSID`），信号良好、省电已关，是**硬件/驱动层**问题，得让负责硬件的人看。插件这边现在能明确区分"车掉线"和"车在线但桌面有问题"。

另：`package.json#files` 里有个陈旧的 `locale` 条目（目录不存在），无害，但我的部署脚本每次会警告一行——要不要顺手清掉，你定。

tools.name: agent_teams_add_member
tools.description: Add a member to the team roster. Planning and idle roster rows do not call a model. After approval, the member session starts with its first ready task or explicit message and remains durable for later work.

name.description: Unique member name inside the team.

role.description: Role of the member (e.g. researcher, engineer, reviewer).

provider.description: Optional LLM provider route. Use only when the user explicitly requests a different provider; requires model.

executionPrompt.description: Optional member-specific execution prompt. It remains editable while staged.

tools.name: agent_teams_amend_task
tools.description: Captain-only controlled contract amendment for one non-terminal quality task: replace a wrong objective/acceptance/verify/inScope/outOfScope when the original contract makes honest completion impossible (for example a verify command that cannot pass, or an inScope that forbids the file the objective names). The amendment is appended to the task's revisions ledger with previous values and the reason, and is rejected once a review/requirements task has passed judgment on this task. Members cannot amend contracts; the implementer re-reads the amended contract before its next quality gate. Lists are full replacements, not deltas.

task_id.description: Task whose contract is being amended.

reason.description: Why the current contract is wrong; recorded in the revisions ledger.

objective.description: Replacement objective.

acceptance.description: Replacement acceptance criteria (full list, not a delta).

verify.description: Replacement verification commands (full list, not a delta).

tools.name: agent_teams_approve
tools.description: Approve and start a staged team plan. Call this only in response to an explicit user approval in a new user turn; never call it during the turn that created or edited the plan. The Web Approve & Run button uses the same runtime directly.

tools.name: agent_teams_claim_task
tools.description: Members claim their own ready task or read their existing attempt_id. Captains must use reassign_task to assign and wake a member; claim_task does not dispatch work. A member cannot own a second unfinished task. The returned attempt_id is required for updates and becomes stale after retry/reassignment.

assignee.description: Deprecated: claim_task only supports a member claiming its own task. Captains must use reassign_task.

tools.name: agent_teams_create
tools.description: Create a team. Use approval=required for a two-phase plan: members and tasks remain unspawned/unclaimed until the user reviews the Web plan and explicitly approves it. Optional profiles expand their configured roster; seed profiles also expand template tasks, while captain profiles leave the graph for the Captain to design. approval=automatic preserves the legacy immediate-execution path.

name.description: Name for the new team (used as its stable id).

description.description: Team purpose / the goal the team will work on.

plan.description: Optional complete ordinary-work roster and DAG in one atomic call, instead of separate add_member/create_task rounds. Mutually exclusive with profile. For quality gates use create_task with the explicit quality contract.

id.description: Local reference used by dependencies in this plan; the result maps it to a durable task id.

approval.description: required stages the plan for explicit user review; automatic starts immediately. Defaults to automatic for API compatibility.

tools.name: agent_teams_create_task
tools.description: Create a task in your team's task list. Use kind=work (default) for research, repository audits and general tasks. kind=review is only a quality gate for an existing implementation/repair task via reviewedTaskId. Every call must include a non-empty subject, including verification and review tasks. Tasks can depend on other tasks (dependencies): a task is only claimable once every dependency is completed. Optionally assign it to a member, who still claims it before working.

subject.description: Required non-empty title for this task. Never omit it, including for verification or review tasks.

description.description: What needs to be done, in detail.

dependencies.description: Task ids this task depends on (must be completed before this task can be claimed).

assignee.description: Member name when an owner is specified. Omission puts this task in the shared pool; roles, subjects and descriptions do not assign an owner.

kind.description: Explicit task kind. Omission means work with no quality gates, even if the subject says implementation/review. Quality kinds require a contract. An implementation may be planned before requirements passes when its dependency chain includes that requirements task.

objective.description: Required non-empty objective for quality kinds.

inScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task may change.

outOfScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task must not change.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria. Required for quality kinds.

reviewedTaskId.description: Existing AgentTeams implementation/repair task id. Required for kind=review; an external repository audit is kind=work.

sourceFindingIds.description: Finding ids this repair must close.

coverageOf.description: User-constraint / goal items this task covers.

resume.description: If true, clear halted in the same lock before creating the task.

tools.name: agent_teams_delete
tools.description: End and archive your team: interrupts members and moves the current tasks and mailboxes out of active state for later inspection. Use when the work is done or explicitly abandoned. A same-name archive replaces its previous generation.

tools.name: agent_teams_edit_plan
tools.description: Atomically revise an AgentTeams plan. While staged, edit tasks and roster without starting work. While running, only update_task is allowed, and only for pending tasks with no prior attempt: correct dependencies, assignees or descriptions before they start; newly ready work is scheduled after commit. Never edit active/finished attempts. Submit dependent edits in order. Never modify .agent-teams files directly.

operations.description: One atomic, ordered batch. Running teams allow only update_task for never-started pending tasks. If any operation is invalid, none of the edits are saved.

member_name.description: Member name for update_member or remove_member.

task_id.description: Task id for update_task or remove_task.

subject.description: Required for add_task; optional replacement for update_task.

description.description: Optional task description.

assignee.description: Optional task assignee; an empty string moves it to the shared pool.

dependencies.description: Complete replacement dependency list for a task.

provider.description: Optional member provider; defaults to the current staged route.

model.description: Optional member model; defaults to the current staged route.

tools.description: Atomically retry, reassign, or let the captain take over one ready unfinished/failed task. The old attempt is revoked before its member is interrupted, so late updates cannot overwrite the new owner. Use assignee="captain" only when you will finish that task in this turn; a captain can own only one unfinished takeover at a time, and an unfinished takeover returns to the member pool when the captain becomes idle.

assignee.description: Active member name, or "captain" for captain takeover.

reason.description: Why the task is being retried or reassigned.

tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

content.text:
The user is now asking for a new, larger feature: a general-purpose noVNC-based VNC connector. This builds on the existing dzrobot-ssh plugin which already has a VNC bridge. The user wants:

1. Input fields: VNC host, WebSocket port, path, VNC password
2. Use noVNC RFB to connect ws://host:port/websockify
3. Support adaptive scaling, fullscreen, disconnect, reconnect
4. If DSH is Electron/Tauri, embed WebView
5. If DSH is a browser plugin, use iframe or new tab
6. Give complete Ubuntu-side TigerVNC + websockify commands
7. Give SSH tunnel secure connection solution

This is a significant build. The context: we have a working plugin `dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh` in D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05 with a VNC bridge (WebSocket upgrade at /api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc), vendored noVNC in novnc/, a vnc-app.html, client panel etc.

Now the user wants a standalone VNC connector with arbitrary host/port/path/password. Let me think about the architecture.

Current state knowledge:
- DSH is the DeepSeek Harness GUI at http://127.0.0.1:19387. The user interacts through this Web GUI. It's a browser-based GUI (Electron? The checkout is at C:\Users\TestFox\AppData\Local\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\app.asar\dsh\ — that's an Electron app, app.asar is an Electron archive!). So DSH IS Electron-based. But plugins run with client code in the renderer and host code in the main process.

- The existing plugin `dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh` has:
  - index.js (host half) — registers HTTP API routes and a WebSocket upgrade at /api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc that bridges to the car's VNC TCP port
  - client.js (client half) — renders panels in the DSH GUI
  - vnc-app.html / novnc/ — the iframe document with noVNC
  - src/vnc.js — VncBridge class with the address cache and banner guard we just built

The new request is a general VNC connector: user enters VNC host, WebSocket port, path, password; connect via ws://host:port/websockify (i.e., connect directly to a websockify endpoint, not through our own bridge); adaptive scaling, fullscreen, disconnect, reconnect; embed WebView if Electron/Tauri, iframe/new tab if browser plugin; plus docs for Ubuntu TigerVNC+websockify and SSH tunnel secure solution.

This is a multi-step build. The user said "请帮我做一个基于 noVNC 的 VNC 连接器" — build me a noVNC-based VNC connector.

Plan:
1. Since DSH is Electron (app.asar), the client code runs in the renderer. But wait — the plugin system: we have host half (main process, node) and client half (renderer). The client half can't open raw WebSockets to arbitrary origins easily? Actually in the renderer, WebSocket to ws://host:port is subject to CSP? In Electron, the renderer has full network access generally, but noVNC needs the page. Actually our existing approach: iframe with vnc.html served by the host half at http://127.0.0.1:port/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc.html, and noVNC inside the iframe connects to a WebSocket (either our own upgrade or directly to the target).

For a generic connector: the user wants to connect to ws://host:port/websockify directly. The cleanest approach consistent with existing architecture: reuse the iframe + vnc.html pattern, but make it generic: pass connection parameters (host, port, path, password) via postMessage or URL params from the client panel to the iframe. The iframe then does new RFB(target) with ws://host:port/path.

But there's a catch: the browser renderer can connect to arbitrary ws:// URLs? In Electron renderer with default settings, yes, WebSocket connections are allowed (webSecurity default on, but ws connections aren't blocked by CORS; only the server can reject by origin). websockify by default doesn't check origin? Actually websockify has --web option; by default noVNC in iframe connects fine. OK.

However, there's the existing knowledge from the README: DSH pages run under dsh-app:// scheme and iframes to http://127.0.0.1 work because loopback is treated as trustworthy. The iframe approach already proven.

For "if DSH is Electron/Tauri, embed WebView" — DSH is Electron. But as a plugin, we can't easily spawn a WebView/browserWindow from the client half; the host half (main process) could spawn a BrowserWindow or use <webview> tag. But plugins in DSH — we don't know if the host half has access to Electron's BrowserWindow module. The host half is node code inside the Electron main process, so `require('electron')` might work. But this is speculative.

Pragmatic approach: use the iframe (works everywhere, including this Electron GUI), and offer a "new tab" option

1. 有输入框：VNC 主机、WebSocket 端口、路径、VNC 密码、还有分辨率选择；
2. 使用 noVNC RFB 连接 ws://host:port/websockify；
3. 支持自适应缩放、全屏、断开、重连；

5. 如果 DSH 是浏览器插件，就用 iframe 或新标签页；
6. 给出 Ubuntu 端 TigerVNC + websockify 的完整命令；
7. 给出 SSH 隧道安全连接方案。

tools.name: agent_teams_add_member
tools.description: Add a member to the team roster. Planning and idle roster rows do not call a model. After approval, the member session starts with its first ready task or explicit message and remains durable for later work.

name.description: Unique member name inside the team.

role.description: Role of the member (e.g. researcher, engineer, reviewer).

provider.description: Optional LLM provider route. Use only when the user explicitly requests a different provider; requires model.

model.description: Optional model override. Omit for the captain's current model (or the configured memberModel default).

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort override: one of the target model's supported effort ids, or "default" to force its default. When omitted, the captain's effort is inherited only for the same provider/model; a changed route uses the target default.

executionPrompt.description: Optional member-specific execution prompt. It remains editable while staged.

tools.name: agent_teams_amend_task
tools.description: Captain-only controlled contract amendment for one non-terminal quality task: replace a wrong objective/acceptance/verify/inScope/outOfScope when the original contract makes honest completion impossible (for example a verify command that cannot pass, or an inScope that forbids the file the objective names). The amendment is appended to the task's revisions ledger with previous values and the reason, and is rejected once a review/requirements task has passed judgment on this task. Members cannot amend contracts; the implementer re-reads the amended contract before its next quality gate. Lists are full replacements, not deltas.

task_id.description: Task whose contract is being amended.

reason.description: Why the current contract is wrong; recorded in the revisions ledger.

objective.description: Replacement objective.

acceptance.description: Replacement acceptance criteria (full list, not a delta).

verify.description: Replacement verification commands (full list, not a delta).

tools.name: agent_teams_approve
tools.description: Approve and start a staged team plan. Call this only in response to an explicit user approval in a new user turn; never call it during the turn that created or edited the plan. The Web Approve & Run button uses the same runtime directly.

tools.name: agent_teams_claim_task
tools.description: Members claim their own ready task or read their existing attempt_id. Captains must use reassign_task to assign and wake a member; claim_task does not dispatch work. A member cannot own a second unfinished task. The returned attempt_id is required for updates and becomes stale after retry/reassignment.

assignee.description: Deprecated: claim_task only supports a member claiming its own task. Captains must use reassign_task.

tools.name: agent_teams_create
tools.description: Create a team. Use approval=required for a two-phase plan: members and tasks remain unspawned/unclaimed until the user reviews the Web plan and explicitly approves it. Optional profiles expand their configured roster; seed profiles also expand template tasks, while captain profiles leave the graph for the Captain to design. approval=automatic preserves the legacy immediate-execution path.

name.description: Name for the new team (used as its stable id).

description.description: Team purpose / the goal the team will work on.

plan.description: Optional complete ordinary-work roster and DAG in one atomic call, instead of separate add_member/create_task rounds. Mutually exclusive with profile. For quality gates use create_task with the explicit quality contract.

id.description: Local reference used by dependencies in this plan; the result maps it to a durable task id.

approval.description: required stages the plan for explicit user review; automatic starts immediately. Defaults to automatic for API compatibility.

tools.name: agent_teams_create_task
tools.description: Create a task in your team's task list. Use kind=work (default) for research, repository audits and general tasks. kind=review is only a quality gate for an existing implementation/repair task via reviewedTaskId. Every call must include a non-empty subject, including verification and review tasks. Tasks can depend on other tasks (dependencies): a task is only claimable once every dependency is completed. Optionally assign it to a member, who still claims it before working.

subject.description: Required non-empty title for this task. Never omit it, including for verification or review tasks.

description.description: What needs to be done, in detail.

dependencies.description: Task ids this task depends on (must be completed before this task can be claimed).

assignee.description: Member name when an owner is specified. Omission puts this task in the shared pool; roles, subjects and descriptions do not assign an owner.

kind.description: Explicit task kind. Omission means work with no quality gates, even if the subject says implementation/review. Quality kinds require a contract. An implementation may be planned before requirements passes when its dependency chain includes that requirements task.

objective.description: Required non-empty objective for quality kinds.

inScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task may change.

outOfScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task must not change.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria. Required for quality kinds.

reviewedTaskId.description: Existing AgentTeams implementation/repair task id. Required for kind=review; an external repository audit is kind=work.

sourceFindingIds.description: Finding ids this repair must close.

coverageOf.description: User-constraint / goal items this task covers.

resume.description: If true, clear halted in the same lock before creating the task.

tools.name: agent_teams_delete
tools.description: End and archive your team: interrupts members and moves the current tasks and mailboxes out of active state for later inspection. Use when the work is done or explicitly abandoned. A same-name archive replaces its previous generation.

tools.name: agent_teams_edit_plan
tools.description: Atomically revise an AgentTeams plan. While staged, edit tasks and roster without starting work. While running, only update_task is allowed, and only for pending tasks with no prior attempt: correct dependencies, assignees or descriptions before they start; newly ready work is scheduled after commit. Never edit active/finished attempts. Submit dependent edits in order. Never modify .agent-teams files directly.

operations.description: One atomic, ordered batch. Running teams allow only update_task for never-started pending tasks. If any operation is invalid, none of the edits are saved.

member_name.description: Member name for update_member or remove_member.

task_id.description: Task id for update_task or remove_task.

subject.description: Required for add_task; optional replacement for update_task.

description.description: Optional task description.

assignee.description: Optional task assignee; an empty string moves it to the shared pool.

dependencies.description: Complete replacement dependency list for a task.

provider.description: Optional member provider; defaults to the current staged route.

model.description: Optional member model; defaults to the current staged route.

tools.name: agent_teams_reassign_task
tools.description: Atomically retry, reassign, or let the captain take over one ready unfinished/failed task. The old attempt is revoked before its member is interrupted, so late updates cannot overwrite the new owner. Use assignee="captain" only when you will finish that task in this turn; a captain can own only one unfinished takeover at a time, and an unfinished takeover returns to the member pool when the captain becomes idle.

assignee.description: Active member name, or "captain" for captain takeover.

reason.description: Why the task is being retried or reassigned.

tools.name: agent_teams_remove_member
tools.description: Remove a member safely: revoke its current attempts, return all unfinished owned tasks to the shared pending pool, interrupt its live turn, and mark it removed.

name.description: Name of the member to remove.

tools.name: agent_teams_resume
tools.description: Explicitly resume a halted team. Requires a non-empty reason. Does not recreate cancelled tasks; only still-pending work is scheduled.

reason.description: Why the team is being resumed.

tools.name: agent_teams_send_message
tools.description: Send coordination or current-task guidance directly to the captain or a teammate. A running recipient receives it at the next model step; an idle recipient wakes. Messages are durably retained until read. Use task creation/reassignment for a new unit of work, not repeated status nudges.

source_task_id.description: Sender task, NOT the recipient task. Members include it with source_attempt_id. Captains sending guidance normally omit both source fields.

source_attempt_id.description: Sender execution capability paired with source_task_id. Stale reports are rejected. Omit for ordinary captain guidance.

content.description: The message text.

from.description: Sender (defaults to the caller: the captain, or the calling member).

tools.name: agent_teams_status
tools.description: Team snapshot: members with live activity and tasks with status/assignee/dependencies/output. Captains also see every team mailbox; members see only their own inbox. Use after mailbox progress deliveries or for an explicit status request. After dispatch, end your turn while members work; do not repeatedly poll.

tools.name: agent_teams_update_task
tools.description: Update a task status/output. Members must supply the current attempt_id returned by claim_task; stale attempts are rejected after takeover/reassignment. Terminal results are immutable, but owners and the captain can append acceptanceResults/commandsRun/evidence_note as attributed supplemental evidence, without reclaiming or changing the verdict. A captain must use reassign_task(assignee="captain") before updating active member-owned work.

attempt_id.description: Members must explicitly include the current attempt_id from their assignment/claim in EVERY update, including failed reviews with findings. If omitted, retry with the same current id; omission does not revoke the attempt.

output.description: Original result summary; immutable after completion/failure.

evidence_note.description: Append-only supplementary observation on a terminal task. Does not reopen work or change the original result.

verdict.description: Required for completing requirements/review. needs_revision and reject must fail the task.

findings.description: Structured review findings. Required when verdict is needs_revision or reject; each item needs id, severity, problem, and requiredFix.

changedPaths.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths changed by this implementation/repair.

acceptanceResults.description: Acceptance evidence in contract order: {criterion, status:"passed"|"failed", evidence?}. Supply one item per acceptance criterion.

commandsRun.description: Verification evidence in contract order: {command, status:"passed"|"failed", exitCode?, evidence?}. Supply one item per verify command.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

A Client query waits for the first valid page response within the configured timeout; otherwise it reports a Client failure or asks you to reconnect and retry. tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

content.text:
The user is asking me to build a new standalone VNC connector feature (part of the dzrobot plugin presumably), with:

1. Input fields: VNC host, WebSocket port, path, VNC password, and resolution selection
2. Use noVNC RFB to connect to ws://host:port/websockify
3. Adaptive scaling, fullscreen, disconnect, reconnect
4. If DSH is Electron/Tauri, embed WebView
5. If DSH is browser plugin, use iframe or new tab
6. Give Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify complete commands
7. Give SSH tunnel secure connection solution

Let me think about the current state of the project.

The plugin is `dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh` in `D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05`. It has:
- `index.js` — host half: HTTP API routes, WebSocket upgrade at `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` that bridges to the car's VNC TCP port (TCP bridge mode)
- `client.js` — client half: panels in DSH GUI
- `vnc-app.html` / `novnc/` — iframe document with noVNC
- `src/vnc.js` — VncBridge (TCP dialing with mDNS cache + RFB banner guard)
- scripts/ — tests

Now the user wants a **generic VNC connector**: connect via WebSocket to `ws://host:port/websockify` (websockify protocol), not the TCP bridge. This is a new mode: instead of the host half bridging TCP to the car's 5901, the browser noVNC connects directly to a websockify endpoint.

Key design decisions:

1. **Connection model**: noVNC's RFB can connect to a WebSocket URL directly. The user wants `ws://host:port/websockify`. So the noVNC client connects directly to the WebSocket — no need for the host-half bridge at all. This is the standard noVNC usage.

   But wait — there's a catch. The DSH client runs under `dsh-app://` scheme. Direct WebSocket from the iframe: the iframe is served from `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dzrobot-ssh/...` by the host half, and inside that iframe, `new WebSocket('ws://host:port/websockify')` should work fine — it's a normal http origin. CORS doesn't apply to WebSocket. So direct connect works from the iframe.

   Alternative: route through the host half as a WebSocket proxy (`/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc-proxy?url=ws://host:port/websockify`). That has advantages: it works even when the target websockify only accepts certain origins, avoids mixed-content issues (ws:// from https pages), and lets the host log/handle errors. But it adds latency and complexity. For flexibility, maybe support both: direct from iframe (default) — simpler and true to the request "使用 noVNC RFB 连接 ws://host:port/websockify".

   Actually, let me think about mixed content. The DSH GUI is at http://127.0.0.1:19387 — http, not https. The iframe is http://127.0.0.1:port. From an http page, ws:// connections are allowed. So direct ws:// from the iframe works.

   But for security (SSH tunnel solution in requirement 7), the flow would be: SSH tunnel local port → websockify on Ubuntu... wait no. Requirement 7: SSH tunnel secure connection. That means: user runs `ssh -L localPort:localhost:remotePort` to the Ubuntu server, websockify runs on the Ubuntu server at some port, and the browser connects to `ws://127.0.0.1:localPort/websockify` through the tunnel. In that case the browser connects to localhost directly — again direct from iframe works.

   So: **the generic connector is pure browser-side** (iframe + noVNC), no host-half bridge needed. This is much simpler than the car-specific TCP bridge.

2. **Where does the UI live?** The existing plugin has a panel in `client.js` for the car. The new request is for a standalone VNC connector — possibly a new panel/section in the same plugin, or a new plugin. Given the plugin structure, adding a "通用 VNC 连接器" section to the existing dzrobot plugin panel makes sense, or a separate new panel.

   Let me look at the plugin structure more carefully. The client registers slots/panels. Let me check what exists.

3. **Electron WebView vs iframe**: DSH is Electron-based (DeepSeek Harness is an Electron app — app.asar mentioned in system prompt). In Electron, a `<webview>` tag would be the "embedded WebView", but inside a plugin panel rendered in the app, `<webview>` might work if `webviewTag: true` is enabled. Risky. The safer universal approach: iframe (works in both Electron and browser). Requirement 4 says "如果 DSH 是 Electron/Tauri，就嵌入 WebView；如果 DSH 是浏览器插件，就用 iframe 或新标签页". 

   How do we detect Electron vs browser from the client? Check `navigator.userAgent` for "Electron", or `window.process?.type`, or the presence of `window.require`. In Electron renderer with nodeIntegration, `window.process.type === 'renderer'`. Tauri has `window.__TAURI__`. 

   Pragmatic approach: detect Electron (`window.process?.versions?.electron` or UA contains "Electron"). If Electron — try to use `<webview>` tag; but webview tag needs `webviewTag: true` in webPreferences, and we can't guarantee that. Fallback: iframe works everywhere. Actually, a `<webview>` in an Electron app is essentially an iframe with a separate renderer process. The practical difference for us: none for display purposes; noVNC needs a real http(s) origin to load ES modules — the webview would need to load the same http://127.0.0.1 URL. So honestly iframe does the job in both cases, and "embed WebView" can be interpreted as "embed the viewer inside the panel" (iframe is the embedding mechanism). 

   I'll implement: detect environment; in Electron, attempt `<webview>` only if available (check `document.createElement('webview').constructor.name` isn't HTMLElement... actually simplest robust check: try creating a webview and see if it has its methods). Hmm, that's over-engineering. 

   Better: The iframe approach is proven in this plugin (it's already documented why iframe is needed — dsh-app:// scheme, ES module loading). For a browser plugin, iframe or new tab (requirement 5). For Electron, "嵌入 WebView" — I'll use the iframe as the embedding mechanism (it IS a WebView in Electron terminology — Electron's iframe... no, Electron calls them webContents).

   Let me be honest in the implementation: provide three display modes:
   - `iframe` (embedded in panel) — works everywhere, default
   - `webview` (Electron `<webview>` tag) — used when running in Electron AND webviewTag is enabled; falls back to iframe automatically
   - `tab` (new browser tab) — opens `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc-generic.html?params...` in a new tab

   For the new tab case, the params (host, port, path, password) must be passed via URL — but password in URL is bad (history, logs). Better: pass via fragment? Also visible. Alternative: pass a session token in URL that the page exchanges... over-complicated. 

   Hmm. Simpler: the generic vnc page (vnc-generic.html) can read its connection config from `localStorage` keyed by a random token in the URL fragment. Fragment isn't sent to the server, so it stays out of logs. The panel writes localStorage, opens tab with `#token=...`. The page reads config from localStorage and clears it. That works but adds moving parts.

   Let me keep the scope sane: 
   - Embedded mode (default): iframe with postMessage passing the config (proven pattern already in this plugin — the panel already passes settings via postMessage to vnc-app.html). Config including password via postMessage to the iframe — that's fine (in-memory only).
   - New tab mode: I'll generate the URL with query params, and for the password use a session token: the host half can expose a tiny `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc-session` POST endpoint that stores config in memory for 2 minutes and returns an id; the tab URL is `vnc-generic.html?session=id`; the page fetches `session=id` to get config (including password) and then the host forgets it. That's clean and avoids password-in-URL. The fetch is same-origin http, fine.

   That's a reasonable, secure-ish design. Password in memory of host process for 2 minutes max, single-use.

   Actually — even simpler and consistent: make the host half's generic page fetch config via `fetch('/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc-session?id=...')`. Let me implement that.

4. **Host-side**: The generic connector doesn't need a bridge. It needs:
   - Serve `/vnc-generic.html` (new standalone noVNC page, adapted from vnc-app.html but generic: takes host/port/path/password/scale/fullscreen params, no car-specific diagnostics... well keep diagnostics since they were valuable)
   - Serve the noVNC assets (already done under /api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/)
   - A session store endpoint: POST `/vnc-session` {host, port, path, password, ...} → {id}; GET `/vnc-session?id=` → config (single-use, TTL 120s)
   - Maybe a websockify-style proxy endpoint for when direct ws:// is blocked (mixed content from https DSH? DSH is http here). I'll skip the proxy; direct ws from the iframe works. Actually wait — should I add a proxy mode? Requirement 2 says "使用 noVNC RFB 连接 ws://host:port/websockify" — direct connection. Keep it direct.

   Hmm, but one consideration: from an Electron renderer, WebSocket connections go through Chromium's network stack — same as browser. ws:// works. OK, direct it is.

5. **noVNC page features**: adaptive scaling (noVNC's `scaleViewport` + `resizeSession` + browser window resize listener), fullscreen (fullscreen on the iframe's documentElement or the screen element), disconnect, reconnect (re-open the WebSocket/重新调用 RFB with same config). The user wants buttons: 缩放适配、全屏、断开、重连、分辨率选择.

   Resolution selection: pass `resizeSession` with chosen WxH (noVNC supports remote resize via SetDesktopSize extension). Also could restart the VNC server at new resolution on Ubuntu side — but that's remote command execution; the generic connector can't ssh into arbitrary hosts. So resolution selection = request desktop size via RFB (works with TigerVNC + RandR). If server doesn't support it, fall back to scaling. I'll implement: dropdown with common resolutions + "自适应" option; when a resolution is chosen, send SetDesktopSize; the page also scales.

6. **Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify commands** (requirement 6): provide a documented script `scripts/ubuntu-setup-vnc.sh` with complete commands:
   - Install: `sudo apt install tigervnc-standalone-server tigervnc-common websockify`
   - Create user, set VNC password: `vncpasswd`
   - systemd unit `vncserver@:1.service` with geometry
   - websockify systemd unit wrapping 5901 → 6080 with `--web /usr/share/novnc`
   - ufw rules
   - Test commands
   
   I should write this as a real script file in the plugin's scripts/ folder and also present the key commands in my final response.

7. **SSH tunnel secure connection** (requirement 7): document + maybe implement a convenience. The flow: 
   ```
   ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 user@ubuntu-host
   ```
   then connect to `ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify` — websockify only listening on localhost on the server. Provide a script `scripts/ubuntu-secure-vnc.sh` or document it. Also the plugin's existing tunnel mode (`vncMode: tunnel`) already does this for the car. For the generic connector, the user just fills host=127.0.0.1, port=6080 after opening the tunnel manually.
