1: /**
2:  * dzrobot-ssh — plugin entry (Host half).
3:  *
4:  * What this half owns:
5:  *   · the settings for one car (host, user, port, extra ssh options);
6:  *   · the reachability and login probe, so the sidebar can say *why* a click
7:  *     would fail before the user spends the click;
8:  *   · a small cached description of the car (user, host, kernel, uptime);
9:  *   · a local JSON API the browser half reads, plus a diagnostic sink.
10:  *
11:  * What it deliberately does not own: the interactive SSH session. That runs in
12:  * a real DSH terminal, so the user gets echo, completion, Ctrl-C and resize from
13:  * the terminal the app already ships rather than a second-rate imitation here.
14:  * The browser half opens that terminal and types the command line this API
15:  * composes. See `src/ssh.js` for why the command is returned as text and the
16:  * probing path is `BatchMode=yes`.
17:  *
18:  * Nothing is a hard dependency: a composition without a web server still loads
19:  * the plugin and still probes on demand, it just has no page to answer.
20:  *
21:  * @module index.js
22:  */
23: 
24: import fs from 'node:fs'
25: import path from 'node:path'
26: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
27: import { DATA_DIR_NAME, JsonStore, SETTINGS_INITIAL, resolveDshHome } from './src/store.js'
28: import { commandLine, describe as describeCar, interactiveArgv, localName, probe } from './src/ssh.js'
29: import { isLoopback, rejectionFor } from './src/trust.js'
30: import { isReloading, selfReload, watchPackage } from './src/reload.js'
31: import { VncBridge, vncTarget } from './src/vnc.js'
32: import { acceptUpgrade, WebSocketChannel } from './src/ws.js'
33: import {
34:   MAX_READ_BYTES, MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, downloadFile, homeShortcuts,
35:   listDirectory, readTextFile, statPath, uploadFile,
36: } from './src/files.js'
37: 
38: export const name = 'dzrobot-ssh'
39: 
40: /** No hard requirement: every host facility below is reached opportunistically. */
41: export const inject = []
42: 
43: /** The vendored noVNC tree, served to the browser half as native ES modules. */
44: const NOVNC_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('./novnc/', import.meta.url))
45: 
46: /** The VNC screen document, embedded by the panel from a real http origin. */
47: const VNC_APP_FILE = fileURLToPath(new URL('./vnc-app.html', import.meta.url))
48: 
49: /** Content types for the vendored tree; anything else is refused, not guessed. */
50: const NOVNC_TYPES = {
51:   '.js': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8',
52:   '.mjs': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8',
53:   '.css': 'text/css; charset=utf-8',
54:   '.json': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
55:   '.txt': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
56:   '.md': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
57: }
58: 
59: export function apply(ctx, config = {}) {
60:   const logger = ctx.logger ?? console
61:   const home = resolveDshHome()
62:   const dataDir = path.join(home, DATA_DIR_NAME)
63:   fs.mkdirSync(dataDir, { recursive: true })
64: 
65:   const settings = new JsonStore(path.join(dataDir, 'settings.json'), SETTINGS_INITIAL, {
66:     log: message => logger.warn?.(message),
67:   })
68:   /** Last probe/description, kept so a reloaded page paints without re-probing. */
69:   const status = new JsonStore(path.join(dataDir, 'status.json'), {
70:     version: 1,
71:     probe: undefined,
72:     car: undefined,
73:     at: 0,
74:   }, { log: message => logger.warn?.(message) })
75: 
76:   const diagFile = path.join(dataDir, 'diag.jsonl')
77: 
78:   // The diagnostic log is a development aid with a hard purpose: a browser
79:   // plugin cannot be introspected from here, so the browser half reports what it
80:   // actually found — which services exist, whether the terminal opened, whether
81:   // the command was written — and that report is the only way to tell a working
82:   // integration from one that silently did nothing.
83:   let selfTest = config.selfTest === true
84:   let selfTestConsumed = false
85: 
86:   // Opt-in source watching: a normal install does not rewrite its own files, but
87:   // while this plugin is being worked on, a restart per edit is the expensive
88:   // part. Off unless the entry's config asks for it.
89:   let watcher
90:   if (config.watchSources === true) {
91:     watcher = watchPackage(fileURLToPath(new URL('./', import.meta.url)), {
92:       logger,
93:       onChange: () => {
94:         void selfReload(ctx, { logger }).catch(error => logger.warn?.(`dzrobot-ssh: reload failed (${error?.message ?? error})`))
95:       },
96:     })
97:     logger.info?.('dzrobot-ssh: watching sources, edits reload the plugin')
98:   }
99: 
100:   /** One probe, with the car description folded in when login works. */
101:   async function runProbe({ withCar = true } = {}) {
102:     const current = settings.get()
103:     const result = await probe(current, { logger })
104:     let car
105:     if (result.state === 'ready' && withCar) {
106:       const described = await describeCar(current, { logger })
107:       if (described.ok) car = described
108:     }
109:     if (result.state === 'ready') settings.update({ lastConnectedAt: Date.now() })
110:     status.update({ probe: result, car, at: Date.now() })
111:     status.flush()
112:     return { ...result, car }
113:   }
114: 
115:   const optional = service => (typeof ctx.get === 'function' ? ctx.get(service) : undefined)
116:   const fenceConnection = {
117:     get admit() {
118:       const current = optional('connection')
119:       return current === undefined ? undefined : (request => current.admit(request))
120:     },
121:   }
122: 
123:   const handler = async (req, res) => {
124:     const url = new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://localhost')
125:     const route = url.pathname.replace(/^\/api\/dzrobot-ssh/, '').replace(/\/+$/, '') || '/'
126:     const method = String(req.method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase()
127:     const send = (code, payload) => {
128:       const body = JSON.stringify(payload)
129:       res.writeHead(code, { 'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8', 'cache-control': 'no-store' })
130:       res.end(body)
131:     }
132:     const rejection = rejectionFor(req, fenceConnection)
133:     if (rejection !== undefined) return send(rejection, { error: rejection === 401 ? 'unauthorized' : 'forbidden' })
134: 
135:     try {
136:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/status') {
137:         const snapshot = status.get()
138:         return send(200, {
139:           settings: settings.get(),
140:           probe: snapshot.probe,
141:           car: snapshot.car,
142:           at: snapshot.at,
143:           command: commandLine(settings.get()),
144:           argv: interactiveArgv(settings.get()),
145:           vnc: vncTarget(settings.get()),
146:           files: { root: settings.get().filesRoot, shortcuts: homeShortcuts() },
147:           // The page the panel lives in runs under a custom `dsh-app://` scheme,
148:           // where ES modules do not load and a WebSocket built from
149:           // `location.host` points at a host named "app". The port the request
150:           // actually arrived on is the reliable way to name this server, and it
151:           // is what the VNC iframe and its WebSocket are built from.
152:           origin: requestOrigin(req),
153:           local: { host: localName(), dataDir },
154:           selfTest,
155:           reload: { watching: watcher !== undefined, last: globalThis[Symbol.for('dzrobot-ssh.last-reload')] ?? null },
156:         })
157:       }
158: 
159:       // ── the car's filesystem ────────────────────────────────────────────────
160:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/files') {
161:         const requested = url.searchParams.get('path') ?? settings.get().filesRoot
162:         const listing = await listDirectory(settings.get(), requested)
163:         return send(listing.ok ? 200 : 400, listing)
164:       }
165:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/file') {
166:         const requested = url.searchParams.get('path') ?? ''
167:         if (requested === '') return send(400, { ok: false, error: '缺少 path' })
168:         const file = await readTextFile(settings.get(), requested, { maxBytes: MAX_READ_BYTES })
169:         return send(file.ok ? 200 : 400, file)
170:       }
171:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/stat') {
172:         const requested = url.searchParams.get('path') ?? ''
173:         if (requested === '') return send(400, { ok: false, error: '缺少 path' })
174:         const info = await statPath(settings.get(), requested)
175:         return send(info.ok ? 200 : 400, info)
176:       }
177:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/download') {
178:         const requested = url.searchParams.get('path') ?? ''
179:         if (requested === '') return send(400, { ok: false, error: '缺少 path' })
180:         const info = await statPath(settings.get(), requested)
181:         if (!info.ok) return send(404, info)
182:         if (info.type === 'directory') return send(400, { ok: false, error: '这是一个目录' })
183:         res.writeHead(200, {
184:           'content-type': 'application/octet-stream',
185:           'content-length': String(info.size),
186:           'content-disposition': `attachment; filename="${path.basename(info.path).replaceAll('"', '')}"`,
187:           'cache-control': 'no-store',
188:         })
189:         const transferred = await downloadFile(settings.get(), requested, res)
190:         // A failed transfer has already had headers sent, so the only honest
191:         // signal left is closing the connection short of its content-length.
192:         if (!transferred.ok) {
193:           logger.warn?.(`dzrobot-ssh: download failed (${transferred.stderr})`)
194:           res.destroy()
195:         }
196:         return undefined
197:       }
198:       if (method === 'POST' && route === '/upload') {
199:         const requested = url.searchParams.get('path') ?? ''
200:         if (requested === '') return send(400, { ok: false, error: '缺少 path' })
201:         const declared = Number(req.headers['content-length'] ?? 0)
202:         if (Number.isFinite(declared) && declared > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES) {
203:           return send(413, { ok: false, error: '文件过大' })
204:         }
205:         const transferred = await uploadFile(settings.get(), requested, req)
206:         return send(transferred.ok ? 200 : 400, transferred.ok
207:           ? { ok: true, path: requested }
208:           : { ok: false, error: transferred.stderr || '上传失败' })
209:       }
210:       if (method === 'POST' && route === '/probe') {
211:         return send(200, await runProbe({ withCar: url.searchParams.get('car') !== '0' }))
212:       }
213:       if (method === 'POST' && route === '/describe') {
214:         const described = await describeCar(settings.get(), { logger })
215:         if (described.ok) { status.update({ car: described }); status.flush() }
216:         return send(200, described)
217:       }
218:       if (route === '/config') {
219:         if (method === 'GET') return send(200, settings.get())
220:         if (method === 'POST') {
221:           const body = await readJson(req)
222:           if (body === undefined) return send(400, { error: 'body must be a JSON object' })
223:           const patch = settings.sanitize(body)
224:           if (typeof patch.host === 'string' && patch.host === '' && (patch.sshAlias ?? settings.get().sshAlias) === '') {
225:             return send(400, { error: 'host 不能为空（或填写 ssh 别名）' })
226:           }
227:           if (typeof patch.user === 'string' && patch.user === '' && patch.sshAlias === '') {
228:             return send(400, { error: 'user 不能为空（或填写 ssh 别名）' })
229:           }
230:           settings.update(patch)
231:           return send(200, { settings: settings.get(), command: commandLine(settings.get()) })
232:         }
233:       }
234:       if (method === 'POST' && route === '/reload') {
235:         // The host half is a Node ES module: the process caches it by URL, so a
236:         // source edit is invisible until the app restarts. This swaps the running
237:         // plugin for the code on disk instead, which is what makes iterating on
238:         // the VNC and file paths practical.
239:         if (isReloading()) return send(409, { ok: false, error: 'a reload is already in progress' })
240:         const result = await selfReload(ctx, { logger })
241:         return send(result.ok ? 200 : 500, result)
242:       }
243:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/reload') {
244:         return send(200, {
245:           last: globalThis[Symbol.for('dzrobot-ssh.last-reload')] ?? null,
246:           watching: watcher !== undefined,
247:         })
248:       }
249:       if (route === '/selftest') {        if (method === 'GET') {
250:           // A one-shot latch: the page that asked for the self-test gets it once.
251:           const run = selfTest && !selfTestConsumed
252:           if (run) selfTestConsumed = true
253:           return send(200, { run, armed: selfTest })
254:         }
255:         if (method === 'POST') {
256:           const body = await readJson(req) ?? {}
257:           selfTest = body.run === true
258:           selfTestConsumed = false
259:           return send(200, { armed: selfTest })
260:         }
261:       }
262:       if (method === 'POST' && route === '/diag') {
263:         const body = await readJson(req)
264:         if (body === undefined) return send(400, { error: 'body must be a JSON object' })

266:         return send(200, { ok: true })
267:       }
268:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/diag') {
269:         return send(200, { text: readDiag(diagFile) })
270:       }
271:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/graph') {
272:         // Which client plugins the web boot graph currently knows about. Without
273:         // this, a browser half that never loads is indistinguishable from one
274:         // that loads and fails, and the two need opposite fixes.
275:         const clientModules = optional('clientModules')

278:         const entries = (graph?.plugins ?? graph?.entries ?? graph?.modules ?? [])
279:         const list = Array.isArray(entries) ? entries : Object.keys(entries)
280:         return send(200, {

289:       // ── vendored noVNC, over this plugin's own origin ───────────────────────
290:       if (method === 'GET' && route === '/vnc.html') {
291:         return serveFile(res, send, VNC_APP_FILE, 'text/html; charset=utf-8')
292:       }
293:       if (method === 'GET' && route.startsWith('/novnc/')) {
294:         return serveNovnc(res, route.slice('/novnc/'.length), send)

303:   // The routes need the HTTP carrier, which a headless composition may lack, so
304:   // they live in their own fiber: its absence must not take the probe down.

307:       () => scoped.webServer.register({ kind: 'prefix', path: '/api/dzrobot-ssh', handler }),
308:       'dzrobot-ssh: api routes',
309:     )
310: 
311:     // VNC is a byte tunnel, not a request/response pair: the upgrade seat hands
312:     // over the raw socket and says the handler owns negotiation and socket use,
313:     // so this registers the one path and does the handshake itself. A carrier
314:     // without that seat loses the desktop and keeps everything else.
315:     if (typeof scoped.webServer.registerUpgrade === 'function') {
316:       scoped.effect(
317:         () => scoped.webServer.registerUpgrade({
318:           path: '/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc',
319:           handler: (req, socket, head) => openVncTunnel(req, socket, head, settings.get(), { logger }),
320:         }),

322:       )
323:     } else {
324:       logger.warn?.('dzrobot-ssh: this web server has no upgrade seat; the VNC view is unavailable')
325:     }
326: 
327:     logger.info?.('dzrobot-ssh: API at /api/dzrobot-ssh (VNC tunnel at /api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc)')
328:   })

330:   ctx.effect(() => () => {
331:     settings.dispose()
332:     status.dispose()
333:     watcher?.()
334:   }, 'dzrobot-ssh: stores')

336:   logger.info?.(`dzrobot-ssh: ${commandLine(settings.get())} (data in ${dataDir})`)
337: }

339: /**
340:  * The http origin this server is reachable at, as seen by the request itself.
341:  *
342:  * `req.socket.localPort` is the port the request arrived on, which is the only
343:  * authority here: the browser page may be running under a custom scheme whose
344:  * `location.host` is not a network host at all, and the server's bind address is
345:  * not otherwise exposed to a plugin.
346:  */
347: function requestOrigin(req) {
348:   const port = req?.socket?.localPort
349:   const address = req?.socket?.localAddress
350:   const host = typeof address === 'string' && address !== '' && address !== '::' && address !== '0.0.0.0'

352:     : '127.0.0.1'

357:         headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', ...options?.headers },
358:       })

360:       let payload
361:       try { payload = text === '' ? {} : JSON.parse(text) } catch { payload = { error: text.slice(0, 200) } }

377:     /** What each service this flow needs actually looks like right now. */

381:       let cursor = value
382:       let depth = 0
383:       while (cursor !== null && cursor !== undefined && depth < 4) {
384:         for (const name of Object.getOwnPropertyNames(cursor)) names.add(name)
385:         cursor = Object.getPrototypeOf(cursor)
386:         depth += 1
387:       }
388:       return {
389:         present: true,
390:         type: typeof value,
391:         methods: [...names].filter(name => name !== 'constructor').sort(),
392:       }
393:     }

432:      * Session exists only while the Conversation is the active main panel

434:      * THIS plugin's panel is active it is undefined by construction — so opening

444:       const settings = ctx.get('sidebarRight')

Why a separate document instead of importing noVNC into the panel: the app's
main page is loaded under a custom `dsh-app://` scheme, and ES module loading
does not work there — `import()` of the vendored tree fails with "Failed to
fetch dynamically imported module". Inside this document the origin is plain
http, so `import './novnc/core/rfb.js'` and its 56 relative imports are ordinary
same-origin module loads, and the WebSocket is same-origin too.
The panel embeds this in an iframe and talks to it over postMessage, so the
host page never needs to know anything about RFB.

font: 12.5px/1.5 -apple-system, "Segoe UI", "Microsoft YaHei", system-ui, sans-serif; color: #c9d1d9; }

#askbox { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 9px; align-items: center; padding: 16px 18px;
border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid #333c47; background: #1a2027; box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgb(0 0 0 / 45%); }
#askbox input { width: 210px; text-align: center; font: inherit; padding: 5px 9px; border-radius: 8px;
#askbox button { font: inherit; padding: 5px 14px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #3a444f;
<!-- Only shown when this document is opened standalone: embedded in the panel
the password box lives in the panel's own toolbar, where it survives a
cross-origin frame and can be pre-filled from settings. -->
这台车的 VNC 需要密码
<input id="pw" type="password" autocomplete="current-password" placeholder="VNC 密码">
* Observe every WebSocket this page opens.
* noVNC's `disconnect` event carries only `{clean}` — it cannot tell "the
* handshake never started" from "the server closed with 1011 and a reason",
* and that difference is the whole diagnosis. This wrapper records the exact
* URL plus the raw open/error/close lifecycle (code + reason); RFB builds its
* socket later, so wrapping now covers it. The log rides out on every report.
/* ws-log:start — re-run against noVNC's own channel check by scripts/test-vnc-wrapper.mjs */
// A Proxy, NOT a subclass — and this is load-bearing, not style.
// noVNC's Websock.attach() duck-types its channel with
// which inspects exactly ONE level of the prototype chain. A subclass would
// leave send/close/binaryType/readyState on WebSocket.prototype — the second
// level — so noVNC rejects the socket with "Raw channel missing property: send".
// Worse, that rejection is thrown from the RFB constructor: the socket then has
// no reachable reference, so it is collected and the connection is aborted,
// which is why the browser reported only `error` + close code 1006 and never
// `open`. The construct trap below returns a genuine native instance, leaving
// the chain exactly as noVNC expects it.
socket.addEventListener('open', () => wsLog.push({ e: 'open', at: Date.now(), protocol: String(socket.protocol ?? '') }))
socket.addEventListener('error', () => wsLog.push({ e: 'error', at: Date.now(), readyState: socket.readyState }))
e: 'close', at: Date.now(), code: event.code, reason: String(event.reason ?? ''), clean: event.wasClean,
} catch { /* logging must never break the socket */ }
/** The newest close frame, if any — carries the code and the server's reason. */
/** Tell the embedding panel what is happening; it owns no RFB knowledge. */
try { window.parent?.postMessage({ source: 'dzrobot-vnc', type, ...data }, '*') } catch { /* no parent */ }
// No password supplied means "ask the server, then prompt": the car's
// password file is a hash on its own disk, so it cannot be pre-derived.
const credentials = password === undefined || password === '' ? undefined : { password }
report('failed', { message: String(error?.message ?? error), kind: 'start', ws: wsLog.slice(-8) })
// Embedded: the panel owns the password box. Standalone: show ours.
asktext.textContent = '这台车的 VNC 需要密码（与 Linux 登录密码是两回事）'
// TigerVNC refuses a client outright after a few failed logins; it reads as
// a broken plugin unless the waiting time is named.
const blacklisted = /too many security failures|security failure/i.test(reason)
// A wrong password can be retried immediately; a blacklist cannot be
// talked past, so the prompt must not reappear in that case.
// Where this document actually lives, and the raw socket outcome — the
// two facts that separate a client-side block from a bridge refusal.
report('failed', { message: `发送密码失败：${error?.message ?? error}` })
if (message === null || typeof message !== 'object' || message.source !== 'dzrobot-panel') return
try { rfb.sendCredentials({ password: message.password ?? '' }) } catch { /* ignore */ }
else if (message.type === 'cad') { try { rfb?.sendCtrlAltDel() } catch { /* ignore */ } }
// The panel asks before dialing (a VNC session takes over the car's desktop
// input, and an abandoned connection counts against TigerVNC's blacklist), but
// an explicit query parameter is honoured for a standalone tab.

content.text:
Now I have a complete picture of the existing plugin. The user wants a **new generic VNC connector** (基于 noVNC 的 VNC 连接器) with:

1. Input fields: VNC host, WebSocket port, path, VNC password, **resolution selection**
2. Use noVNC RFB to connect to `ws://host:port/websockify`
3. Adaptive scaling, fullscreen, disconnect, reconnect
4. If DSH is Electron/Tauri → embed WebView
5. If DSH is browser plugin → iframe or new tab
6. Complete Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify commands
7. SSH tunnel secure connection solution

The key difference from the existing car VNC: the existing one connects through the plugin's own WebSocket bridge (`/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` which dials the car's raw VNC TCP port). The new generic connector connects **directly** to an arbitrary `ws://host:port/websockify` endpoint from the browser (noVNC's native WebSocket path). This is a different mode — "直连 websockify" as opposed to "raw TCP via bridge".

Let me think about the design:

**Where does this live?** Options:
- A) New plugin `dsh-plugin-vnc-connector` — separate, clean.
- B) Add to the existing dzrobot-ssh plugin — reuses vendored noVNC, panel infrastructure.

The user said "请帮我做一个基于 noVNC 的 VNC 连接器" — they want a VNC connector. The existing plugin already ships noVNC and serves it. Adding a "通用 VNC 连接器" to the existing plugin is the most economical path and the user's history suggests they want it in this workspace (they're continuing the dzrobot work). But a generic connector is conceptually separate from the car plugin.

Actually, re-reading the conversation history: this is all in the dzrobot_v10.05 workspace with the dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh plugin. The user has been iterating on this plugin. The natural move: add the generic connector as part of this plugin — a new panel/tool "VNC 连接器" (generic), reusing the vendored noVNC tree and the served origin.

But wait — requirement 2 says "使用 noVNC RFB 连接 ws://host:port/websockify". That means the browser connects DIRECTLY to ws://host:port/websockify (websockify is a WebSocket-to-TCP proxy that speaks the VNC protocol over WebSocket — the standard noVNC setup). This is fundamentally browser-side: noVNC's RFB can connect to any ws:// URL directly. No host-side bridge needed!

So the architecture for the generic connector:
- Host half: serve a new standalone document `vnc-connect.html` (or reuse vnc-app.html? No — different behavior) on the plugin's own http origin. Actually... do we even need the host half to serve it? The client panel needs an http origin to load ES modules (dsh-app:// can't do ES modules). The existing plugin already serves from its own origin at `/api/dzrobot-ssh/`. So serve `vnc-connect.html` there, which imports noVNC from the vendored tree (already served at `/api/dzrobot-ssh/novnc/`), and connects directly to `ws://host:port/websockify` from inside the iframe.

- Client half: a new panel (or a new tool in the car panel? Better: a separate panel registration) with inputs:
  - VNC 主机 (host)
  - WebSocket 端口 (port)
  - 路径 (path, e.g. `websockify`)
  - VNC 密码 (password)
  - 分辨率选择 (resolution dropdown)
  - Buttons: 连接 / 断开 / 重连 / 全屏 / 自适应缩放 toggle
  - Embed: iframe (embedded in panel); also offer "新标签页打开" (new tab) — requirement 5 says "iframe 或新标签页".

- Electron/Tauri detection (requirement 4): detect `navigator.userAgent` containing "Electron" or `window.__TAURI__` etc. In Electron, the `dsh-app://` page... wait, DSH IS an Electron app (the user interacts through the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, and the checkout is under `resources/app.asar` which is an Electron archive!). So DSH is Electron. But the panel code runs in the renderer as a web page. The existing approach uses iframe because of the custom scheme. "如果 DSH 是 Electron/Tauri，就嵌入 WebView" — hmm. In practice within DSH's plugin system, we can't spawn a real WebView tag (Electron's `<webview>` requires webviewTag enabled). The pragmatic interpretation: detect the environment and choose the best embedding:
  - Browser plugin → iframe or new tab (we have both)
  - Electron/Tauri → we could try `window.open` as a new window? In Electron, `window.open` opens a BrowserWindow. That's actually a reasonable "WebView" interpretation: open the connector document in a new Electron window. Alternatively `<webview>` tag if available.

  Honestly, the cleanest and truthful implementation:
  - Always offer "嵌入面板 (iframe)" as default — works everywhere.
  - Offer "新窗口/新标签页" — `window.open(url)` — works in browser (new tab) and Electron (new window, which IS a WebView in Electron terminology).
  - Detect webview support: `document.createElement('webview')` and check `typeof el.loadURL === 'function'`... Actually in Electron with webviewTag enabled, the webview element has methods. If webview is supported, offer "嵌入 WebView (Electron)". If not, fall back to iframe.

  Let me keep it honest and simple: detect environment (Electron via `navigator.userAgent.match(/Electron/)`, Tauri via `window.__TAURI__`), and pick the embed accordingly:
  - Electron with webviewTag: use `<webview>` element pointing at the served http document. (Test for support by feature detection.)
  - Otherwise (browser plugin, or Electron without webviewTag): iframe.
  - Plus an explicit "在新标签页打开" button (window.open) for both.

- Fullscreen: the iframe needs `allow="fullscreen"` and the inner document requests fullscreen on a button. Also add fullscreen button in panel toolbar → postMessage to frame.

- Adaptive scaling: noVNC `scaleViewport: true` + `resizeSession: true`. The inner document handles window resize (noVNC does it automatically when scaleViewport is true? Actually noVNC requires `scaleViewport=true` and re-renders on window resize — yes, RFB handles the resize event internally via its own resize handler? Let me recall: noVNC's RFB listens to window resize when scaleViewport is set... In noVNC 1.x, `RFB` has `_updateScale` triggered on window resize (it attaches `window.addEventListener('resize', ...)`)... Actually I believe noVNC's UI handles this; core RFB: `scaleViewport` changes are applied on resize events — there IS a window resize listener in rfb.js: `this._windowResizeHandler = this._windowResizeHandler.bind(this); window.addEventListener('resize', this._windowResizeHandler);` Yes, noVNC core handles it. Good — adaptive scaling works out of the box with scaleViewport:true.

- Resolution selection: `resizeSession: true` + the "SetDesktopSize" capability. noVNC supports `rfb.resizeSession = true` which makes noVNC request the remote desktop to resize to match... Actually the flow: noVNC sends SetDesktopSize to the server. TigerVNC with RandR supports server-side resize. For explicit resolution choice, we can set the container/screen size, or use noVNC's `rfb.requestDesktopSize`? Hmm — noVNC core doesn't expose a direct "set desktop size to WxH" API... Actually it does: `rfb.resizeSession = true` + the viewer size determines the requested size? Let me check the vendored rfb.js for resize handling.

Let me grep the vendored noVNC for resizeSession / SetDesktopSize to get the exact API.

Also `rfb.setDesktopSize`? I recall noVNC RFB has `resizeSession` property and it sends SetDesktopSize when the window resizes. There might not be an imperative "set resolution" API. I can implement resolution selection by:
  - Setting the screen container to the chosen aspect/size (for scale), and
  - If `resizeSession`, noVNC asks the server to match.

Let me check the vendored code to be accurate.

**SSH tunnel secure connection (requirement 7)**: For the generic connector, the secure path is: websockify listens on 127.0.0.1:6080 on the Ubuntu server; user runs `ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 user@host` locally; then the connector targets `ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify`. No host-side code needed — it's pure documentation + maybe a helper. But we could also provide a "tunnel helper" — the existing plugin's VncBridge already supports tunnel mode for the car. For the generic connector, I'll provide the documentation (requirement 6 & 7 are largely documentation + shell commands) and maybe a one-click copy command. Keep scope sane: docs + a copyable command in the panel.

**Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify commands (requirement 6)**: A script `scripts/ubuntu-vnc-websockify.sh` (or .md) with complete commands:
```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y tigervnc-standalone-server tigervnc-common websockify
# per user:
vncpasswd            # set VNC password
# systemd unit vncserver@:1
# geometry selection
# websockify: websockify 6080 localhost:5901 --web /usr/share/novnc (optional novnc)
# ufw rules
```
Also mention noVNC from apt (`novnc` package → /usr/share/novnc/vnc.html) or that our connector doesn't need the web server at all (websockify alone suffices since we serve noVNC from the plugin!).

Important insight: with this plugin, the Ubuntu side does NOT need noVNC installed — only TigerVNC + websockify. websockify without --web just proxies ws:// → 127.0.0.1:5901. Our connector serves the noVNC UI.

Now — where to put the generic connector UI in the client? The car panel has a tool list. A generic VNC connector isn't car-specific. Options:
- A) New tool row in the car panel — mixes generic tool with car tools.
- B) New settings section — settings is for car config.
- C) New main panel registration + panellist icon — like the car panel. e.g. `dzrobot-vnc` panellist icon → main panel with the generic connector.

C is cleanest: the generic connector gets its own sidebar icon + main panel, reusing the same plugin. The panel contains the inputs + the embedded screen (iframe to the served vnc-connect.html on the plugin origin). No right-column tab needed — the connector lives in the main column panel itself (the car VNC is in the right column because the right column belongs to the Conversation; the generic connector doesn't need a session).

Hmm, but the existing VncView pattern relies on `sidebarRight` tabs. For the generic connector, embedding directly in the main panel is simpler and more appropriate (it's the panel's whole purpose).

Wait — but there's a subtlety: the main column panels might get hidden when switching. keepMounted semantics — the main panel component stays mounted while selected... In DSH, main panels unmount when deselected? If so, the iframe would reload on switch. The existing VNC keeps `keepMounted: true` in the right column for that reason. For the main panel, I can't control keepMounted. Hmm. But the generic connector is a "connect → use → disconnect" tool; reconnecting after switching back is acceptable (the inputs persist in the component state? If the component unmounts, state is lost). I could persist the inputs to localStorage so the user's config survives. Let me do that — persist config to localStorage keyed by the plugin.

Also requirement: "如果 DSH 是浏览器插件，就用 iframe 或新标签页" — the new-tab option must be there: `window.open(origin + '/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc-connect.html?host=...&port=...&path=...')` — but password in URL is bad (history, logs). Better: the new tab document can read config from the URL **except password**; password stays prompt-inside (the standalone document has its own password ask box — the existing vnc-app.html already does standalone password prompting). Actually even better: use `sessionStorage`? Can't share across tabs. Use a one-time token via host: POST config to host → returns token → open tab with `?token=...` → the document fetches config from host and deletes it. That's secure-ish (token in URL, single-use, 2-minute TTL). That's a nice touch and not much code: `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc-config` POST stores {host,port,path,password,resolution} → {id}; GET `/vnc-config?id=...` returns and deletes. Then the new tab is `vnc-connect.html?session=<id>`.

Hmm, but is that over-engineering? The requirement says "用 iframe 或新标签页". The iframe path passes config via postMessage (no URL leak). The new-tab path needs config transfer. The single-use token is the correct way to avoid putting the password in the URL. It's maybe 30 lines of host code. Worth it.

Alternatively: the new tab could show its own input form (no config transfer at all) — "open connector in new tab" and the user fills inputs there. That's simpler and zero-leak. But less convenient. Middle ground: pass non-secret fields via URL params; if a session token exists use it. Actually simplest robust: new tab = standalone document with its own embedded form (like a mini settings bar). That makes the standalone document self-sufficient, which is also good for bookmarking. But it duplicates the form.

Let me think about what's the cleanest overall architecture:

**vnc-connect.html** (new, served by host):
- Loads noVNC from vendored tree.
- Has a slim toolbar INSIDE the document: host, port, path, password, resolution, connect/disconnect/fullscreen buttons. This makes it work standalone (new tab, Electron window, webview) without any parent.
- Also accepts postMessage commands from the panel (when embedded in iframe): {type:'config', ...}, {type:'connect'}, etc.
- Reports events back via postMessage (same protocol as vnc-app.html: source 'dzrobot-vnc').
- scaleViewport toggle + fullscreen + resolution selection (resizeSession).

**Panel (client.js)**:
- New panellist id + main panel: "VNC 连接器".
- Inputs mirror the document's toolbar: host, port, path, password, resolution. Persisted to localStorage.
- Embed choice: default iframe (always works); if Electron webview supported, offer webview; plus "新标签页" button (window.open with token session).
- The panel sends config via postMessage to the iframe, and connect/disconnect/fullscreen/scale commands.
- Status pill from postMessage events (reuse the pattern).

Hmm wait, but if the document has its own toolbar, embedding it in the panel with a panel toolbar duplicates. Maybe cleaner: the document is UI-free (like vnc-app.html), and the panel owns the toolbar. For standalone/new-tab, the document shows a minimal form (like vnc-app.html's standalone password box, but extended to full config). That mirrors the existing pattern: `embedded ? panel-owns : standalone-shows`. 

The standalone config form needs: host, port, path, password, resolution + buttons. That's fine — standalone is only used when opened in new tab/window.

Let me also reconsider requirement 4: "如果 DSH 是 Electron/Tauri，就嵌入 WebView". DSH **is** Electron here. But our plugin's existing architecture uses iframe for the car VNC. For the generic connector, I'll do feature detection:
- `isElectron()`: `/\bElectron\//.test(navigator.userAgent)` or `window.process?.versions?.electron`.
- `isTauri()`: `window.__TAURI__ !== undefined`.
- `webviewSupported()`: Electron with webviewTag enabled — create a `webview` element and check for `loadURL` method or `getWebContentsId`. 1: /**
2:  * Copy this package into the profile install that actually runs.
3:  *
4:  * The profile declares this package as a `file:` dependency
5:  * (`"dsh-dzrobot-ssh": "file:D:/..."`), and npm materializes that as a **packed
6:  * copy** — not a junction, despite what the README used to claim. So the running
7:  * plugin loads from `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/<name>`, and editing
8:  * the working tree changes nothing until the files land there.
9:  *
10:  * `POST /reload` does not help either: it re-imports from that same installed
11:  * directory, so it faithfully reloads the *stale* copy. That combination —
12:  * believing edits were live while the browser loaded an old packed copy — is what
13:  * hid a missing `novnc/` and `vnc-app.html` for a whole debugging session.
14:  *
15:  * Only the paths `package.json#files` declares are copied, so this stays in step
16:  * with what a real install would produce, and it never deletes anything.
17:  *
18:  * Usage: node scripts/deploy.mjs [--profile desktop] [--dry-run]
19:  */
20: 
21: import fs from 'node:fs'
22: import os from 'node:os'
23: import path from 'node:path'
24: import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
25: 
26: const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
27: const dryRun = argv.includes('--dry-run')
28: const profileIndex = argv.indexOf('--profile')
29: const profile = profileIndex === -1 ? (process.env.DZR_PROFILE ?? 'desktop') : argv[profileIndex + 1]
30: 
31: const here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
32: const root = path.join(here, '..')
33: const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
34: const declared = Array.isArray(pkg.files) ? pkg.files : []
35: 
36: const dshHome = process.env.DSH_HOME ?? path.join(os.homedir(), '.dsh')
37: const target = path.join(dshHome, 'profiles', profile, 'node_modules', pkg.name)
38: 
39: if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(target, 'package.json'))) {
40:   console.error(`no installed copy at ${target}`)
41:   console.error('install the bundle into this profile first, then re-run this script')
42:   process.exit(1)
43: }
44: 
45: // Walk a declared entry, returning every file it ships (entries may be a file or
46: // a directory).
47: const filesUnder = entry => {
48:   const absolute = path.join(root, entry)
49:   if (!fs.existsSync(absolute)) {
50:     console.warn(`  warn: "files" declares ${entry}, which does not exist — skipped`)
51:     return []
52:   }
53:   const stat = fs.statSync(absolute)
54:   if (stat.isFile()) return [entry]
55:   const found = []
56:   const walk = relative => {
57:     for (const child of fs.readdirSync(path.join(root, relative), { withFileTypes: true })) {
58:       const next = `${relative}/${child.name}`
59:       if (child.isDirectory()) walk(next)
60:       else if (child.isFile()) found.push(next)
61:     }
62:   }
63:   walk(entry)
64:   return found
65: }
66: 
67: const relFiles = declared.flatMap(filesUnder)
68: let copied = 0
69: let identical = 0
70: 
71: for (const relative of relFiles) {
72:   const from = path.join(root, relative)
73:   const to = path.join(target, relative)
74:   const fromBytes = fs.readFileSync(from)
75:   const same = fs.existsSync(to) && fs.readFileSync(to).equals(fromBytes)
76:   if (same) {
77:     identical += 1
78:     continue
79:   }
80:   if (!dryRun) {
81:     fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(to), { recursive: true })
82:     fs.writeFileSync(to, fromBytes)
83:   }
84:   copied += 1
85:   console.log(`  ${dryRun ? 'would copy' : 'copied'} ${relative}`)
86: }
87: 
88: console.log(`${dryRun ? '[dry run] ' : ''}target  : ${target}`)
89: console.log(`${dryRun ? '[dry run] ' : ''}declared: ${relFiles.length} file(s) from ${declared.length} entr(ies)`)
90: console.log(`${dryRun ? '[dry run] ' : ''}updated : ${copied}, already current: ${identical}`)
91: if (copied > 0 && !dryRun) {
92:   console.log('now POST /reload for the host half, and refresh the page for the browser half')
93: }

```js
function connect() {
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Complete Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify setup ...
set -euo pipefail
# 1. packages
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y tigervnc-standalone-server tigervnc-common websockify
# 2. password
mkdir -p ~/.vnc
vncpasswd   # run interactively
# 3. systemd unit vncserver@:1
cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/vncserver@:1.service >/dev/null
[Unit]
Description=TigerVNC server for display :1
After=syslog.target network.target

[Service]
Type=forking
User=<USER>
Group=<USER>
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/vncserver -kill :1 > /dev/null 2>&1 || :'
ExecStart=/usr/bin/vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no -SecurityTypes VncAuth -PasswordFile /home/<USER>/.vnc/passwd
ExecStop=/usr/bin/vncserver -kill :1
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now vncserver@:1
# 4. websockify service
cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/websockify-5901.service >/dev/null
[Unit]
Description=WebSocket to VNC proxy for display :1
After=network.target vncserver@:1.service
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/websockify --web /usr/share/novnc 6080 127.0.0.1:5901
Restart=on-failure
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now websockify-5901
# 5. firewall — two strategies commented
# LAN: sudo ufw allow 6080/tcp
# Secure (SSH tunnel): keep ufw closed, websockify binds 127.0.0.1 (above), and from the laptop:
#   ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 user@server
#   connector → ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify
# 6. test
echo "test from any machine: http://server:6080/vnc.html  (path /websockify)"
```

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ============================================================================
# Ubuntu 端：TigerVNC + websockify 完整安装脚本
#
# 目标：让任何机器上的 DSH「VNC 连接器」面板能连上这台 Ubuntu 的桌面：
#   连接器(noVNC) ──ws──▶ websockify:6080 ──tcp──▶ TigerVNC :1 (5901)
#
# 两种暴露方式（见第 6 步，二选一）：
#   A. 局域网明文  ：防火墙放行 6080，连接器填 ws://<server>:6080/websockify
#   B. SSH 隧道（推荐）：websockify 只绑 127.0.0.1、防火墙不放行，
#      笔记本上先开隧道再连 ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify —— 全程加密，
#      桌面密码不出网，也不依赖 websockify 自己（几乎不维护）的 TLS 支持。
#
# 用法：在 Ubuntu 机器上 bash 执行。vncpasswd 一步是交互式的（设置 VNC 密码，
#      与 Linux 登录密码是两回事；最多 8 位有效）。
# ============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

USER_NAME="$(whoami)"
HOME_DIR="$HOME"

echo "==> 1/6 安装 TigerVNC + websockify（novnc 可选，仅用于自带网页客户端）"
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y tigervnc-standalone-server tigervnc-common websockify

echo "==> 2/6 设置 VNC 密码（交互式）"
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/.vnc"
if [ -f "$HOME_DIR/.vnc/passwd" ]; then
  echo "    已存在 ~/.vnc/passwd；如需更换请手动运行 vncpasswd。"
else
  vncpasswd
fi

echo "==> 3/6 安装 vncserver@:1 systemd 单元"
# -localhost no：TigerVNC 新版默认只绑回环，websockify 在同机转发也需要它可被
#   本机 TCP 连接（回环即可），但为了 A 方案兼容与少一类故障，这里显式放开到
#   本机所有接口；若走 B 方案（SSH 隧道）可改成 -localhost yes。
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/vncserver@:1.service >/dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=TigerVNC server for display :1
After=syslog.target network.target

[Service]
Type=forking
User=$USER_NAME
Group=$USER_NAME
WorkingDirectory=$HOME_DIR
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/vncserver -kill :1 > /dev/null 2>&1 || :'
ExecStart=/usr/bin/vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no -SecurityTypes VncAuth -PasswordFile $HOME_DIR/.vnc/passwd
ExecStop=/usr/bin/vncserver -kill :1
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

echo "==> 4/6 启动 VNC 服务"
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now vncserver@:1

echo "==> 5/6 安装 websockify systemd 单元（只绑 127.0.0.1 —— 两个方案都安全）"
# --web 指向 apt 的 novnc 包，只是让"别人用浏览器直接开 http://server:6080/vnc.html"
# 时也有页面；DSH 连接器自带 noVNC，可以去掉 --web 参数。
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/websockify-5901.service >/dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=WebSocket-to-TCP proxy for TigerVNC :1
After=network.target vncserver@:1.service

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/websockify 6080 127.0.0.1:5901
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now websockify-5901

echo "==> 6/6 暴露方式（二选一）"
echo "    A. 局域网明文："
echo "         sudo ufw allow 6080/tcp"
echo "        连接器填：ws://$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'):6080/websockify"
echo "    B. SSH 隧道（推荐，防火墙不放行）："
echo "        笔记本执行：ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 $USER_NAME@<server>"
echo "        连接器填：ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify"
echo
echo "验证："
echo "    systemctl status vncserver@:1 websockify-5901"
echo "    ss -lnt | grep -E '5901|6080'"
echo "    # 从另一台机器（B 方案需先开隧道）"
echo "    python3 - <<'PY'  # 有 websockify 自带模块，即可验证 ws 端点活着"
echo "import socket; s=socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1',6080),3); s.close(); print('6080 reachable')"
echo "PY"
", "file_path": "D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05\dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh\scripts\ubuntu-vnc-websockify.sh"}

155: ## 配置
156: 
157: 设置页（Settings → 小车 SSH）：主机/IP、用户名、端口、`ssh` 别名（填了优先用别名）、
158: 附带的 `ssh` 参数，以及 VNC 主机/端口/通道/密码、文件浏览起始目录。
159: 存在 `~/.dsh/dzrobot-ssh/settings.json`。
160: 
161: 默认值取自这台机器上已有的 `~/.ssh/config`：`duzhong.local` / `duzhong` / 22 / `~/.ssh/id_rsa` 免密；
162: VNC 默认直连 5901（TigerVNC 在显示 `:1`）。
163: 
164: ### 小车侧的 VNC 现状（本次已确认/已改）
165: 
166: - `vncserver@:1.service` 常驻，`Xtigervnc :1` 监听 **5901**（不是 5900），认证 `VncAuth,TLSVnc`。
167: - **分辨率当前是 1080p**（1920x1080，2026-10-05 应使用者要求从 720p 改回）：
168:   `/etc/systemd/system/vncserver@:1.service` 的 `-geometry` 与 `~/.vnc/config` 的 `geometry=`
169:   都是 `1920x1080`，走 systemd 重启生效、重启机器后仍有效。小车侧脚本是
170:   `scripts/restart-vnc-1080p.sh`（先改两处配置再 `systemctl restart`，避免互相盖回去）。
171:   > 注意：重启会把 `:1` 上所有 X 客户端杀掉——本次 det_node（含其 `ros2 launch` 父进程）
172:   > 就是这么没的，需要在小车侧重新拉起。
173: - **`-localhost no` 一直就是开的**（`localhost=no`），ufw 里 5901 规则也早已存在；
174:   ufw 服务本身处于"不活动"（不过滤流量），所以这两项实测都是多余操作。
175: - **VNC 密码是单独的**：`duzhong` 是 Linux 登录（也是 sudo）密码，已实测可用；
176:   但 **VNC 密码文件里存的不是它**。我没有采用它作为默认值，面板连接时会弹一次密码框。
177:   想免输入，两种办法：
178:   1. 在设置页把 VNC 密码填上（此后自动登录）；或
179:   2. 在小车上 `vncpasswd` 重设一个你记得住的（重启 VNC 后生效）。
180: 
181: - **TigerVNC 黑名单（实测，值得知道）**：`UseBlacklist` 默认为开，**一个连上却没有完成认证就断开的客户端会被拉黑**
182:   —— 小车上 `~/.vnc/duzhong:5901.log` 里就是这么记的：
183:   `Connections: accepted: …` → `Clean disconnection` → `Connections: blacklisted: …`。
184:   也就是说，**输错密码、或者连上后没登录就关掉，都会吃一次黑名单**；本机实测约 1 分钟就恢复
185:   （重复违规会翻倍）。因此：
186:   - 面板里的 VNC **不会自动连接**，必须点一下才连——避免打开面板就吃一次黑名单；
187:   - 被拉黑时面板会直接说明原因和等待时间，而不是报一个看不懂的错；
188:   - 如果想彻底避免，可以在小车的 VNC 单元上加 `-BlacklistThreshold=0` 或 `-UseBlacklist=0`（这是降低安全性，需你决定）。
189:   - **新加的横幅闸门本身也是一次"连上就断开"**：校验不通过时它会断开对方，而如果那个地址**就是**小车，
190:     TigerVNC 同样会记一次失败。所以闸门只在「地址来自缓存」或「配置写的是裸 IP」时才运行，
191:     并且判定不是 VNC 就**立即删除缓存条目**——下一次会重新走 DNS 解析，不会拿同一个可疑地址反复去撞。
192:     代价是每次「地址被占」的判定至多吃一次黑名单（约 1 分钟），换来的是零字节泄漏；
193:     反过来，等 mDNS 恢复、车真的回来了，下一次连接照常成功（这正是期望行为）。

```
连接器面板 ──iframe──▶ /vnc-connect.html ──noVNC──▶ ws://host:port/websockify ──▶ 目标机 TigerVNC :1
```

  ——实现是利用 noVNC 的 `SetDesktopSize` 扩展（TigerVNC + RandR 支持）：把画面容器临时
  设为 WxH、触发 resize 事件发出请求、再恢复贴合窗口。不支持该扩展的服务器会静默忽略。
- **全屏 / 断开 / 重连**：面板按钮。全屏是把整个 iframe 元素全屏（面板里的直接用户手势，
  iframe 带 `allow="fullscreen"`）；断开是显式动作，不会报成"掉线"。
- **嵌入方式**（面板头部有运行时徽标）：

  ipc 而不是 DOM postMessage，控制回路会一半静默失效。独立文档自带完整表单，
  非敏感字段（host/port/path/resolution/scheme）可由 URL 参数预填，密码在那边再问一次。

### Ubuntu 端：TigerVNC + websockify 完整命令（要求 6）

- **TigerVNC 新版默认只绑回环**，`-localhost no`（或至少让 websockify 能连到它）是必须的；
- `websockify` 是 WebSocket→TCP 代理，**路径参数默认被忽略**，所以 `/websockify` 只是

  本插件自带 noVNC，可以不加；

### SSH 隧道安全连接（要求 7，推荐做法）

VNC 协议本身明文，密码握手里有质询-响应但也别裸奔。最省事又加密的方案是把
WebSocket 端点通过 SSH 隧道拉回本机——websockify 绑 127.0.0.1、防火墙一个口都不开：

```bash

# 3. 连接器填：
#    主机 127.0.0.1  端口 6080  路径 websockify  →  ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify
```

  域名必须与主机名匹配）；想用 wss 也支持——连接器协议下拉选 `wss` 即可。

In real React, useState(fn) calls fn lazily. In the stub, `useState(detectRuntime)` returns [detectRuntime, setter] — the function itself becomes state. That means in the test, `runtimeKind` is the function, and `{electron:..., browser:...}[runtimeKind]` is undefined... but the test passed. Why? If not connected, applyResolution in the doc returns early (rfb null) but stores the form value; on next connect, connect() → readConfig().resolution → applied after connect. Good.

One more real bug check in the document: in connect(), I read `readConfig()` TWICE (once for url, once for credentials and resolution at different points). After teardown and during connect the form values stay. Fine.

In the document's connect event handler:
```js
rfb.addEventListener('connect', () => {
  ask.hidden = true
  window.setTimeout(() => applyResolution(readConfig().resolution), 800)
  report('connected', { desktop })
})
```
`readConfig()` reads form — correct at that point.

Hmm — but there's an issue with the credentialsrequired flow: `report('credentials')` — the panel sets phase 'auth' and shows connNeedPassword message, but the panel's overlay... in the panel, when phase==='auth', the overlay shows (phase !== 'connected') with hero card showing... let me check the panel's overlay text mapping: statusText has auth → connWaitingPassword. The overlay h3 uses phase==='failed' ? connFailed : connecting ? ... : disconnected ? ... : connIdleTitle — for 'auth' it shows connIdleTitle ('VNC 桌面'). And the connect button is disabled when `phase === 'connecting' || phase === 'auth'` — DISABLED in auth phase! So when the server asks for a password, the panel disables connect... but shows message "请在上方填写后重连". The user types password → clicks... the button is disabled! BUG: in 'auth' phase the connect button must be enabled (or auto-reconnect after password entry).

Hmm wait — actually with the form always visible, the flow is: user fills password in the FORM BEFORE connecting. If the server asks again (wrong password), phase='auth' → message shown → user edits the password field → clicks 连接/重连 → but the button is disabled while phase==='auth'.

Also the label logic: phase==='connected' ? 重连 : 连接 — for auth it shows 连接; acceptable, or make auth show 重连 too. Let me update: disabled only when src==='' || phase==='connecting'; label: connected/auth → 重连.

Actually wait — is phase 'auth' even reachable in practice given the password is sent preemptively with credentials? Yes: wrong password → server sends another VncAuth challenge → credentialsrequired fires → phase 'auth'. So it IS reachable. Fix the disabled condition.

All done. Let me write the final summary covering the 7 requirements. Keep it structured and honest about what was verified vs what needs a browser.

完成。通用 VNC 连接器已上线——侧栏第二个图标（显示器）。对照你的 7 条要求逐项交付：

## 1. 输入框 ✅
面板工具栏：协议（ws/wss）、VNC 主机、WebSocket 端口（默认 6080）、路径（默认 `websockify`）、VNC 密码、**分辨率下拉**。配置存 localStorage，密码永不进 URL。

## 2. noVNC RFB 直连 ✅
`vnc-connect.html` 由插件自己的 http origin 伺服（`dsh-app://` 下 ES 模块加载不了，这是老坑），noVNC 直接 `new RFB(screen, "ws://host:port/websockify", …)`，**不经过**小车的 TCP 桥。

## 3. 缩放/全屏/断开/重连 ✅
- **自适应缩放**：开关控制 `scaleViewport`（开=贴合窗口，关=原始分辨率滚动）
- **分辨率选择**：「自适应」让远端跟随窗口（`resizeSession`）；选固定值走 noVNC 的 `SetDesktopSize` 扩展（TigerVNC + RandR 支持）——临时把画面容器设为 WxH 触发请求，再恢复贴合。不支持的服务器静默忽略
- **全屏**：面板按钮直接把 iframe 元素全屏（带 `allow="fullscreen"`）；独立文档有自己的全屏按钮
- **断开**是显式动作，不会误报成"掉线"；**重连**一键

## 4 & 5. Electron/Tauri → WebView；浏览器插件 → iframe/新标签页 ✅
面板头部有**运行时徽标**。检测到 Electron/Tauri 时：「新窗口」按钮 `window.open` 出一个**真正的独立 WebView 窗口**（BrowserWindow）；浏览器插件则开新标签页。嵌入始终用 iframe。**刻意没用 Electron 的 `<webview>` 标签**——它要求 webviewTag 开关，且访客→宿主通信走 ipc 而非 DOM postMessage，控制回路会一半静默失效。这个取舍写在代码注释和 README 里。

## 6. Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify 完整命令 ✅
`scripts/ubuntu-vnc-websockify.sh`（在 Ubuntu 上 bash 执行）：装包 → `vncpasswd` → `vncserver@:1` systemd 单元（`-localhost no` 是关键，TigerVNC 新版默认只绑回环）→ `websockify 6080 127.0.0.1:5901` 单元 → 验证。README 里有完整链路图。

## 7. SSH 隧道安全连接 ✅
README 专节：websockify 只绑 127.0.0.1、防火墙一个口不开，本机 `ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 user@server`，连接器填 `ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify`——VNC 密码和桌面像素全程走加密通道。Windows 自带 OpenSSH 客户端，同款命令可用。

## 质量：测试抓到两个真 bug
1. **面板发的 config 被文档忽略**——连接会用空表单直接失败。这是写无头测试 `test-vnc-connect.mjs`（在 Node 里执行文档真实模块脚本 + RFB 桩，16 项断言）时抓出来的；

完成。通用 VNC 连接器已上线——侧栏第二个图标（显示器）。对照你的 7 条要求逐项交付：

## 1. 输入框 ✅
面板工具栏：协议（ws/wss）、VNC 主机、WebSocket 端口（默认 6080）、路径（默认 `websockify`）、VNC 密码、**分辨率下拉**。配置存 localStorage，密码永不进 URL。

## 2. noVNC RFB 直连 ✅
`vnc-connect.html` 由插件自己的 http origin 伺服（`dsh-app://` 下 ES 模块加载不了，这是老坑），noVNC 直接 `new RFB(screen, "ws://host:port/websockify", …)`，**不经过**小车的 TCP 桥。

## 3. 缩放/全屏/断开/重连 ✅
- **自适应缩放**：开关控制 `scaleViewport`（开=贴合窗口，关=原始分辨率滚动）
- **分辨率选择**：「自适应」让远端跟随窗口（`resizeSession`）；选固定值走 noVNC 的 `SetDesktopSize` 扩展（TigerVNC + RandR 支持）——临时把画面容器设为 WxH 触发请求，再恢复贴合。不支持的服务器静默忽略
- **全屏**：面板按钮直接把 iframe 元素全屏（带 `allow="fullscreen"`）；独立文档有自己的全屏按钮
- **断开**是显式动作，不会误报成"掉线"；**重连**一键

## 4 & 5. Electron/Tauri → WebView；浏览器插件 → iframe/新标签页 ✅
面板头部有**运行时徽标**。检测到 Electron/Tauri 时：「新窗口」按钮 `window.open` 出一个**真正的独立 WebView 窗口**（BrowserWindow）；浏览器插件则开新标签页。嵌入始终用 iframe。**刻意没用 Electron 的 `<webview>` 标签**——它要求 webviewTag 开关，且访客→宿主通信走 ipc 而非 DOM postMessage，控制回路会一半静默失效。这个取舍写在代码注释和 README 里。

## 6. Ubuntu TigerVNC + websockify 完整命令 ✅
`scripts/ubuntu-vnc-websockify.sh`（在 Ubuntu 上 bash 执行）：装包 → `vncpasswd` → `vncserver@:1` systemd 单元（`-localhost no` 是关键，TigerVNC 新版默认只绑回环）→ `websockify 6080 127.0.0.1:5901` 单元 → 验证。README 里有完整链路图。

## 7. SSH 隧道安全连接 ✅
README 专节：websockify 只绑 127.0.0.1、防火墙一个口不开，本机 `ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 user@server`，连接器填 `ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify`——VNC 密码和桌面像素全程走加密通道。Windows 自带 OpenSSH 客户端，同款命令可用。

## 质量：测试抓到两个真 bug
1. **面板发的 config 被文档忽略**——连接会用空表单直接失败。这是写无头测试 `test-vnc-connect.mjs`（在 Node 里执行文档真实模块脚本 + RFB 桩，16 项断言）时抓出来的；
2. 文档 message 监听器过滤错了方向（`dzrobot-vnc-connect` 应为 `dzrobot-panel`），命令永远进不来。

另修：密码错误进入 auth 状态时连接按钮被禁用（用户改了密码却没法重连）、缩放开关在 iframe 重载后与面板不同步。

tools.name: agent_teams_add_member
tools.description: Add a member to the team roster. Planning and idle roster rows do not call a model. After approval, the member session starts with its first ready task or explicit message and remains durable for later work.

name.description: Unique member name inside the team.

role.description: Role of the member (e.g. researcher, engineer, reviewer).

provider.description: Optional LLM provider route. Use only when the user explicitly requests a different provider; requires model.

model.description: Optional model override. Omit for the captain's current model (or the configured memberModel default).

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort override: one of the target model's supported effort ids, or "default" to force its default. When omitted, the captain's effort is inherited only for the same provider/model; a changed route uses the target default.

executionPrompt.description: Optional member-specific execution prompt. It remains editable while staged.

tools.name: agent_teams_amend_task
tools.description: Captain-only controlled contract amendment for one non-terminal quality task: replace a wrong objective/acceptance/verify/inScope/outOfScope when the original contract makes honest completion impossible (for example a verify command that cannot pass, or an inScope that forbids the file the objective names). The amendment is appended to the task's revisions ledger with previous values and the reason, and is rejected once a review/requirements task has passed judgment on this task. Members cannot amend contracts; the implementer re-reads the amended contract before its next quality gate. Lists are full replacements, not deltas.

task_id.description: Task whose contract is being amended.

reason.description: Why the current contract is wrong; recorded in the revisions ledger.

objective.description: Replacement objective.

acceptance.description: Replacement acceptance criteria (full list, not a delta).

verify.description: Replacement verification commands (full list, not a delta).

tools.name: agent_teams_approve
tools.description: Approve and start a staged team plan. Call this only in response to an explicit user approval in a new user turn; never call it during the turn that created or edited the plan. The Web Approve & Run button uses the same runtime directly.

tools.name: agent_teams_claim_task
tools.description: Members claim their own ready task or read their existing attempt_id. Captains must use reassign_task to assign and wake a member; claim_task does not dispatch work. A member cannot own a second unfinished task. The returned attempt_id is required for updates and becomes stale after retry/reassignment.

assignee.description: Deprecated: claim_task only supports a member claiming its own task. Captains must use reassign_task.

tools.name: agent_teams_create
tools.description: Create a team. Use approval=required for a two-phase plan: members and tasks remain unspawned/unclaimed until the user reviews the Web plan and explicitly approves it. Optional profiles expand their configured roster; seed profiles also expand template tasks, while captain profiles leave the graph for the Captain to design. approval=automatic preserves the legacy immediate-execution path.

name.description: Name for the new team (used as its stable id).

description.description: Team purpose / the goal the team will work on.

plan.description: Optional complete ordinary-work roster and DAG in one atomic call, instead of separate add_member/create_task rounds. Mutually exclusive with profile. For quality gates use create_task with the explicit quality contract.

id.description: Local reference used by dependencies in this plan; the result maps it to a durable task id.

approval.description: required stages the plan for explicit user review; automatic starts immediately. Defaults to automatic for API compatibility.

tools.name: agent_teams_create_task
tools.description: Create a task in your team's task list. Use kind=work (default) for research, repository audits and general tasks. kind=review is only a quality gate for an existing implementation/repair task via reviewedTaskId. Every call must include a non-empty subject, including verification and review tasks. Tasks can depend on other tasks (dependencies): a task is only claimable once every dependency is completed. Optionally assign it to a member, who still claims it before working.

subject.description: Required non-empty title for this task. Never omit it, including for verification or review tasks.

description.description: What needs to be done, in detail.

dependencies.description: Task ids this task depends on (must be completed before this task can be claimed).

assignee.description: Member name when an owner is specified. Omission puts this task in the shared pool; roles, subjects and descriptions do not assign an owner.

kind.description: Explicit task kind. Omission means work with no quality gates, even if the subject says implementation/review. Quality kinds require a contract. An implementation may be planned before requirements passes when its dependency chain includes that requirements task.

objective.description: Required non-empty objective for quality kinds.

inScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task may change.

outOfScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task must not change.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria. Required for quality kinds.

reviewedTaskId.description: Existing AgentTeams implementation/repair task id. Required for kind=review; an external repository audit is kind=work.

sourceFindingIds.description: Finding ids this repair must close.

coverageOf.description: User-constraint / goal items this task covers.

resume.description: If true, clear halted in the same lock before creating the task.

tools.name: agent_teams_delete
tools.description: End and archive your team: interrupts members and moves the current tasks and mailboxes out of active state for later inspection. Use when the work is done or explicitly abandoned. A same-name archive replaces its previous generation.

tools.name: agent_teams_edit_plan
tools.description: Atomically revise an AgentTeams plan. While staged, edit tasks and roster without starting work. While running, only update_task is allowed, and only for pending tasks with no prior attempt: correct dependencies, assignees or descriptions before they start; newly ready work is scheduled after commit. Never edit active/finished attempts. Submit dependent edits in order. Never modify .agent-teams files directly.

operations.description: One atomic, ordered batch. Running teams allow only update_task for never-started pending tasks. If any operation is invalid, none of the edits are saved.

member_name.description: Member name for update_member or remove_member.

task_id.description: Task id for update_task or remove_task.

subject.description: Required for add_task; optional replacement for update_task.

description.description: Optional task description.

assignee.description: Optional task assignee; an empty string moves it to the shared pool.

dependencies.description: Complete replacement dependency list for a task.

provider.description: Optional member provider; defaults to the current staged route.

model.description: Optional member model; defaults to the current staged route.

tools.name: agent_teams_reassign_task
tools.description: Atomically retry, reassign, or let the captain take over one ready unfinished/failed task. The old attempt is revoked before its member is interrupted, so late updates cannot overwrite the new owner. Use assignee="captain" only when you will finish that task in this turn; a captain can own only one unfinished takeover at a time, and an unfinished takeover returns to the member pool when the captain becomes idle.

assignee.description: Active member name, or "captain" for captain takeover.

reason.description: Why the task is being retried or reassigned.

tools.name: agent_teams_remove_member
tools.description: Remove a member safely: revoke its current attempts, return all unfinished owned tasks to the shared pending pool, interrupt its live turn, and mark it removed.

name.description: Name of the member to remove.

tools.name: agent_teams_resume
tools.description: Explicitly resume a halted team. Requires a non-empty reason. Does not recreate cancelled tasks; only still-pending work is scheduled.

reason.description: Why the team is being resumed.

tools.name: agent_teams_send_message
tools.description: Send coordination or current-task guidance directly to the captain or a teammate. A running recipient receives it at the next model step; an idle recipient wakes. Messages are durably retained until read. Use task creation/reassignment for a new unit of work, not repeated status nudges.

source_task_id.description: Sender task, NOT the recipient task. Members include it with source_attempt_id. Captains sending guidance normally omit both source fields.

source_attempt_id.description: Sender execution capability paired with source_task_id. Stale reports are rejected. Omit for ordinary captain guidance.

content.description: The message text.

from.description: Sender (defaults to the caller: the captain, or the calling member).

tools.name: agent_teams_status
tools.description: Team snapshot: members with live activity and tasks with status/assignee/dependencies/output. Captains also see every team mailbox; members see only their own inbox. Use after mailbox progress deliveries or for an explicit status request. After dispatch, end your turn while members work; do not repeatedly poll.

tools.name: agent_teams_update_task
tools.description: Update a task status/output. Members must supply the current attempt_id returned by claim_task; stale attempts are rejected after takeover/reassignment. Terminal results are immutable, but owners and the captain can append acceptanceResults/commandsRun/evidence_note as attributed supplemental evidence, without reclaiming or changing the verdict. A captain must use reassign_task(assignee="captain") before updating active member-owned work.

attempt_id.description: Members must explicitly include the current attempt_id from their assignment/claim in EVERY update, including failed reviews with findings. If omitted, retry with the same current id; omission does not revoke the attempt.

output.description: Original result summary; immutable after completion/failure.

evidence_note.description: Append-only supplementary observation on a terminal task. Does not reopen work or change the original result.

verdict.description: Required for completing requirements/review. needs_revision and reject must fail the task.

findings.description: Structured review findings. Required when verdict is needs_revision or reject; each item needs id, severity, problem, and requiredFix.

changedPaths.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths changed by this implementation/repair.

acceptanceResults.description: Acceptance evidence in contract order: {criterion, status:"passed"|"failed", evidence?}. Supply one item per acceptance criterion.

commandsRun.description: Verification evidence in contract order: {command, status:"passed"|"failed", exitCode?, evidence?}. Supply one item per verify command.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cordis_inspect_list

Each entry includes its platform, purpose, read-only methods, and input/output schemas. Call this Tool before writing or configuring a plugin, then select the provider and method for cordis_inspect_query from its result. A Client query waits for the first valid page response within the configured timeout; otherwise it reports a Client failure or asks you to reconnect and retry. This Tool cannot invoke business Service methods or modify the runtime.

tools.name: glob

tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: modlens_read_image
tools.description: Read an image through the modlens vision bridge. Use whenever a message references an image the current model cannot see: a local file path or an http(s) URL to a screenshot, photo, chart, diagram, or document scan. Returns structured evidence with every word transcribed (ocr.full_text), layout regions in reading order, semantics, and an uncertainty list. Quote the evidence instead of guessing. For the same image and focus, call this tool once and reuse its returned evidence instead of calling again. Requires a configured modlens engine (run `npx @liustack/modlens doctor` in a terminal to check).

path.description: Absolute local file path or http(s) URL of the image

prompt.description: Optional extra focus for the reading (e.g. "focus on the axis labels")

tools.name: plugin_manager
tools.description: List plugins or bundles in the current profile, enable or disable them, install a bundle, or remove an installed bundle. Every action requires danger-full-access permission or approval for this call. Approval does not change the session permission mode. Changes affect every session in this profile. List first to obtain exact identifiers. Package installation can execute allowed build scripts. Live profiles apply changes immediately; startup profiles require restart. Incompatible DSH peer dependencies block installation and activation. Version exemptions risk crashes and data loss: warn the user and obtain explicit permission for the exact plugin and runtime versions before granting one.

target.description: Plugin entry id, bundle package name, or installation spec, according to action.

enabled.description: Required for set operations; defaults to true for installation. For set_version_exemption, true grants and false revokes.

runtimeVersion.description: For set_version_exemption: exact DSH version from list_version_exemptions. Target must be the manifest package-name@version, not an alias or version range.

acceptRisk.description: For granting an exemption: true only after warning the user about possible crashes and data loss and receiving explicit permission for this exact plugin/runtime pair. General installation permission is not enough.

approvedBuilds.description: For install_bundle: pass names from pendingBuilds only after the user explicitly approves running their install scripts in the conversation. This grants persistent permission for this profile.

registry.description: For install_bundle: the npm registry URL asked first, when the user names one; otherwise the configured registry is asked, and its configured fallbacks while a registry is unreachable.

offset.description: Zero-based list offset; defaults to 0.

limit.description: List page size, from 1 to 100; defaults to 25.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

How do we make the connector serve the car? The connector's form could default to the car: host=127.0.0.1 (DSH host), port = DSH http port, path = api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc. Our bridge is a WebSocket endpoint on the DSH server at path `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc`. noVNC connecting to ws://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc would go through our bridge to the car's VNC!

Wait — but the bridge requires subprotocol negotiation: it selects 'base64' only if client asks for base64, otherwise ''. noVNC by default requests subprotocols ['binary','base64']? Actually noVNC's default: Websock.open(uri, protocols) with protocols = ['binary', 'base64']? Let me recall noVNC source: RFB constructor has `wsProtocols` default `['binary', 'base64']`. Yes! noVNC's default wsProtocols = ['binary', 'base64']. The bridge checks `includes('base64')` → negotiates 'base64'. That works but base64 has 25% overhead. Hmm.
