Now I have the full picture. Plan of edits:

**Edit 1**: `makeVncTabShell` (line 1364): replace `makeVncView` with `makeVncConnectorPanel`. The connector panel doesn't take props. So:
```js
return h('div', { className: 'dzr_tabroot' },
  h(makeVncConnectorPanel(ctx, t)))
```

**Edit 2**: Remove the standalone connector registration (lines 1937-1952).

**Edit 3**: Prefill car bridge when no saved config: in makeVncConnectorPanel's origin effect, after origin set, if localStorage had no saved config → set host/port/path/scheme to `${origin}` bridge + prefill password from settings.vncPassword (via /status payload.settings). The /status payload contains `settings` (status.settings used in makeVncTabShell). So:

```js
useEffect(() => {
  let alive = true
  api('/status').then(payload => {
    if (!alive) return
    setOrigin(String(payload.origin ?? ''))
    const originUrl = String(payload.origin ?? '')
    if (originUrl !== '' && !hasConnectorConfig()) {
      try {
        const u = new URL(originUrl)
        save({
          ...configRef.current,
          scheme: u.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss' : 'ws',
          host: u.hostname,
          port: u.port === '' ? (u.protocol === 'https:' ? '443' : '80') : u.port,
          path: 'api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc',
          password: configRef.current.password === '' ? String(payload.settings?.vncPassword ?? '') : configRef.current.password,
        })
      } catch { /* origin unparseable */ }
    }
    diag(...)
  })...
}, [])
```

Need `hasConnectorConfig()` helper:
```js
function hasConnectorConfig() {
  try { return localStorage.getItem(CONNECTOR_STORE_KEY) !== null } catch { return true }
}
```
Return true when unavailable to avoid clobbering.

- no standalone connector sidebar icon / main panel (they're merged)
- the VNC tab shell renders the connector panel (i.e., makeVncTabShell tree contains the connector's form fields).

Let me read test-client.mjs around lines 225-350 to update precisely.

Keeping makeVncView dead code is confusing but removing it touches more tests (line 231-237 use makeVncView). Since it's still exported and tested, but no longer wired... I think cleanest: remove makeVncView entirely? That's more surgery (delete ~220 lines + tests). "火速修改" — fast. Keep makeVncView code (harmless, still served vnc.html for nothing? actually vnc.html no longer used).

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. - `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

Now I have concrete evidence. Let me analyze:

**The actual failure the user hit:**

The browser tried:
```
wss://duzhong.local:6080/websockify
```

Note: **`wss://`** and port **6080**. And it failed with 1006 immediately (~700ms).

Problems:
1. The user (or the prefill) set the **VNC host** field to `duzhong.local` directly instead of the DSH bridge. So the browser tries to connect **directly from the browser** to `duzhong.local:6080` — the car. 
2. It used **`wss://`** (secure) — port 6080 websockify is almost certainly plain `ws://`, not TLS. So the TLS handshake fails → immediate error → 1006.
3. Even with `ws://`, the browser is connecting to the car directly: is the car's 5901 open? Yes over IPv4. But is websockify running on the car at 6080? Unknown — but the earlier evidence said the car has TigerVNC on 5901 and NO websockify. So `wss://duzhong.local:6080/websockify` would fail regardless.
4. Also: the browser page origin is `http://127.0.0.1:19387` (insecure). Modern browsers **block `wss://` from... ** no, they don't block wss from http (mixed content is the reverse: https page → ws:// blocked). Actually a **secure context** restriction: from an http origin, connecting to `wss://` is allowed. But `wss://` to a non-TLS port fails the TLS handshake → close 1006.
5. Another angle: `duzhong.local` resolves to IPv6 first (AAAA ×2) plus one A. Chrome tries in order; if websockify isn't listening at all, connection refused.

So the fix for the user: the connector's default should be **the plugin's own bridge** — `ws://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` — which the prefill was supposed to set. But the diag shows `wss://duzhong.local:6080/websockify`, meaning either:
- The user typed it themselves (following my "first use the car" suggestion: I told them to run websockify on the car and fill `ws://duzhong.local:6080/websockify`) — plausible! But then port 6080 requires websockify running on the car, which they didn't install (they tried `sudo apt install x11vnc` in the WRONG shell — Windows!).
- OR the prefill logic is broken and produced this.

Wait — the trace shows they changed the protocol field to wss at some point. The `ctor` url is `wss://duzhong.local:6080/websockify`. Two possibilities: user typed host=duzhong.local, port=6080, protocol=wss; or my prefill did it. My prefill sets `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` — that doesn't match at all. So the user typed it — following my earlier advice in the previous turn ("先在车上跑 websockify ... 面板填 ws://duzhong.local:6080/websockify"). But they picked wss and never got websockify installed on the car (because they ran apt on Windows!).

So the diagnosis:
- **Root cause of "连不上"**: they're connecting browser → car:6080/websockify directly, but (a) websockify isn't installed/running on the car (their apt attempt went to Windows), and (b) they selected `wss://` while 6080 would be plain WS.

- **The right move**: don't use websockify at all on the car. **Use the plugin's own bridge**: set protocol `ws`, host `127.0.0.1`, port `19387`, path `api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc`. That path goes through the plugin, which connects to the car's 5901 (verified OPEN just now). The car doesn't need websockify, x11vnc, or anything.

Also I should double check: does the car's 5901 actually speak RFB, and does the bridge work end-to-end? Earlier verified "真车 RFB 横幅 RFB 003.003 126ms". Let me re-verify now that 5901 is OPEN.

Another important thing: why did the prefill not apply? Possibly:
- The user had previously saved connector config in localStorage (I warned: "若之前 localStorage 里存过连接器配置，会显示你上次的值"), so the prefill was overridden by their stored values (host=duzhong.local, port=6080, protocol=wss). That's consistent and expected behavior. So the panel is showing THEIR saved values, not the bridge.

So the fix should be: make the default/bridge option prominent and correct — e.g. the car panel's VNC tab should offer a clear "直连小车（推荐）" vs "自定义" toggle, or the prefill should reset when the user clicks "连接" on the car tab... Actually simplest robust fix: **when the VNC tab is opened from the car panel, and the stored config points somewhere unreachable, show a hint**. Hmm.

Let me think about what the user actually wants: They want VNC to work with the car. The unified tab should default to the bridge (works with zero setup on the car). Their stored config points at the car's websockify which doesn't exist.

Best fix (minimal, high value):
1. Add a **「直连小车」/「自定义」** switch in the VNC tab. In 直连小车 mode, the form is locked/auto-filled with the plugin bridge URL (ws://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc) and it just works. 自定义 unlocks the form. Default = 直连小车 when the stored config is absent OR points to a non-bridge target... but careful about overriding user intent.
2. Also: validate `wss` on port 6080 etc.? Better: when connect fails with 1006, show a targeted hint: "如果是 ws:// 直连 websockify，请确认对端已运行 websockify；若要用小车，请切到「直连小车」".

Also there's the mixed-content issue worth checking: page origin is `http://127.0.0.1:19387`; `wss://` from http origin — allowed, no block. Fine.

Another thing to verify: is the **bridge** path still working after the refactor? Let me test the bridge end-to-end with a real WebSocket client to `ws://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` and read the RFB banner. That's the decisive test. There's `scripts/test-live-ws.mjs` for that. Let me run it.

Also I should fix the user's immediate problem AND explain the image.

Let me also reconsider: is it possible the browser **cannot** reach `duzhong.local` at all (IPv6, DNS)? The browser would try ws://duzhong.local:6080 — DNS resolves (mDNS), but nothing listens on 6080 → refused. Right.

Now I see the structure. The prefill only applies when `!hasConnectorConfig()` — i.e. first run. The user has a saved config pointing at `duzhong.local:6080` (wss). So they got the form with their values.

Wait — but actually, did they type it, or did something else write it? The stored config had scheme=wss which normalizes only if explicitly 'wss'. Default is 'ws'. So the user changed the scheme dropdown to wss. And host=duzhong.local, port=6080. So yes, the user typed those — following my previous suggestion.

Now, the fix. What's the most useful, minimal change?

Option A: Add a "直连小车" button in the panel that fills the bridge config in one click.
Option B: Add a mode switch.

Given the user wants it to just work with the car, and the tab IS the car's VNC tab, I think the best UX:
- Add a prominent **「用小车的直连通道」/「恢复默认」** action button in the toolbar that resets the form to the plugin bridge + car password. One click, works.
- Plus: on connection failure with 1006/timeout, show an actionable hint in the message area: e.g. "对方没在监听 / 协议不匹配（6080 通常是 ws:// 而非 wss://）/ 或点「小车通道」直连".

Also worth adding: **the resolution selector already exists**.

Let me also double check whether `wss://` from an `http://` origin is a problem. Actually there's a subtle issue worth surfacing: if the user enables `wss` but the server is plain `ws`, it fails. Conversely if the page were https and they used ws://, mixed content would block. Our hint should mention protocol mismatch.

Additionally, I want to add a **preflight reachability note**: we can't do TCP probes from the browser. But the panel can ask the Host to probe the target: we have a host half with HTTP API. Does the host expose a generic TCP probe? There's `probe-car.sh` script but that's for the car. A host-side "probe" endpoint would let the panel say "目标端口不可达" instead of a bare 1006. That's genuinely useful and cheap: add `/api/dzrobot-ssh/probe?host=&port=` to index.js. Hmm, that's a security consideration (SSRF) but it's a local plugin for the user's own machine; and it's the same trust domain as the bridge itself. Actually the bridge already connects to arbitrary host:port? No — the bridge connects to the configured car only.

Let me keep scope tight but effective. The user says "火速" (hurry) earlier; now they want it working. Priorities:

1. **One-click "小车通道" button** → immediate fix for their situation.

A visible, one-click "小车通道" button + a hint is the honest approach.

Hmm, but wait. Let me reconsider: is there value in ALSO fixing the *root* confusion — that they wanted websockify on the car? Two things they might be doing:
- Wanting VNC to the car desktop → bridge is the answer (no setup on car).
- Wanting the generic connector against a Linux box they're setting up (x11vnc/websockify) → then the commands must run on Ubuntu, over SSH.

The image suggests they're trying to set up VNC on some Ubuntu machine but ran it on Windows. So my answer must clarify: run those on the car (via SSH) or on the target Ubuntu box.

Now I have the full picture. Let me implement:

1. **`bridgeConfig` helper** — build bridge config from origin + stored password.
2. **「小车通道」button** in the toolbar — one click resets to the bridge target.
3. **Actionable hint on failure** — when the connection dies with 1006 and no clean close, explain likely causes (nothing listening / protocol mismatch wss vs ws / target unreachable) — and show the 小车通道 suggestion.

Let me write the changes.

For the hint, best place: compute a `failureHint` derived value in render, based on phase + config. Something like:

```js
const failureHint = (() => {
  if (phase !== 'failed' && phase !== 'disconnected') return ''
  const cfg = config
  const isBridge = cfg.path === 'api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc'
  if (isBridge) return ''   // bridge failures already have a decent message
  const bits = []
  if (cfg.scheme === 'wss') bits.push(t('connHintSchemeWss'))
  bits.push(t('connHintNothingListening'))
  return bits.join(' ')

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Build a noVNC-based VNC connector with 7 requirements: (1) input fields for VNC host, WebSocket port, path, VNC password, **plus resolution selector**; (2) use noVNC RFB to connect to `ws://host:port/websockify`; (3) support adaptive scaling, fullscreen, disconnect, reconnect; (4) if DSH is Electron/Tauri, embed WebView; (5) if DSH is a browser plugin, use iframe or new tab; (6) provide complete Ubuntu-side TigerVNC + websockify commands; (7) provide SSH tunnel secure-connection solution.
- Follow-up correction (verbatim): "VNC连接器不独立存在，而是取代掉"小车\VNC桌面"，火速修改" — the standalone connector must not exist separately; it must **replace** the car panel's "VNC 桌面" tab.
- Latest user messages: pasted a terminal screenshot showing `sudo apt install x11vnc` → "已在此计算机上禁用 Sudo。若要启用它，请转到"设置"应用中的 Developer Settings page." and asks "这是什么意思" (what does this mean); and "vnc又连不上了" (VNC can't connect again).

## Key Technical Concepts
- DSH (DeepSeek Harness) is an **Electron** app (checkout at `C:\Users\TestFox\AppData\Local\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\app.asar\dsh\`), GUI at `http://127.0.0.1:19387`.
- Plugin halves: host half (Node, main process) serves HTTP routes + WebSocket upgrade; client half (renderer) renders panels in the DSH GUI.
- DSH pages render under `dsh-app://` scheme; ES modules cannot load there, so noVNC must be served from the plugin's own `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` origin and embedded via **iframe**.
- Profile installs `file:D:/…` plugin deps as a **packaged copy** governed by `package.json#files` — NOT a junction (an earlier README claim of junction was wrong and has been corrected). Reload re-imports from the installed location, not the source tree.
- `scripts/deploy.mjs` syncs source → installed copy (`--dry-run` available); host supports `POST /reload`.
- noVNC channel validation inspects only **one prototype level** (`Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(rawChannel))`), so subclassing `WebSocket` breaks it; a `new Proxy(NativeWebSocket, { construct })` trap returning a native instance is the correct wrapper.
- `scaleViewport` = fit-to-window toggle; resolution selection uses `resizeSession` for "adaptive" and noVNC's `SetDesktopSize` extension (temporarily size the screen container to WxH, then restore).
- Electron/Tauri detection shows a runtime badge; "new window" uses `window.open` (real BrowserWindow) on Electron/Tauri, new tab in browser; `<webview>` tag deliberately avoided (needs webviewTag flag and uses ipc, not DOM postMessage, which would silently break half the control loop).
- TigerVNC new versions bind loopback only; `-localhost no` is required for remote access.

## Files and Code
- `D:\User\Desktop\dzrobot_v10.05\` — workspace root / plugin source tree (`dsh-plugin-dzrobot-ssh`).
- `vnc-connect.html` — the generic connector document served by the plugin host; contains the panel→document postMessage protocol (`dzrobot-panel` direction) and noVNC RFB bootstrap; verified 200 from the running plugin.
- `novnc/` + `vnc-app.html` + `vnc.html` — vendored noVNC assets; `package.json#files` must declare them (missing entries caused 404s).
- `client.js` — legacy `makeVncView` marked LEGACY (still used by `vnc.html` serving and tests) but **no longer mounted**; `makeVncConnectorPanel` is now mounted in the car panel's VNC tab; standalone sidebar icon + `main` panel registration removed.
- `src/vnc.js` — `VncBridge` (car TCP→WebSocket upgrade at `/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc`, address cache, RFB banner guard).
- `test-host.mjs`, `test-live-ws.mjs` — start from source tree (blind spot: they did not test the installed copy).
- `test-vnc-wrapper.mjs` — feeds real `vnc-app.html` wrapper code into real `Websock.attach()`; asserts subclasses are rejected.
- `test-package-files.mjs` — asserts runtime assets are declared in `files`, exist in the installed copy, and are byte-identical to the source tree.
- `test-vnc-connect.mjs` — executes the document's real module script in Node with an RFB stub; 16 assertions.
- `test-client.mjs` — asserts connector registers no standalone panel/icon, tab mounts connector, must not mount legacy view.
- `scripts/ubuntu-vnc-websockify.sh` — Ubuntu install path: packages → `vncpasswd` → `vncserver@:1` systemd unit with `-localhost no` → `websockify 6080 127.0.0.1:5901` unit → verify.
- `scripts/debug-ws-handshake.mjs` — browser-identical handshake headers, raw response dump.
- `diag.jsonl` — probe log with timestamps for causality.
- README — corrected the junction claim; SSH tunnel section: websockify bound to 127.0.0.1, no firewall ports opened, `ssh -N -L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080 user@server`, connector points at `ws://127.0.0.1:6080/websockify`.

## Errors and Fixes
- `Raw channel missing property: send` → caused by `class extends WebSocket` wrapper (leaves `send`/`close`/`binaryType` one prototype level too deep). Threw from the `RFB` constructor, socket became unreachable, GC'd, connection aborted → browser saw only error + 1016/1006, never `open`. Fixed with a `construct`-trap `Proxy`.
- `/vnc.html`, `/novnc/core/rfb.js` 404 → `package.json#files` omitted `novnc/` and `vnc-app.html`, so the packaged install copy lacked them. Fixed by declaring them; `test-package-files.mjs` reproduces and now guards it.
- "Your VNC is already connected" was a **wrong claim**: the 4 `accepted: 10.240.174.14` log lines were my own test connections, not the user's browser.
- Connector config from panel was ignored by the document (connection used an empty form and failed immediately) → caught by `test-vnc-connect.mjs`.
- Document message listener filtered the wrong direction (`dzrobot-vnc-connect` instead of `dzrobot-panel`) → commands never arrived.
- Auth-state bug: connect button disabled on wrong password, so the user could not retry after correcting the password.
- Scale toggle desynced from the panel after iframe reload.
- TDZ error `Cannot access 'save' before initialization` → `save` was defined after the effect that used it for prefill; moved definition before the effect.
- Car-side `dhd` driver fails to join the hotspot (`WLC_E_SET_SSID`) — hardware/driver level, needs the hardware owner; signal good, power-saving off.
- User feedback corrections to honor: never claim a connection state without evidence attributable to the user's own client; tests must exercise the **installed** artifact, not just the source tree.

## Pending Jobs
- Answer "what does this mean" for the pasted screenshot (Windows/Chinese-locale message: `sudo` is disabled on this machine by policy; enabling requires Settings → Developer Settings page — i.e. Developer Mode / sudo enablement on Windows, so `sudo apt install x11vnc` is not a valid path on this host).
- Diagnose "vnc又连不上了" (VNC cannot connect again) — needs fresh evidence from `diag.jsonl` and the panel/document state after the connector merge.
- Optional, user's call: remove the stale `locale` entry in `package.json#files` (directory does not exist; deploy script warns each run).

## Current Work
- Connector merge into the car panel's VNC tab was completed, deployed (70 files synced), hot-reloaded (`evicted:8`), and all six suites passed (host / client / wrapper / guard / connect / package).
- The user then reported a new connection failure ("vnc又连不上了") alongside an unrelated screenshot about `sudo` being disabled, showing the failure is in the current merged state.

## Next Step
- Explain the screenshot briefly (Windows blocked `sudo`; it is not Linux, so `apt`/TigerVNC/websockify must run on the **Ubuntu** machine, from an Ubuntu terminal or the provided `scripts/ubuntu-vnc-websockify.sh`), then investigate the renewed VNC failure by reading `diag.jsonl` and verifying the served connector/URL state.

## Critical Context
- One VNC surface only: car panel → 「VNC 桌面」 tab → connector form. First run prefills `ws://<DSH host>:<port>/api/dzrobot-ssh/vnc` (plugin's own bridge straight to car 5901; no websockify needed on the car) plus the saved car password; once the user edits and persists values, those win over prefill. Intended: pre-merge behavior for the car, editable to any `ws://host:port/websockify`.
- Passwords are stored in localStorage, never placed in URLs.
- Serving origin matters: `dsh-app://` cannot load ES modules, hence the iframe + plugin HTTP origin design.
- Verified: 4 browser-facing URLs return 200; served page is the fixed (Proxy) version; browser-identical WebSocket handshake correct (accept key, subprotocol, extensions properly rejected); real car RFB banner `RFB 003.003` arrived in 126 ms; six suites green. **Unverified: actual desktop rendering** — requires the user's browser interaction.
- Approval prompts are disabled; do not request sandbox escalation (`sandbox_permissions`). File policy is danger-full-access.
- Current model route: `modlens-our-free-model/z-ai/glm-5.3`.
- Treat the ambiguous "VNC 桌面" and "小车" identifiers as the car panel and its VNC tab; keep panel/document postMessage direction (`dzrobot-panel`) intact when editing.
